title: Bid Intelligence record (DRAFT)
description: DRAFT 2026-09-23. One record per project and package version: what an LLM pulls from the bid package (drawings, spec book, addenda, RFP / bid instructions, GC invitation) so G3 can avoid disqualification, price scope correctly, protect margin, and compare projects. Every field is an evidence envelope ($defs/envelope); the per-field schema constrains only value. x-tier: 1 = check on every project, 2 = extract when addressed, 3 = optional. Statutory reference facts live in a maintained reference table, never in document fields. Research report: see BID_INTELLIGENCE.md.

project_profile.title: Project profile
project_profile.description: Who and what the project is and who governs it: owner, location and land status, building and work type, delivery method and how each GC is buying our scope, published budget, design team, AHJ and permit status, code editions, and any published competitive field. Fixed categories so every project can be compared and segmented.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The owner entity named in the documents (legal name from the agreement, advertisement or cover sheet), the operator, brand or anchor tenant when different, and the owner type from a fixed list: private, a Nevada public body by kind, federal, tribal or other public. WHY: Owner type is the switch that attaches Nevada public-works reference rules (prevailing wage, subcontractor listing, bidder's preference) and routes A1's compliance checks; treating a quasi-public authority as private misses a whole compliance category and can make the bid non-responsive. The owner name exposes repeat owners whose standards, payment habits and change-order behavior we already know. WHERE: Advertisement for bids, Instructions to Bidders, bid form header, Division 00 agreement, cover sheet and title-block owner block, GC invitation email.

operator_or_tenant.description: Operator, brand or anchor tenant when different from the owner

value.description: Owner of the project as the documents name it

owner.x-extraction-notes: Take the owner from the owner's documents, not the GC (BDR already stores GCs). Classify owner_type from the named entity; never copy the team's go/no-go owner_type answer. A county-run airport or a county-created authority is public even when it behaves commercially. Use nv_state_agency for state departments and nv_higher_education for NSHE institutions; both usually put the work on State-owned property, which project_location.land_status records. Whether NRS 338 or Davis-Bacon actually applies is decided from the documents in A1 labor_and_compliance (federal money can attach wage rules to a private owner); this field records only who the owner is. The verbatim owner text is the envelope citation, so there is no basis property.
owner.x-reference-facts: The State Public Works Division is the building official for construction on State-owned property (NRS 341.100, 341.105); the 2026-09-23 fact-check names UNLV, CSN and state-agency jobs as following that permit path.
owner.x-bdr-overlap: Go/no-go rubric answer owner_type is a coarser, team-typed version; BDR does not store the owner name.

project_location.title: Project location and land status
project_location.description: The site as the documents give it: street address or intersection, city or community, county, APN when shown, a short site description (campus, property or base name, or the other sites on a multi-site job) and the land status (State-owned, federal, tribal or other). Code adds the NRS 338.025 prevailing wage region from the county, the distance from Las Vegas City Hall from the geocoded address, and whether the location matches the address BDR holds. WHY: Location prices outlying work: Clark wage-book zone pay starts 25 miles from Las Vegas City Hall and prices Mesquite, Laughlin, Primm and Indian Springs work, and Pahrump is in Nye County and the Southern Rural region, which has a different book. State-owned property makes SPWD the building official and, on SPWD contracts, triggers the NRS 339.025(2) sub bond; federal enclaves such as Nellis and Creech have no local AHJ. BDR's project address is free-text intake and carries none of this, and location is also the join key for travel, badging and comparable-project search. WHERE: Cover sheet project data and vicinity map, title block, civil site plan (APN, legal description), advertisement or ITB, GC invitation email.

address_text.description: Street address or intersection as written

city_or_community.description: City or community as written (Laughlin, Primm, Pahrump)

site_description.description: Campus, property or base name; other sites on a multi-site job

pw_region.description: NRS 338.025 wage region; set by code from county, model returns null

distance_mi_from_lv_city_hall.description: Set by code from the geocoded address; model returns null

matches_bdr_address.description: Set by code: agrees with the BDR project address; model returns null

project_location.x-extraction-notes: The model fills only the document properties and returns null for pw_region, distance_mi_from_lv_city_hall and matches_bdr_address, which code sets (region from county by the NRS 338.025 table, distance from the geocoded address). A 'Las Vegas' mailing address does not mean the City of Las Vegas: record county and community as written and leave jurisdiction to ahj. Set land_status from document text, or from an owner that is a state agency, an NSHE institution, a military installation or a federal agency, and name that rule in the envelope note. The Clark wage-book zone band and its premium are reference facts attached by rule from pw_region and the distance; they are never stored in this value. For a multi-site job record the primary site and list the others in site_description.
project_location.x-reference-facts: NRS 338.025 sets four prevailing wage regions: Clark (Clark County); Southern Rural (Esmeralda, Lincoln and Nye counties, including Pahrump); Washoe (Washoe County); Northern Rural (Carson City plus Churchill, Douglas, Elko, Eureka, Humboldt, Lander, Lyon, Mineral, Storey, Pershing and White Pine counties). Clark 2025-26 book (Amendment 07, effective 6/24/26), Wireman and Communication Technician zone pay measured from Las Vegas City Hall: 25-55 mi +$3.50, 56-85 mi +$4.50, over 85 mi +$8.50. The Clark book year runs October 1 to September 30; bids opening on or after October 1, 2026 fall under the 2026-27 book, and rates at bid opening lock for up to 36 months (NRS 338.030(9)). SPWD is the building official on State-owned property (NRS 341.100, 341.105). On SPWD contracts each sub whose work exceeds $50,000 or 1% of the project, whichever is greater, furnishes a bond to the Division (NRS 339.025(2)). Laughlin and Primm are unincorporated Clark County.
project_location.x-bdr-overlap: BDR projects.address is free-text intake; code compares it with this field (matches_bdr_address).

building_type.title: Building type, occupancy and construction type
building_type.description: The primary building use from a fixed list, any secondary uses on a mixed-use project, the IBC occupancy groups and construction types from the code analysis, and whether the code sheet declares the building a high-rise and fully or partly sprinklered. WHY: $/SF, fixtures per SF and labor per SF only compare within a building type (a warehouse shell and a hospital differ several-fold per SF), and occupancy drives emergency lighting, fire alarm type and healthcare essential electrical systems. Construction type changes wiring methods: the Southern Nevada amendment to NEC 800.24(C) requires low-voltage cable in concealed spaces of Type I and II buildings to be plenum-rated or in metal raceway. High-rise status drives voice evacuation, the fire command center and emergency power on Las Vegas towers and is a comparison key; sprinkler status changes fire alarm detection scope. WHERE: Architectural code analysis or life-safety sheet, cover sheet project description, Division 01 summary of work, GC invitation.

secondary_types.description: Other uses on a mixed-use project

ibc_occupancy_groups.description: IBC occupancy groups as listed on the code analysis

construction_types.description: IBC construction types as listed; a podium lists both

high_rise.description: High-rise as stated on the code or life-safety sheet

value.description: Building use, occupancy and code classification

building_type.x-extraction-notes: Pick one dominant use for primary_type and list the rest in secondary_types. Copy occupancy groups and construction types exactly as the code analysis lists them; a podium building lists both types (for example I-A and V-A). Without a code sheet return null for occupancy, construction type, high_rise and sprinklered rather than inferring them from use. Record high_rise only as the code or life-safety sheet states it; never compute it from building height. The cost consequences of construction type are evaluated in A4 southern_nevada_amendment_triggers and A5; this field only records the classification.
building_type.x-reference-facts: Southern Nevada 2023 NEC amendment 800.24(C): low-voltage cable in concealed spaces of Type I and II buildings must be plenum-rated or in metal raceway (Clark County 2023 NEC amendments). IBC 202 defines a high-rise building as one with an occupied floor more than 75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access (standard definition, not part of the 2026-09-23 fact-check).
building_type.x-bdr-overlap: Go/no-go rubric answer project_type (team-typed); map it to primary_type when backfilling older projects.

work_type.title: Work type (new vs renovation)
work_type.description: Whether the electrical work is ground-up new construction, an addition, a renovation or remodel, a tenant improvement, core and shell only, a service upgrade or retrofit, site and infrastructure only, or a substantial mix. WHY: Renovation and TI work carry demolition, existing-conditions discovery, occupied-building and outage costs that new construction does not; mixing them in history hides why a remodel came in at double the $/SF of a shell. WHERE: Cover sheet project description, electrical demolition sheets, Division 01 summary of work, GC invitation.
work_type.x-extraction-notes: Electrical demolition sheets or 'existing to remain' notes rule out new_construction. Use mixed only when a meaningful share is both (an addition plus a remodel of the existing building). Occupancy during the work is A3 occupancy_during_construction, not this field.

delivery_method.title: Delivery method and G3's contract position
delivery_method.description: How the owner is buying the prime contract (design-bid-build hard bid, CM at risk, design-build, multi-prime or CM agency, negotiated, job order contract or IPD) and where G3's price goes: to a GC, directly to the owner, to a design-builder, or to another trade. WHY: Delivery method predicts realistic hit rate and how much room exists to refine scope after the first number: a CMAR GMP number may be re-bid, a hard bid is awarded low. When G3 bids directly to the owner (multi-prime or a small public electrical-only job), G3 carries the prime's obligations: bid security to the owner, listing its own subs under NRS 338.141, bidder's preference paperwork and prime bonds. WHERE: Advertisement for bids, Instructions to Bidders, bid form addressee, Division 00 procurement description, GC invitation email.

owner_delivery_method.description: How the owner buys the prime contract

value.description: Owner delivery method and G3's contract position

delivery_method.x-extraction-notes: owner_delivery_method is the owner-to-prime method; how each GC is buying our scope is electrical_procurement_basis. Nevada award rules (low bid, best value) live in A1 bid_submission.award_basis; keep the two consistent. If only the GC invitation states it ('CMAR GMP pricing'), use it and cite the email. Set g3_contract_position to prime_to_owner only when the bid form or advertisement is addressed to electrical bidders; a Division 01 'Contractor' is normally the GC.
delivery_method.x-reference-facts: NRS 338.141 subcontractor listing applies to competitively bid public works estimated over $100,000 advertised under NRS 338.1385(1)(a) or 338.143(1)(a), and to NDOT work under NRS 408.327; design-build final proposals are exempt (NRS 338.1727). CMAR and design-build are separate NRS 338 procedures. The NRS 338.1389 bidder's preference belongs to whoever bids to the public body, so it matters to G3 only when G3 bids direct or through the prime's flow-down clauses. SPWD qualifies primes under NRS 338.1375; local governments prequalify primes under NRS 338.1377 and 338.1379.
delivery_method.x-bdr-overlap: Go/no-go rubric answer bid_method may be one of these two concepts; the team decides which (see open questions) and the rubric is then pre-filled from this field.

electrical_procurement_basis.title: How each GC is buying our scope
electrical_procurement_basis.description: For each inviting GC, whether we are pricing a complete plan-and-spec lump sum, a design-assist number, a design-build electrical scope where we carry the design, a budget or ROM number, a GMP-development number, or a negotiated open-book price. WHY: Design-build electrical means we carry engineering, stamped drawings and design liability that must be priced; a budget number is non-binding but sets an expectation the GC will hold us to later. GCs on the same project can be at different stages (one negotiating a GMP, others hard bidding), and pricing on the wrong basis either leaves design cost out or over-commits on a conceptual set. WHERE: GC invitation email or portal message, bid form, Division 00 and 01 summary of work, delegated-design language in Division 26.

applies_to_gc.description: GC name as in the invitation; null when it applies to every GC

basis.description: How this GC is buying our scope

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per inviting GC, or one row for all when owner documents set it

electrical_procurement_basis.x-extraction-notes: One row per inviting GC when invitations differ, or a single row with applies_to_gc null when owner documents set the basis for everyone. Budget requests usually appear only in the invitation ('budget pricing', 'ROM', 'GMP set', 'pricing set'). Delegated design of one system (for example fire alarm) does not make the whole scope design_build_electrical; A6 delegated_design_items records it. Code derives the project-level flag for analytics (any binding row versus all budget).
electrical_procurement_basis.x-bdr-overlap: BDR project numbers carry a B suffix for budgetary projects; this field should agree with it and can propose it for new projects (existing project numbers are never rewritten).

published_budget_or_estimate.title: Published budget or engineer's estimate
published_budget_or_estimate.description: Every construction budget, engineer's estimate, cost range or GMP target printed in the advertisement, ITB, bid form or invitation, with what it covers (total project, construction only, electrical only or one bid package) and which package, phase or alternate it belongs to. WHY: Public advertisements often publish an engineer's estimate or range; it sanity-checks our number and the go/no-go value band, drives A1's license monetary limit check, and a budget well below realistic electrical cost signals a likely rebid, value engineering round or cancellation. WHERE: Advertisement for bids, Instructions to Bidders, public agency bid portal notice, bid form, GC invitation.

range_low.description: Low end when a range is stated

range_high.description: High end when a range is stated

applies_to.description: Bid package, phase, base bid or alternate the figure belongs to

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

published_budget_or_estimate.x-extraction-notes: Record only numbers printed in the documents or invitation; never estimate one. One row per published figure (base bid, each bid package, alternates priced separately). This is the single extraction point for the published estimate: A1 bid_submission.license_monetary_limit_check reads it through computed_from instead of extracting its own.
published_budget_or_estimate.x-bdr-overlap: Go/no-go rubric answer est_value_band (team estimate); this field can pre-fill it.

design_team.title: Design team
design_team.description: Each design firm on the cover sheet, title blocks and seals pages, one row per role: architect of record, separate interiors or TI architect, electrical engineer of record, lighting designer, technology or low-voltage consultant, fire alarm or life-safety designer and civil engineer, with office city and the stamping professional when legible. WHY: Some architects issue coordinated sets and some produce chronic plan/spec conflicts and heavy addenda; EOR habits (copper-only, sole-sourced gear, EMT-only, heavy testing) directly set feeder, gear and lighting cost. A per-firm history tells the team how much design-risk contingency to carry, and a separate lighting designer usually means a spec-grade, rep-controlled fixture package. WHERE: Cover sheet consultant list, title blocks by discipline, Division 00 and 26/27/28 seals pages, project directory.

firm_normalized.description: Set by code for cross-project matching; model returns null

office_city.description: Office city from the title block

stamping_professional.description: Stamping architect or engineer when legible on the seal

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per design firm and role

design_team.x-extraction-notes: Read this project's title blocks and seals; large firms change the stamping engineer per project. Code fills firm_normalized (drops Inc., LLC and punctuation) so the same firm matches across projects. On design-build electrical there may be no electrical_engineer_of_record row; say so in the envelope note. Products and basis of design tied to a lighting designer live in A4 specified_products.

ahj.title: Permitting jurisdiction (AHJ) and permit status
ahj.description: The building department that issues the electrical permit and inspects (unincorporated Clark County, City of Las Vegas, Henderson, North Las Vegas, Boulder City, Mesquite, Nye County, the State Public Works Division, federal, tribal or other), the fire authority named for fire alarm and life-safety acceptance, how the jurisdiction was determined, and the permit status of the bid set (not submitted, in plan review or permitted) with permit number, application date and whether plan-check comments are incorporated. WHY: Each jurisdiction adopts codes and the Southern Nevada NEC amendments on its own schedule and has its own plan-review times, fees and inspection practice; the wrong AHJ gives optimistic permit lead time and wrong fee allowances. Bidding drawings still in plan check means comments can still change scope, and the application date decides which code edition applies. WHERE: Cover sheet code or jurisdiction block and permit stamp, project address and APN, Division 01 permits article, GC invitation.

building_department.description: Building department that permits and inspects electrical work

fire_authority.description: Fire authority named for fire alarm and life-safety acceptance

permit_number.description: Permit or plan-check number when shown

plan_check_comments_incorporated.description: Whether the set says plan-check comments are incorporated

value.description: Permitting jurisdiction, fire authority and permit status

ahj.x-extraction-notes: A 'Las Vegas' mailing address is often unincorporated Clark County (much of the Strip); Laughlin and Primm are unincorporated Clark County; Pahrump is Nye County. Prefer the jurisdiction named on the cover sheet or permit block; when only an address is available set ahj_basis to inferred_from_address so the team confirms it. On State-owned property the building department is state_public_works_division; on federal enclaves (Nellis, Creech) use federal, since there is no local AHJ. Record permit_status only from the set or the invitation ('drawings are in plan check', a permit stamp). Do not assert from memory which code edition a jurisdiction enforces; code_editions reads the adoption table.
ahj.x-reference-facts: SPWD's building official permits, plan-reviews and inspects all construction and electrical work on State-owned property (NRS 341.100, 341.105). The Southern Nevada NEC amendments were developed by the SNBO NEC Committee (voting members Clark County, Henderson, Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Boulder City, Pahrump, Mesquite, CCSD and three industry representatives) and are not code until each jurisdiction adopts them. Clark County: adopted July 15, 2025, effective January 11, 2026. City of Las Vegas: approved July 16, 2025, effective January 5, 2026. Pahrump is in Nye County, the Southern Rural wage region.
ahj.x-bdr-overlap: BDR stores the project address; the AHJ and permit status are not stored.

code_editions.title: Code editions cited and enforced
code_editions.description: Every code and standard edition the documents cite (NEC, the Southern Nevada NEC amendments, IBC, IFC, IECC or ASHRAE 90.1, NFPA 72, 101, 99, 110 and 70E), one row per place it is cited (drawings, specifications, invitation), plus code-set values for the NEC edition the AHJ enforces for this permit date and whether a cited edition is out of date. WHY: Clark County and the City of Las Vegas now enforce the 2023 NEC and 2024 I-codes for applications from January 2026, but spec books written in 2024 and 2025 often still cite the 2020 NEC or 2021 IECC, so we price one rule set and get inspected to another. The energy code edition sets lighting-control and acceptance-testing scope. WHERE: Cover sheet or code analysis sheet, E-001 general notes, Division 26 05 00 references article, Division 01 regulatory requirements.

code_label.description: Name as written when code is other

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

codes.description: One row per code per place it is cited

expected_nec_edition_for_ahj.description: Set by code from the adoption table, AHJ and application date; model returns null

cited_nec_outdated.description: Set by code: a cited NEC edition is older than the expected edition; model returns null

value.description: Code editions cited and the edition the AHJ enforces

code_editions.x-extraction-notes: One row per code per place cited: the drawing code block and the Division 26 references article each get their own rows, so a drawings-versus-specs mismatch shows as two rows and code also files it in document_conflicts as code_edition. Record the edition exactly as cited; never fill one from memory. expected_nec_edition_for_ahj and cited_nec_outdated are set by code from the maintained adoption table using ahj.building_department and ahj.permit_application_date (the bid date when no application date is stated); the model returns null for both. The amendments that change cost are evaluated in A4 southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.
code_editions.x-reference-facts: Clark County adopted the 2023 NEC with the Southern Nevada amendments on July 15, 2025, effective January 11, 2026, and enforces the 2024 IBC, IRC, IEBC, UMC, UPC and IECC with the 2023 NEC for new building permit applications from that date. City of Las Vegas: approved July 16, 2025, effective January 5, 2026, the same set plus the 2024 IFC and WUI code; projects submitted before then could use the prior codes. The amendments were developed by the SNBO NEC Committee, were not jointly adopted, and take effect only as each jurisdiction adopts them.

competitive_field.title: Published plan holders and competing bidders
competitive_field.description: Any published plan holder or prospective bidder list in the package or harvest: the prime bidders and electrical contractors it names, firms whose trade it does not state, the list date and the kind of list. WHY: Win rate and spread only make sense against how many electrical contractors chased the job. Primes on the list that did not invite G3 are outreach targets, and the list feeds the go/no-go competitor question that the team now answers from memory. WHERE: Owner or agency plan holder lists on public portals, prebid sign-in sheets issued by addendum, GC invitation cc lists when disclosed.

prime_bidders.description: Firms the list identifies as prime or general contractors

electrical_contractors.description: Firms the list identifies as electrical contractors

other_firms.description: Firms whose trade the list does not state

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

competitive_field.x-extraction-notes: Record names exactly as listed; classify a firm as prime or electrical only when the list states its trade, otherwise put it in other_firms. Code normalizes names and joins them with the GCs that invited G3, which BDR already holds. Plan holder lists usually sit on the owner's portal rather than in the package; extract one only when the harvest includes it. A prebid sign-in sheet shows attendance, not intent to bid.
competitive_field.x-bdr-overlap: Go/no-go rubric answer competitor_known; BDR holds the GCs that invited G3.

bid_brief.title: Bid brief
bid_brief.description: The derived bid-day page: snapshot, ranked risks, disqualification checklist, RFIs to send, the single proposal-facing exclusions list, GC leveling self-check, labor condition profile, go/no-go pre-fill, bid window and comparables. Every line names its source field keys and adds no fact that is not in the record.

brief_summary.title: Bid snapshot
brief_summary.description: Three or four plain sentences: what the project is (type, size, work type, owner, location), what our scope covers at a glance, the biggest money or disqualification risk, and anything unusual about this bid, with the field keys it draws on. WHY: Lets the executive and estimators decide in seconds whether and how to pursue, without opening the full record. WHERE: Derived from project_profile, quantities_rollup, top_risks and A6 scope_of_work_narrative.

summary.description: Three or four sentences built only from record fields

source_field_keys.description: Field keys the summary draws on

brief_summary.x-extraction-notes: Summarize only facts present in the record and list their field keys; no sales language and no new facts. Do not restate A6's scope narrative in detail. Rebuild after each addendum.

top_risks.title: Top risks
top_risks.description: The five to ten findings with the highest cost or consequence, ranked, each with a one-line description, category, relative cost band, recommended action and the field keys and citations it comes from. WHY: Money is lost on bid day through small, cumulative misses; a ranked list forces the few items that can swing margin (copper-only, liquidated damages, commissioning scope, late addenda, sole-source or long-lead gear) to be seen and priced before the number goes out. WHERE: Derived from every section of the record, including A4 specified_products.sourcing_restriction_by_rfq_category and power_distribution.long_lead_equipment for vendor pricing risk.

source_field_keys.description: Field keys the risk comes from

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

top_risks.x-extraction-notes: Rank by likely dollars or disqualification, not document order. Every risk names field keys and carries citations; no uncited risks. cost_impact is a relative band, never a dollar figure. A not_stated critical item is a risk to price, qualify or RFI; a not_found item is reviewer work shown in extraction_coverage_and_quality, not here. Sole-source, rep-controlled and long-lead package risks come from A4 (the former vendor_pricing_risks field is removed). Rebuild after each addendum.

disqualification_checklist.title: Disqualification checklist
disqualification_checklist.description: Every pass/fail requirement for our bid to each GC and, on public work, for the GC's bid to the owner that depends on us: the GC's own cutoff, owner deadline, mandatory prebid or site walk, addenda acknowledgment, bid security, bid form, required attachments, license classification and monetary limit, State Fire Marshal licensing for fire alarm scope, prequalification, qualification minimums, subcontractor listing information, bidder's preference documents and clean-bid rules; each with deadline and completion state. WHY: A missed attachment, acknowledgment or mandatory meeting voids a bid regardless of price and is a more common cause of rejection than a pricing error; one checklist in one place is the cheapest protection. WHERE: Derived from A1 bid_submission and labor_and_compliance fields, A2 items due with the bid, A5 fire alarm licensing, and BDR actions for completion state.

requirement.description: What must be done, in one line

applies_to_gc.description: GC it applies to; null for owner-level requirements

completion_state.description: Set by the app from BDR actions

source_field_keys.description: Field keys the requirement comes from

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

disqualification_checklist.x-extraction-notes: Code builds rows from the source fields; the model writes only the requirement line. The app sets completion_state from BDR actions (addenda acknowledged, proposal sent, prebid attended). Deadlines are stored with the offset as written and shown in Pacific time; a time with no stated zone is flagged, not assumed. One row per GC for GC-specific requirements. Statutory items are attached from the reference table by rule and labeled as reference. A1's bid_disqualification_risk_flags candidate is folded into this field.
disqualification_checklist.x-reference-facts: A Nevada fire alarm scope needs a State Fire Marshal firm license and an SFM certificate of registration for every installer, a certificate holder on every job site, and a designer who is NICET Level II or a PE (NAC 477.300); NSCB C-41c (Fire Alarms) is an alternative classification to C-2 or C-2c. Under NRS 338.141 path (b), the three lowest primes submit their first-tier sub list with NRS 624 license numbers within 2 hours after bid opening and a late list makes the bid nonresponsive, so the GC needs G3's legal name and license number immediately after opening.
disqualification_checklist.x-bdr-overlap: BDR internal and actual bid due dates and bid_notes (GC bid instructions free text).

rfis_to_send.title: RFIs to send before bid
rfis_to_send.description: Questions G3 should ask before the RFI cutoff, drafted and ranked, each with the reason, the sheet or section, whether the answer changes price, the field keys that raised it and where it stands. WHY: GCs and courts hold bidders to what they should have asked; an RFI sent before cutoff turns a costly ambiguity into a binding answer for every bidder instead of a risk only we price. WHERE: Derived from document_conflicts, design_completeness, referenced_documents_not_provided, scope_bearing_notes and A6 rows marked ambiguous or conflicting.

ref_sheet_or_section.description: Sheet or spec section the question concerns

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

rfis_to_send.x-extraction-notes: Show A1's RFI cutoff (bid_submission.rfi_cutoff_and_contact_rules) next to the list. Skip questions already answered in prebid_rfi_log. Draft wording only; the estimator sends and the app tracks lifecycle_state. When A1 bid_submission.exclusions_qualifications_allowed requires a clean bid, exclusions that cannot be carried become questions here before the cutoff.

exclusions_and_qualifications_to_carry.title: Exclusions and qualifications to carry
exclusions_and_qualifications_to_carry.description: The single proposal-facing list of draft exclusions, qualifications, assumptions and clarifications, each tied to its reason (a not-stated or others-assigned responsibility, an open conflict or RFI, a missing reference, a design gap, a contract term, or a GC package that differs), the GCs it applies to, and the estimator's decision. WHY: GC leveling reads exclusions before price: a clean, specific list that matches the documents protects margin without looking like missing scope, while vague or missing exclusions leave us holding scope the GC plugs in at our cost. WHERE: Derived from A6 scope_responsibility.default_exclusions_and_clarifications candidates, A2 contract_terms.contract_term_actions rows marked qualify_on_proposal, document_conflicts, prebid_rfi_log open items, referenced_documents_not_provided and design_completeness.

applies_to_gcs.description: GCs this line applies to; empty means all

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

exclusions_and_qualifications_to_carry.x-extraction-notes: This is the only field that writes proposal wording: A6 supplies candidates without text and A2 supplies the accept, price, qualify or executive-review decision without text, and both are cited through source_field_keys. Never exclude something the documents clearly assign to electrical; A6 price_do_not_exclude rows become pricing items in top_risks. When A1 bid_submission.exclusions_qualifications_allowed requires a clean bid, lines convert to RFIs. Only lines with estimator_decision carry reach BDR proposal generation.

leveling_self_check.title: GC leveling self-check
leveling_self_check.description: The scope lines GCs most often level electrical bids on (commissioning support, startup and testing, independent testing, temporary power, low-voltage boundary, fire alarm, OFCI connections, mechanical equipment wiring and VFDs, firestopping, trenching, saw-cut and patch, pads and pole bases, core drilling, permits and fees, utility fees, painting, seismic bracing, studies, bonds), with what each GC's scope sheet says, our current position, and a note where our number may look thin or heavy. WHY: A low number with silent gaps gets plugged by the GC at our cost or set aside; stating our position on each common leveling line against each GC's own scope sheet makes the number compare cleanly and keeps us from over-qualifying ourselves out. WHERE: Derived from A6 responsibility_matrix and gc_trade_package_by_gc, A3 commissioning and testing fields, and exclusions_and_qualifications_to_carry.

applies_to_gc.description: GC whose scope sheet this row compares; null for all

gc_scope_sheet_position.description: What the GC scope sheet says

note.description: Where our number may look thin or heavy

value.description: One row per fixed leveling line, per GC when scope sheets differ

leveling_self_check.x-extraction-notes: Internal analysis, not a document fact; label it so. Keep the scope_line list fixed so it compares across projects. One row per line, or per line and GC when GC scope sheets differ.

labor_condition_profile.title: Labor condition profile
labor_condition_profile.description: A fixed list of the conditions that change labor productivity or pay on this job, each marked applies, does not apply or not stated, with its extent: occupied or operating facility, swing or graveyard shift, weekend or holiday work, escort, badging and screening, ICRA containment, hard-lid or high ceilings, high-rise vertical logistics, remote zone travel, multi-phase remobilization, restricted outage windows and limited laydown or hoisting. The estimator enters any factor; the field generates none. WHY: Labor is where electrical jobs lose money, and estimators apply factors for these conditions by habit. A consistent profile shows why two jobs of similar size priced differently and lets estimate_vs_actual labor variance be compared by condition across projects. WHERE: Computed from A3 schedule_and_site (occupancy_during_construction, working_hours, off_hours_work_items, outage_shutdown_windows, escort_requirements, badging_and_screening, healthcare_icra, phasing, site_logistics), A4 wiring_and_lighting.ceiling_types_by_area, project_profile.building_type (high_rise) and project_profile.project_location (distance).

extent_note.description: Areas or share as stated in the source fields

estimator_factor_percent.description: Labor factor entered by the estimator; never generated

value.description: One row per fixed labor condition

labor_condition_profile.x-extraction-notes: Code sets applies from the source fields by fixed rules, and extent_note may restate only what those fields say. estimator_factor_percent is entered by the estimator, never generated, and survives re-runs. Wage premiums for shifts, weekends and zones are reference facts attached by rule when state prevailing wage applies (A1 labor_and_compliance.prevailing_wage_basis); they are never written into this value. There is no 'energized work prohibited' condition: NFPA 70E already requires an electrically safe work condition unless energized work is justified, and the cost driver is restricted_outage_windows.
labor_condition_profile.x-reference-facts: Clark 2025-26 prevailing wage book (Amendment 07), Wireman and Communication Technician: swing shift (4:30 pm to 1:00 am) +15% and graveyard shift (12:30 am to 9:00 am) +30%, both requiring 8 consecutive hours on 5 consecutive days; weekend and holiday hours at double time; zone pay from Las Vegas City Hall 25-55 mi +$3.50, 56-85 mi +$4.50, over 85 mi +$8.50; wiremen welding +5%; work within 5 ft of a 60 ft or greater fall +0.5x. Bids opening on or after October 1, 2026 use the 2026-27 book.
labor_condition_profile.x-bdr-overlap: BDR's labor_time = night_work flag is a coarse version of the shift conditions.

go_no_go_signals.title: Go / no-go signals
go_no_go_signals.description: Evidence from the record for each BDR go/no-go rubric question (project type, owner type, labor needed, bid method, competitor known, GC known, subs needed, value band, scope fit), with a suggested answer and the direction each signal points. WHY: Pre-filling the rubric from the documents speeds the decision and keeps answers consistent across estimators, so hit-rate history compares like with like. WHERE: Derived from project_profile (including competitive_field), quantities_rollup, labor_condition_profile, A1 labor_and_compliance and A6 scope fields.

evidence.description: One line of evidence from the record

go_no_go_signals.x-extraction-notes: Suggest only; the team confirms the rubric. gc_known comes from the team, not the documents; competitor_known may be suggested from competitive_field when a list exists. The go/no-go call usually happens before most fields are extracted, so signals refresh as fields fill.
go_no_go_signals.x-bdr-overlap: BDR go/no-go rubric answers (project_type, owner_type, labor_needed, bid_method, competitor_known, gc_known, subs_needed, est_value_band, scope_fit).

bid_window_days.title: Bid window
bid_window_days.description: Calendar days from invitation to the earliest GC cutoff and to the owner's bid due, working days to G3's internal bid due, and calendar days between the last addendum and the earliest GC cutoff. WHY: Short windows and late addenda correlate with rushed takeoffs and missed items; seeing it up front lets the team decline, add help or carry more contingency. The GC cutoff, not the owner's time, is our real deadline. WHERE: Computed from BDR invitation date and internal and actual bid due, A1 bid_submission.gc_sub_bid_cutoffs and addenda_log dates.

invite_to_gc_cutoff_days.description: Calendar days from invitation to the earliest GC cutoff

invite_to_owner_due_days.description: Calendar days from invitation to the owner bid due

working_days_to_internal_due.description: Working days from invitation to the internal bid due

last_addendum_to_gc_cutoff_days.description: Calendar days from the last addendum to the earliest GC cutoff

value.description: Bid window lengths computed by code

bid_window_days.x-extraction-notes: Computed by code in Pacific time; fractional days allowed. Recompute when an addendum moves the bid date or a GC changes its cutoff. last_addendum_to_gc_cutoff_days is negative when an addendum lands after a GC's cutoff.
bid_window_days.x-bdr-overlap: BDR invitation date, internal bid due and actual bid due.

comparable_projects.title: Comparable past projects and segment record
comparable_projects.description: Past BDR projects most like this one (same building and work type, similar size, service and unit type, same EOR, architect, owner, GC or location) with outcome, our $/SF and spread against the winner, plus our binding bids and wins in this segment. WHY: A single blended hit rate is useless for decisions; our own record in the same segment, and what similar jobs cost per SF, is the most direct check on both the go/no-go call and the final number. WHERE: Computed by the app from history across BDR records; not extracted from documents.

spread_pct.description: Signed percent between our amount and the winner

segment_label.description: Segment used, e.g. GC x building type x delivery method

segment_bids.description: Our binding bids in the segment

value.description: Comparable past projects and segment record, computed by the app

comparable_projects.x-extraction-notes: Works only if project_profile keys (owner type, delivery method, building type, work type, design team, location) are filled consistently on every record; backfill older projects. Exclude budget-basis projects (every electrical_procurement_basis row budget_or_rom) from bid and win counts. The segment definition and minimum sample are the team's call (see open questions).
comparable_projects.x-bdr-overlap: BDR bid outcome won/lost, list of GCs bidding, per-GC proposal amounts; RFP matching finds duplicates, not comparables.

bid_submission.title: Bid submission rules
bid_submission.description: Everything G3 must do to get a responsive, on-time number to each GC, and to the owner when G3 bids direct: per-GC cutoffs and routes, the owner's bid time, opening and withdrawal rules, forms and license data, exclusions policy, alternates, unit prices, allowances, the substitution window, bid security, hold periods, addenda acknowledgment, question deadlines, meetings and walks, attachments, prequalification, stated licenses and the license limit check, award basis, participation goals and document-sharing limits. Fields where GCs layer their own rules on the owner's carry one row per party (owner_documents or a named GC) so the page can show each GC's strictest rule.

gc_sub_bid_cutoffs.title: GC cutoff for sub bids
gc_sub_bid_cutoffs.description: For each GC inviting G3, when that GC must receive sub numbers: a fixed date and time, a date only, or a lead time before the owner's bid time, with the time zone as written and whether a later GC message moved it. WHY: This, not the owner's printed due time, is G3's real deadline. A number that reaches the GC after its cutoff never makes it into the GC's bid, so we lose without ever being compared on price. Each GC on the same project can set a different cutoff. WHERE: GC invitation email, portal bid invite message (BuildingConnected, Procore, PipelineSuite and others), GC bid-day cover letter or scope sheet header, later GC reminder emails.

gc_name.description: GC name matched to the GCs on the BDR project

cutoff_datetime.description: Absolute cutoff when both a date and a time are written

cutoff_date_only.description: Cutoff date when the GC gives a date with no time

offset_before_owner_due.description: Lead time when the cutoff is written relative to the owner's bid time, for example 2 hours before bid

time_zone_as_stated.description: Time zone written with the cutoff

revised_by_later_message.description: True when a later GC message changed the cutoff; the row holds the latest value

cite.description: Envelope citation ids that support this row

items.description: A GC's cutoff for sub numbers

value.description: One row per GC that states a cutoff

gc_sub_bid_cutoffs.x-extraction-notes: Read the invitation and follow-up GC messages, not the spec book. A vague cutoff ('prior to bid', 'morning of bid day') stays in the citation quote with the time properties null. One row per GC, matched to the GCs already on the BDR project; when a GC revises its cutoff keep one row with the latest value and set revised_by_later_message. Code computes each GC's lead time against the actual bid due and the absolute time for relative cutoffs. Never fill a cutoff from a GC's habit on past bids. Record not_stated when no invitation states a cutoff.
gc_sub_bid_cutoffs.x-bdr-overlap: BDR stores internal bid due and actual bid due per project, not per GC. This field can seed internal bid due and adds a per-GC cutoff and time zone.

submission_channels.title: How and where to submit
submission_channels.description: Each route the bid must travel: to each GC (portal, email address, hand delivery) and, when the documents require it, directly to the owner (sealed hard copy, original bid bond by courier), with portal registration that must happen first and format rules such as a single PDF, file naming or subject line. WHY: A bid sent through the wrong channel is treated like a late bid. Hybrid jobs (portal upload plus a hard-copy original bond or form) are the easiest to miss because the team watches only the portal, and new portal accounts can take a day or more to approve. WHERE: GC invitation email or portal message; Advertisement for Bids (00 11 16); Instructions to Bidders (00 21 13); bid form cover page.

gc_name.description: GC name when recipient_type is gc; null for owner routes

portal_or_address.description: Portal name exactly as written, email address, or delivery address

registration_required.description: True when a portal account or plan-holder registration must exist before submitting

hard_copy_items.description: Items that must arrive physically, such as an original bid bond or signed form

format_rules.description: File format, naming, page, or subject line rules as stated

cite.description: Envelope citation ids that support this row

items.description: A route the bid or part of it must travel

submission_channels.x-extraction-notes: GCs often layer their own delivery rules on top of the owner's Division 00 method; record each route as its own row. Record portal names exactly as written. An owner route matters to G3 when G3 bids direct or when the documents make a sub item (an original bid bond, a listing form) reach the owner. Record not_stated when no document says how to submit.
submission_channels.x-bdr-overlap: BDR stores bidding_url and harvests invitations by method (Procore, PipelineSuite, NGEM, gc_portal); the submission route can differ from where documents were downloaded.

gc_instruction_deltas.title: Other GC bid instructions
gc_instruction_deltas.description: Instructions in a GC's invitation or sub bid instructions that no topic field captures: email subject line and file naming, a required cover letter or signer, requests to state gear lead times, crew size or schedule duration with the quote, bid-day contact availability, post-bid scope review calls, and other GC-specific rules. WHY: For a sub the GC's instructions control, and a number that ignores a GC's own rule can be set aside during leveling. The topic fields (forms, exclusions, bonds, attachments, cutoffs, routes, breakdowns, validity) now carry one row per GC, so this field catches the rest and nothing in an invitation goes unread. WHERE: GC invitation email, portal message, GC bid instructions attachment, GC pre-bid emails.

gc_name.description: GC name matched to the GCs on the BDR project

instruction.description: Short plain statement of the instruction

cite.description: Envelope citation ids that support this row

value.description: One row per GC instruction not held by a topic field

gc_instruction_deltas.x-extraction-notes: One row per instruction. Do not repeat what a topic field holds: cutoff (gc_sub_bid_cutoffs), route (submission_channels), form and license data (bid_form_format), exclusions policy, price breakdown, alternates, unit prices, bid bond, validity, attachments, RFI cutoff, prequalification, trade package scope (scope_responsibility.gc_trade_package_by_gc) and subcontract or insurance terms (contract_terms). An invitation that adds nothing gives an empty list with status found; not_stated only when no invitation text is available. Where a GC is stricter than the owner, code shows it by comparing the owner_documents and gc_invitation rows of the topic fields.
gc_instruction_deltas.x-bdr-overlap: BDR bid_notes holds GC bid instructions as free text; this field structures what the topic fields do not.

owner_bid_deadline_rules.title: Owner bid time, opening and withdrawal rules
owner_bid_deadline_rules.description: The owner's bid due date and time as the latest addendum states it, the time zone as written, which clock governs, the late-bid rule and any grace minutes, the opening type and time, any stated rule that a late addendum extends the bid date, and the rules for modifying or withdrawing a bid, including a window to withdraw for a clerical error. WHY: Addenda move bid dates and BDR's actual bid due is typed by a person, so this is the check on it. National portals may post Eastern or Central time, and time-stamped portals reject a bid one second late. A public opening publishes competitor prices for win/loss history. When a late addendum lands inside the owner's own extension window, or a bid-day math error surfaces after submission, the team needs the rule at hand. WHERE: Advertisement for Bids (00 11 16); Instructions to Bidders (00 21 13) deadline, opening, addenda and withdrawal articles; owner portal listing header; addenda.

bid_due_datetime.description: Owner bid due date and time per the latest addendum

time_zone_as_stated.description: Time zone written with the bid time

opening_datetime.description: Opening date and time when different from the due time

window_before_due.description: Addenda issued within this period before the due time trigger the rule

late_addendum_extension.description: Stated rule that an addendum issued close to the deadline extends the bid date

modification_before_deadline.description: How a bid may be modified or withdrawn before the deadline, as stated

window.description: Time after the deadline or opening to request withdrawal, as written

error_withdrawal.description: Withdrawal for a clerical or math error after the deadline

value.description: Owner bid deadline and procedure rules

owner_bid_deadline_rules.x-extraction-notes: Take the bid date from the latest addendum; the base value it replaced goes to superseded_by_addendum, and code compares bid_due_datetime with BDR's actual bid due and flags a mismatch. Never assume Pacific on a national portal: an unwritten time zone is not_stated. Record grace minutes only when printed. The error-withdrawal window comes only from this project's Instructions to Bidders: Division 00 often edits the AIA A701 default, so the default is never filled in. Whether the owner honored its own late-addendum rule is computed from document_control.addenda_log and the bid date history, not extracted.
owner_bid_deadline_rules.x-reference-facts: AIA A701-2018 Section 4.4.3 (form default only): a bidder that finds a clerical error after the bid time must notify the Architect within two days (not stated as business days) or within the time the jurisdiction's law sets; on satisfactory proof the bid is withdrawn and may not be resubmitted. The project's own Instructions to Bidders govern.
owner_bid_deadline_rules.x-bdr-overlap: BDR stores actual bid due (date and time) as a team entry; this field confirms it from the documents and adds time zone, governing clock, late rule, opening, extension and withdrawal rules.

bid_form_format.title: Required bid form and license data
bid_form_format.description: For the owner's documents and for each GC: whether a specific form must be used (owner bid form, the GC's own form or spreadsheet, portal line items) or G3's own proposal is accepted, the form reference, signature or notary rules, which license and business data must be written on it, and any product whose manufacturer must be named on the bid and whether that choice then binds. WHY: Submitting on our own letterhead when a form is mandatory is an avoidable non-responsiveness trigger, and forms replaced by late addenda are a common miss. A form that makes a named switchgear, fixture or generator manufacturer binding locks vendor choice at bid time. A missing license number on a bid or listing form can be used to challenge responsiveness on public work. WHERE: Bid Form (00 41 00) and its supplements, Instructions to Bidders, subcontractor listing form, GC invitation attachments and spreadsheets, addenda.

signature_or_notary_rules.description: Signature authority, original ink, notary or seal rules as stated

license_data_required.description: License and business data the form requires

binding_after_bid.description: True when the form says the named manufacturer may not be changed after bid

manufacturers_to_name.description: Products whose manufacturer must be named on the bid

bid_form_format.x-extraction-notes: One row for the owner's documents and one per GC that sets its own format. Use the latest addendum version of each form. Record only the product categories the form makes bidders name; approved manufacturer lists and substitution terms stay in specified_products.products. G3's license and business numbers come from company data, never from the documents.
bid_form_format.x-bdr-overlap: BDR generates its own per-GC proposal documents; this flags when that format is not acceptable and which license data the form needs.

exclusions_qualifications_allowed.title: Exclusions, qualifications and voluntary alternates
exclusions_qualifications_allowed.description: For the owner's documents and each GC: whether the bid may carry written exclusions, clarifications and assumptions or must be clean (unqualified), and separately whether voluntary alternates or value-engineering options may be offered. WHY: If qualifications are not allowed, every item we would normally exclude must be resolved by RFI before the cutoff or priced in; a qualified bid on a clean-bid job can be thrown out, while an unaddressed item on a job that allows exclusions may be plugged against us in leveling. Whether aluminum feeders, MC cable or alternate gear may be offered as a voluntary alternate is a separate pricing-strategy decision. WHERE: Instructions to Bidders, bid form certification language, GC invitation ('no qualified bids', 'clean bid', 'voluntary alternates welcome').

source_party.description: Whose rule this row records: the owner's bid documents or one GC's invitation or sub bid instructions

gc_name.description: GC name matched to the GCs on the BDR project; null on owner_documents rows

exclusions_qualifications_allowed.x-extraction-notes: Keep the exact phrase ('no qualified bids', 'bids with exceptions may be rejected') in the citation. The page shows the strictest rule that applies to each GC. A GC may reject exclusions yet invite value-engineering options on a separate sheet, so the two properties are answered independently.
exclusions_qualifications_allowed.x-bdr-overlap: BDR proposals carry scope lines; there is no stored flag for whether exclusions or voluntary alternates are permitted.

required_price_breakdown.title: Required price breakdown
required_price_breakdown.description: The line items the bid form or a GC spreadsheet requires the electrical number to be split into (by building, phase, system such as site lighting, fire alarm or low voltage, by CSI section, labor versus material, or other separately priced items). Alternates, unit prices and allowances have their own fields. WHY: GCs level electrical bids line by line; a lump sum against a form that asked for a breakdown gets set aside or miscategorized even when the total is competitive. The breakdown also dictates how pricing must be organized before bid day. WHERE: Bid Form (00 41 00) breakdown or schedule of values page, GC bid spreadsheet or scope sheet, portal line items, bid form addenda.

alternates.title: Bid alternates
alternates.description: Every add or deduct alternate that changes electrical scope directly (add generator and ATS, LED upgrade package) or indirectly (a mechanical, architectural or site alternate that adds or removes connections, circuits or trenching), with number, title, defining drawings and spec sections, and who asks G3 to price it. WHY: Owners pick the winning GC on base bid plus selected alternates, so an unpriced or guessed alternate can flip the award. Other trades' alternates that ripple into electrical become unpriced scope if accepted later. WHERE: Alternates section (01 23 00), bid form alternates schedule, drawings with alternate clouds or notes, addenda.

The bid form description is often vaguer than the drawings; cite both. An empty list with status found means the documents say there are no alternates; not_stated means silence. Indirect rows name the other trade's alternate and the electrical items it touches.

unit_prices.title: Required unit prices
unit_prices.description: Each unit price the bid form or a GC requires for electrical or underground work ($/LF additional trench, $/each light pole, $/LF conduit and wire by size, $/CY rock excavation), with unit, base quantity if stated, what the rate must include (OH&P, mobilization, restoration) and whether add and deduct rates differ. WHY: Blank unit price lines can make a bid non-responsive, and unit prices become the contract rate for quantity changes for the life of the job, so an unloaded rate bleeds margin on every change. WHERE: Unit Prices section (01 22 00), unit price form in the bid form supplements or bid form schedule, GC spreadsheet.

allowances.title: Allowances to carry
allowances.description: Each cash, quantity or contingency allowance touching electrical work (fixture allowance, utility company fee allowance, temporary power allowance, testing and inspection allowance), with subject, amount, what it covers (material only, material and labor, installed complete), markup treatment and how unused amounts are credited. WHY: Allowances must be carried exactly as stated or the bid looks like a math error or is non-responsive. When the allowance section and the product section disagree on labor, G3 can end up installing allowance material at no charge. WHERE: Allowances section (01 21 00), bid form allowance schedule, the product section the allowance points to (for example 26 51 00 for a fixture allowance), Supplementary Conditions.

substitution_prior_approval.title: Substitution request deadline
substitution_prior_approval.description: The deadline (a fixed date and time, or a lead time before bid) and procedure for getting a non-named product approved before bid: required form, supporting data, where to submit, how approvals are announced, and whether substitutions after bid are barred. WHY: Pre-bid approval is usually the only legitimate way to bid a lower-cost gear, fixture or generator manufacturer. Missing the date locks the bid to the basis-of-design price and lead time, and addenda often move or reopen the window. WHERE: Instructions to Bidders substitution clause, Substitution Procedures (01 25 00), bidding-phase substitution request form, addenda and RFI answers.

substitution_prior_approval.x-extraction-notes: Store a relative deadline as written (relative_deadline plus relative_anchor); code computes the absolute deadline for the bid brief and calendar from BDR's actual bid due. Instructions to Bidders and 01 25 00 sometimes conflict; keep both positions and let the latest addendum govern. Per-section manufacturer lists and or-equal terms belong in specified_products.products, which points here for the deadline.

bid_bond.title: Bid bond
bid_bond.description: For the owner's documents and each GC: whether bid security is required of G3 itself or only of the prime bidder, the amount (percent of bid or fixed sum), accepted instruments, required form, surety qualifications, whether an original must be delivered in hard copy, and forfeiture terms. WHY: A missing required bid bond is an instant disqualification and a same-day bond request can fail. The bond uses surety capacity, and the forfeiture language defines what it costs to walk away from a number we cannot honor. WHERE: Bid Security form (00 43 13), Instructions to Bidders, Advertisement for Bids, GC invitation (flow-down to subs).

required_license_classifications.x-extraction-notes: Extract only licenses the documents or a GC's invitation state. Never add a class because the scope seems to need it: under NAC 624.200 a full C-2 performs all C-2 subclass work, so scope-implied subclasses are usually wrong, and the separate State Fire Marshal fire alarm license is applied by the maintained scope-to-license rule in labor_and_compliance.compliance_rule_checks. Whether G3 holds each license comes from company license data and is compared by code. Staff certifications (NICET, RCDD, SFM certificate of registration per installer) belong in low_voltage_life_safety.
required_license_classifications.x-reference-facts: NAC 624.200: a full C-2 may install any electrical wires, fixtures, apparatus, raceways and conduit and may do all work of every C-2 subclass. Subclasses: C-2a Electrical Wiring; C-2b Integrated Ceilings; C-2c Fire Detection; C-2d Low Voltage Systems (fiber or 91 V or less; does not cover fire detection); C-2e Lines to Transmit Electricity (overhead or underground secondary lines, poles, towers, transformers, substations, breakers); C-2f Residential Wiring (600 V or less, 3 stories or fewer); C-2g Photovoltaics (not wiring beyond the service panel). Site-lighting feeders are ordinary C-2 wiring, not C-2e. Fire alarm may be done under C-2, C-2c or C-41c (Fire Alarms, NAC 624.572) and also needs a State Fire Marshal firm license, with an SFM certificate holder on every job site and a NICET Level II or PE designer (NAC 477.300). A bid or contract outside the license scope is void (NAC 624.640(1)), and a licensee must confirm that anyone whose bid it considers is appropriately licensed (NAC 624.640(6)).

labor_and_compliance.description: What the project documents say about wage law, wage determinations, classification exceptions, premium time, certified payroll, apprentices, labor agreements, local hire, safety staffing, Nevada public works listing and preference, federal overlays and sales tax, plus compliance_rule_checks, where the maintained statutory reference table is applied to the record. prevailing_wage_basis.title: Prevailing wage basis
prevailing_wage_basis.description: Which wage law the documents apply: Nevada prevailing wage (NRS 338), federal Davis-Bacon or Davis-Bacon Related Acts, both, an express statement that prevailing wage does not apply, or silence. WHY: The wage base is one of the largest labor cost drivers. Bidding open-shop rates on public work, or missing a federal overlay's weekly payroll, is a direct margin hit and a compliance exposure. WHERE: Advertisement for Bids, Instructions to Bidders, Supplementary Conditions labor article, wage determination exhibits, federal clauses exhibit.
prevailing_wage_basis.x-extraction-notes: Decide from the documents, not from owner type: a private owner using federal money can carry Davis-Bacon, and a public job can be silent. not_prevailing_wage needs text that says so. Silence on a public job is not the same as no prevailing wage: compliance_rule_checks compares owner type and the estimate with the NRS 338.080 threshold. When both apply, record state_and_federal; the rate schedule is now the same, but federal payroll rules still differ (see certified_payroll).
prevailing_wage_basis.x-reference-facts: Nevada prevailing wage applies to public works estimated at $100,000 or more, with no splitting to avoid it (NRS 338.080). Davis-Bacon Related Acts cover federal and federally assisted construction contracts over $2,000. On April 17, 2026 USDOL accepted Nevada's state prevailing wage rates as the Davis-Bacon rates, retroactive to the October 1, 2025 rates, with future updates adopted together, so there is no higher-of comparison between schedules; federal weekly certified payroll, the $2,000 threshold and the federal WD reference still apply.
prevailing_wage_basis.x-bdr-overlap: BDR wage_type (prevailing_wage | non_prevailing_wage) is the team's answer; compare it with this field and flag mismatches.

wage_determinations.title: Wage determinations
wage_determinations.description: Each wage determination the documents cite or attach: for the state schedule, the region, book year and amendment number as printed; for a federal decision, the WD number, modification and construction type; the effective date and covered bid window when printed; and whether it is attached or only referenced. WHY: Rates differ by region and change every October 1, with amendments between. A book from the wrong year or region under- or over-prices labor; bids opening on or after October 1, 2026 fall under the 2026-2027 book, so a number priced this week on the 2025-2026 book is wrong if the opening slips. WHERE: Wage rate exhibit attached to Division 00, Supplementary Conditions, Instructions to Bidders, federal wage decision exhibit, addenda.

wage_determinations.x-extraction-notes: One row per determination. Record book year and amendment exactly as printed; leave dates null when not printed and never compute them. Compare every addendum's wage exhibit with the prior one. Rates are joined from the maintained rate table by pw_region, book_year and amendment, never re-extracted from the PDF. The October 1 rollover and the 36-month rate lock are rules in compliance_rule_checks (pw_book_rollover, pw_rate_lock_36_months), not properties here. When the documents cite a determination that is not in the package, attached is false and the envelope may be referenced_not_provided.
wage_determinations.x-reference-facts: NRS 338.025 sets four regions: Clark (Clark County); Southern Rural (Esmeralda, Lincoln and Nye counties); Northern Rural (Carson City plus Churchill, Douglas, Elko, Eureka, Humboldt, Lander, Lyon, Mineral, Storey, Pershing and White Pine); Washoe (Washoe County). Rates are issued October 1 of odd years for 2 years (NRS 338.030(7)), adjusted and reissued October 1 of even years (NRS 338.030(8)), and amended mid-year; each book covers bids from October 1 to September 30. The current Clark book, '2026 Prevailing Wage Rates, Clark County Region' (determination date October 1, 2025; Amendment #07 effective 6/24/26), covers public works over $100,000 bid or awarded October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026. Rates in effect at bid opening apply until completion or 36 months after opening, whichever is earlier; then the rates in effect on the last day of that period apply for the next 36 months and are never lower (NRS 338.030(9)-(10)). Misclassification: federal DBA debarment is a fixed 3 years (29 CFR 5.12(a)(1)); Nevada disqualification under NRS 338.017 as amended by AB 502 (effective January 1, 2026) is up to 180 days for a first offense, 180 days to 3 years for a second, 3 to 5 years for a third and at least 5 years after that; a federal SAM debarment also bars Nevada public work for its period.
wage_determinations.x-bdr-overlap: Extends BDR wage_type with the specific determination.

WHY: Rates in the current state book come from the maintained rate table, so re-reading them from each PDF only adds the risk of pricing from a stale or wrong-year copy. What matters per project is an exception: a special determination, a reclassification by addendum, or an owner assigning low-voltage or fire alarm work to a costlier craft. Misclassification brings back wages and disqualification. WHERE: Special or federal wage determination classification tables, Supplementary Conditions labor article, Division 27/28 Part 1 articles, addenda.

craft_classifications.x-extraction-notes: Do not copy the classification table of the current state book. Extract printed rates only from a determination that is not the current state book, and code flags any difference from the rate table. Copy titles verbatim. Never map crafts to G3 scope by judgment; the reference table carries the standard mapping. Watch addenda that add or reclassify a craft. An empty list with status not_stated is the normal answer when only the standard book is cited.
craft_classifications.x-reference-facts: The Clark 2025-2026 book lists four electrical crafts, rates are totals including fringes: Electrician - Communication Technician (Installer/Technician $66.04, Senior Technician $90.56); Electrician Lineman/Groundman/Heavy Equipment Operator (Lineman $84.32); Electrician - Neon Sign; Electrician - Wireman ($90.92, Cable Splicer $91.44). There is no separate sound or low-voltage line: fire alarm, DAS, CCTV and security, sound, nurse call and data are Communication Technician scope, and raceway installation is excluded from Communication Technician and is Wireman work. The Wireman and Communication Technician rates are labeled 'Union Rate' and are the NECA-IBEW Local 357 rates.

overtime_and_shift_rules.title: Premium time and shift pay rules
overtime_and_shift_rules.description: Project text that sets premium pay: whether premium time for required night, weekend or compressed work is in the base bid or paid as extra, daily and weekly overtime thresholds, alternative schedules such as four 10-hour days and their paperwork, shift premiums, and holiday and weekend rules, from the specs, Supplementary Conditions, a PLA or a GC exhibit. WHY: Night, weekend and 10-hour shifts are common on Las Vegas resort and public jobs. On prevailing wage work the book's shift premiums and daily overtime can turn a planned night shift into premium hours that were never priced, and a clause putting all premium time in the base bid moves that risk to us. WHERE: Supplementary Conditions labor article, Division 01 work-hours article, PLA exhibit, GC subcontract exhibit.
