overtime_and_shift_rules.x-extraction-notes: Record only project text; the wage book's premiums are reference data joined by rule. Where the documents only say 'per NRS 338', leave the numbers null and say so in the note. Which hours and areas must be worked off-hours is schedule_and_site.working_hours and off_hours_work_items; GC-ordered acceleration is contract_terms.acceleration_without_compensation.
overtime_and_shift_rules.x-reference-facts: Clark 2025-2026 book, Wireman and Communication Technician: swing shift (4:30 pm to 1:00 am) +15%; graveyard shift (12:30 am to 9:00 am) +30%, both requiring 8 consecutive hours on 5 consecutive days; weekend and holiday hours at double time; zone pay measured from Las Vegas City Hall: 25 to 55 miles +$3.50, 56 to 85 miles +$4.50, over 85 miles +$8.50; wiremen welding +5%; work within 5 ft of a fall of 60 ft or more +0.5x.
overtime_and_shift_rules.x-bdr-overlap: BDR labor_time (day_work | night_work) and labor_note; this field holds the pay rules that price those hours.

certified_payroll.title: Certified payroll and labor reporting
certified_payroll.description: Whether certified payroll is required, how often, the system or format (LCPtracker, a state online system, WH-347), the GC's own deadline for G3's payroll and whether late payroll is backcharged, and other labor reports required (apprentice hours, workforce utilization, fringe statements, worker interviews). WHY: Reporting takes office hours every covered period and some owner systems need onboarding before mobilization. The GC's deadline is often earlier than the statute and sets G3's internal deadline; a late payroll can be backcharged by the GC and is an NSCB discipline ground. WHERE: General or Supplementary Conditions labor compliance article, prevailing wage exhibit, owner labor compliance manual, GC subcontract exhibit.

system_or_format.description: Named system or form exactly as written

gc_deadline.description: Time after the period end by which the GC requires G3's certified payroll, as written

backcharge_for_late_payroll.description: True when the GC states it will backcharge or withhold for late payroll

certified_payroll.x-extraction-notes: Record the named system exactly. The GC's deadline is often in the subcontract exhibit rather than Division 00; store it as written. Code compares it with the NRS 338.070(7) safe harbor in compliance_rule_checks and sets G3's internal deadline to the earlier date.
certified_payroll.x-reference-facts: Nevada: the contractor and each sub keep monthly payroll records (NRS 338.070(5)-(7)); the public body must receive a copy for each calendar month within 15 days after month end, and a sub that gives its record to the GC within 10 days after month end is protected from GC withholding for late filing. Failing to file a required certified payroll report is an NSCB discipline ground (NRS 624.3016(9)). Federal DBRA: weekly certified payrolls for each week of covered work (29 CFR 5.5(a)(3)(ii); WH-347 optional) on contracts over $2,000. Apprentice-ratio compliance is checked by the Labor Commissioner through the annual AUA report, not by the awarding body.
certified_payroll.x-bdr-overlap: BDR Certified Payroll module (/payroll, PW-only enrollment); this field says whether and how the project must be enrolled and gives the GC deadline the module should track.

apprentice_utilization.title: Apprentice utilization
apprentice_utilization.description: What the documents say about apprentice utilization: whether they invoke the Apprentice Utilization Act, the construction type they state (vertical, horizontal or mixed), any percent they print, and any owner request for apprentice reporting on this project. WHY: Apprentice compliance is now measured per contractor per calendar year across all Nevada public works, so one project's clause does not set its own target; what the project adds is the owner's reporting asks and the crew mix it implies. G3's annual compliance and per-job apprentice request log live in company compliance records, outside this record. WHERE: Instructions to Bidders, Supplementary Conditions, public works special conditions, addenda and pre-bid minutes.

clause_invoked.description: Whether the documents invoke the Apprentice Utilization Act

percent_stated.description: Apprentice percent printed in the documents

owner_reporting_requested.description: Apprentice reporting the owner asks for on this project, as stated

value.description: Apprentice utilization as the documents state it

apprentice_utilization.x-extraction-notes: Record only what the documents print; if they cite the statute without numbers, leave percent_stated null. There is no per-project waiver to extract after SB 82 (2023): a waiver or 'SB 207' reference in older boilerplate is flagged in the note as outdated text, not recorded as a status. Scan addenda and pre-bid minutes for 'apprentice'.
apprentice_utilization.x-reference-facts: NRS 338.01165 as amended by SB 82 (2023) and AB 502 (2025, effective January 1, 2026): minimums of 10% of hours on vertical and 3% on horizontal construction per apprenticed craft (the Labor Commissioner may raise them by up to 2 points), measured per contractor per calendar year across all its Nevada public works; no penalty when the year's required apprentice hours are under 40 (vertical) or 24 (horizontal). Annual report due February 15. Good faith requires requesting apprentices no earlier than 30 days before starting and no later than 5 days after, then every 30 days. Vertical penalties: 7.5% to under 10%, $2,500 or $2 per short hour; over 4% to under 7.5%, $3,000 or $4; 4% or less, $5,000 or $6 (whichever is higher in each band); horizontal bands are 2-3%, 1-2% and 1% or less. Failing to report: $10,000 to $75,000 or 180-day to 2-year disqualification. No apprentice is required in a craft with no recognized program in the jurisdiction (NRS 338.01165(6)); job-order contracts have their own waiver (NRS 338.1574). The per-project 'more than three employees' trigger and awarding-body waivers were 2019 SB 207 guidance and are obsolete.

project_labor_agreement.title: Project labor agreement and union rules
project_labor_agreement.description: Whether a project labor agreement or union requirement applies: agreement name or exhibit, whether subs must sign a letter of assent, covered trades, hiring hall dispatch rules for electricians, core employee allowances, and benefit fund contributions. WHY: A PLA can force hiring through the hall, add fund contributions and change crew makeup and cost; missing it can make a competitive bid impossible to staff as priced. WHERE: Instructions to Bidders, Supplementary Conditions, PLA exhibit, owner labor policy, GC invitation.

agreement_reference.description: Agreement name, exhibit or document reference

letter_of_assent_required.description: True when subs must sign a letter of assent

hiring_hall_dispatch_required.description: True when electricians must be dispatched through the hall

fund_contributions.description: Benefit or industry fund contributions required, as written

project_labor_agreement.x-extraction-notes: Scan Division 00, Supplementary Conditions, exhibits and the invitation for 'project labor agreement', 'PLA', 'community workforce agreement', 'letter of assent' and 'signatory'; always run the check rather than skipping it by owner type or local history. Leave dispatch details null when no agreement exists.
project_labor_agreement.x-reference-facts: FAR subpart 22.5 (FAC 2026-01, effective March 13, 2026) requires a project labor agreement on federal construction contracts estimated at $35 million or more unless the senior procurement executive grants an exception. The Clark Electrician - Wireman and Communication Technician prevailing rates are the NECA-IBEW Local 357 union rates, so no separate IBEW wage benchmark is stored.
project_labor_agreement.x-bdr-overlap: BDR labor_note may mention union requirements as free text.

local_workforce_requirements.title: Local hire and workforce goals
local_workforce_requirements.description: Owner or funding-program workforce requirements beyond wage law: local or Nevada-resident hiring percentages, disadvantaged or veteran worker hiring goals, workforce reporting, and penalties. WHY: These goals limit who G3 can staff with and add reporting, which changes crew planning and cost on public authority and publicly funded projects. WHERE: Supplementary Conditions, owner workforce or community benefits exhibit, Instructions to Bidders, bid form certifications.

target.description: Target as written, for example '15% of craft hours by Clark County residents'

cite.description: Envelope citation ids that support this row

local_workforce_requirements.x-extraction-notes: Record only what is written. Workforce conditions tied to the Nevada bidder's preference go in bidders_preference; apprentice rules go in apprentice_utilization.

safety_training_and_staffing.title: Safety staffing, training and programs
safety_training_and_staffing.description: Safety requirements in the documents, the GC safety exhibit or the subcontract that cost money: required worker and foreman training (OSHA 10 or 30, NFPA 70E and others), a dedicated or full-time safety person above a crew size, written programs due before mobilization (site-specific safety plan, fall protection, lockout/tagout, confined space, heat illness) and when they are due, project-specific heat illness rules beyond the state regulation, and whether the GC fines or backcharges safety violations. WHY: A required full-time safety person or paid training is labor cost rarely in a standard estimate; written programs due before mobilization take office hours; heat rules beyond the regulation (stop-work temperatures, extra breaks) cut summer productivity on trenching and site work; GC safety fines come straight out of margin. WHERE: Division 01 safety section, GC safety exhibit or subcontract safety article, owner safety manual, GC invitation or prequalification.

other_name.description: Training name when training is other

applies_to.description: Who must have it

is_required.description: Whether a dedicated safety person is required of subs

trigger.description: Crew size, contract value or other trigger as written

full_time.description: True when the role must be full time on site

programs_due.description: When written programs are due, as written, for example '10 days before mobilization'

heat_illness_project_rules.description: Project-specific heat rules beyond the state regulation, as stated

fines_or_backcharges.description: True when the GC states fines or backcharges for safety violations

value.description: Project safety staffing, training and program requirements

safety_training_and_staffing.x-extraction-notes: This field absorbs contract_terms.gc_safety_requirements (programs, dedicated staff, training, fines, submission timing) and the former heat_illness_requirements field. Orientation hours stay only in schedule_and_site.badging_and_screening. EMR and safety-rate caps are qualification_minimums; badging, background checks and drug testing are schedule_and_site. The Nevada OSHA heat rule and the Clark County Dust Control Class apply by regulation and are attached by compliance_rule_checks; record them here only when the project documents themselves require them.
safety_training_and_staffing.x-reference-facts: Nevada OSHA heat illness regulation R131-24AP (adopted October 28, 2024; effective when filed November 15, 2024; enforced since April 29, 2025) applies to employers with more than 10 employees: a one-time written job hazard analysis listing job classifications where most employees are exposed to heat for more than 30 minutes of any 60-minute period, a designated person, and safety-program provisions for potable water, a rest break for an employee showing heat-illness signs, means of cooling, monitoring, training before work and emergency procedures. It has no temperature trigger and no preventive 95 F cool-down breaks (those are California rules); Nevada OSHA treats days of 90 F or more as heat priority days for inspections. Clark County AQR 94.10: the site superintendent, all construction supervisors and foremen of on-site contractors and subcontractors, and water-truck drivers must complete the Dust Control Class at least once every 3 years.

subcontractor_listing.title: Subcontractor listing
subcontractor_listing.description: Whether the documents invoke a public works subcontractor listing rule (NRS 338.141 or an owner rule), which listing path they use (a public body list of portions over 3 percent of its estimate, or subs over 5 percent of the prime's bid), the portions on that list and whether electrical is one, the listing form, the information the GC needs from G3, and whether G3 must list its own lower-tier subs. WHY: If G3 is not listed correctly and on time the GC's bid can be non-responsive and G3 can lose the work. When electrical is on the public body's list, the GC must name its electrical sub in the bid itself. WHERE: Instructions to Bidders, bid form subcontractor list page, public works special conditions, GC invitation (requests for license and scope information).

applies.description: Which listing rule the documents invoke

portions_listed.description: Portions of work on the public body's list, as written

electrical_on_public_body_list.description: True when an electrical portion is on the public body's list

info_gc_needs_from_g3.description: Information the GC asks G3 for

g3_must_list_lower_tier.description: True when G3 must disclose its own lower-tier subs

value.description: Subcontractor listing rule as the documents state it

subcontractor_listing.x-extraction-notes: Record what the documents say; the statute's thresholds and deadlines are reference data. Copy the portions from a public body list verbatim. Use not_applicable_stated only when the documents say listing does not apply; otherwise silence is not_stated and compliance_rule_checks uses owner type. Whether G3 was actually listed is team entry in history_and_outcome.
subcontractor_listing.x-reference-facts: NRS 338.141 applies to competitively bid public works advertised under NRS 338.1385(1)(a) or 338.143(1)(a) (estimated cost over $100,000) and to NDOT work under NRS 408.327; design-build final proposals are exempt (NRS 338.1727). Path (a): if the public body provides a list of the portions it estimates to exceed 3% of estimated cost, the bid names the first-tier sub for each. Path (b): with no list, the bid names every first-tier sub paid more than 5% of the prime's total bid; only under path (b), within 2 hours after bid opening ends, the three lowest bidders submit every first-tier sub paid more than $250,000 and, if any sub is not over $250,000, every first-tier sub paid 1% of the prime's total bid or $50,000, whichever is greater. The bid gives each listed sub's name and a description of its work (338.141(2)); NRS 624 license numbers go on the post-opening list (338.141(1)(b)(3)). The prime lists itself and describes self-performed work over 1% of its bid (338.141(3)). A late list, or naming a sub on SPWD disqualified status without an acceptable replacement before award, makes the bid nonresponsive. Last amended 2013.

bidders_preference.title: Nevada bidder's preference
bidders_preference.description: Whether the documents invoke Nevada's public works bidder's preference, whether they state that federal funding precludes it, and the conditions the GC's invitation or subcontract passes to subs when the GC bids with the preference (Nevada-licensed workforce share, Nevada-registered vehicles, payroll records kept in Nevada, penalty pass-through). WHY: A GC bidding with the preference can beat lower non-preference bids, which changes which GC we sharpen our number for. If the GC uses it, G3's crews, vehicles and paperwork must meet the affidavit, and a sub that causes noncompliance owes a penalty. WHERE: Instructions to Bidders, bid form, bidder's preference affidavit, Division 00 statute references, GC subcontract exhibit.

invoked.description: Whether the documents invoke the bidder's preference

federal_preclusion_stated.description: True when the documents say federal funding rules out the preference

flowdown_conditions_to_subs.description: Conditions passed to subs when the GC bids with the preference, as stated

sub_penalty_flowdown_stated.description: True when the GC states it will pass the noncompliance penalty to subs

value.description: Bidder's preference as the documents state it

bidders_preference.x-extraction-notes: Record only what the documents and the GC say; the percent, threshold and filing terms are reference data. The preference belongs to whoever bids to the public body, so it matters to G3 when G3 bids direct or when a GC flows its affidavit commitments down.
bidders_preference.x-reference-facts: NRS 338.1389: for public works estimated over $250,000, a bidder holding an NSCB Certificate of Eligibility provides it with the bid and files the NRS 338.0117 affidavit within 2 hours after opening; its bid is then deemed best if it is not more than 5% above the lowest bid without a preference. Federal funding turns the preference off only where federal law would preclude or reduce federal assistance (338.1389(10)). The affidavit commits the job, subs included, to: at least 50% of all workers holding a Nevada driver's license or ID; Nevada-registered project vehicles; the design-build 50% design-professional rule where it applies; and payroll records kept in Nevada. A sub that causes noncompliance owes 1% of its largest contract (338.0117(6)). A certificate needs a CPA affidavit showing at least $5,000 a year in Nevada sales/use or governmental services tax for 60 months. Objections are due within 3 business days of opening.

federal_funding.title: Federal funding and flow-down clauses
federal_funding.description: Whether the documents state a federal owner or federal funding (agency, grant or loan program, military installation), and which federal requirements they flow to subs as a result: Davis-Bacon, Buy America or BABA, the Buy American Act, DBE, a federal PLA, E-Verify, SAM registration, anti-kickback and other federal clauses. WHY: Federal overlays attach by funding source, not by the owner's public or private label, so owner type cannot rule them out. Each overlay adds cost (domestic products, weekly payroll, paperwork) that must be priced. WHERE: Advertisement for Bids funding statement, Instructions to Bidders, Supplementary Conditions, federal clauses exhibit, bid form certifications.

agency_or_program.description: Federal agency, grant or loan program named

flowdown_requirements.description: Federal requirements the documents flow to subs

value.description: Federal funding and invoked federal clauses

federal_funding.x-extraction-notes: If the funding source is not stated, record not_stated rather than assuming state-only; no_federal_funds needs text that says so. Details live in prevailing_wage_basis, wage_determinations, certified_payroll, buy_american_domestic_content, participation_goals and project_labor_agreement; this field says which overlays the documents invoke.
federal_funding.x-reference-facts: Davis-Bacon Related Acts cover federal and federally assisted construction contracts over $2,000, with weekly certified payroll. FAR subpart 22.5 requires a PLA on federal construction estimated at $35 million or more unless excepted. USDOT-assisted work falls under the DBE Interim Final Rule (see participation_goals).
federal_funding.x-bdr-overlap: Complements the go/no-go owner_type answer; funding source can differ from owner type.

buy_american_domestic_content.title: Buy American and domestic content
buy_american_domestic_content.description: Each domestic content regime the documents invoke (BABA under 2 CFR 184, the Buy American Act clause FAR 52.225-9, an agency Buy America rule, or an owner or state preference), the clause cited, which categories it covers (iron and steel, manufactured products, construction materials), certifications required, listed waivers, and products the documents name as affected. WHY: Domestic content rules can eliminate normally competitive imported gear, fixtures and conduit and force a smaller, pricier, slower vendor pool; bidding normal sourcing on a covered project yields a non-compliant low number or a costly re-source after award. The component test differs by regime, so the regime must be recorded. WHERE: Division 00 federal requirements, Buy America exhibit or certification form, Product Requirements (01 60 00), Instructions to Bidders funding note.

clause_reference.description: Clause or regulation cited, as written

certification_required.description: True when a domestic content certification is required

affected_products.description: Products the documents name as covered

cite.description: Envelope citation ids that support this row

value.description: One row per domestic content regime invoked

buy_american_domestic_content.x-extraction-notes: Record which regime the documents invoke and the clause they cite; component-percentage tests are reference data by regime and never copied from memory. List products only when the documents name them. A regime row should trigger a domestic-content certification request on BDR's vendor RFQs for the affected categories. An empty list with status found means the documents state no domestic content rule applies.
buy_american_domestic_content.x-reference-facts: BABA (2 CFR 184, federally assisted infrastructure): manufactured products need domestic components over 55% of cost. FAR 52.225-9 (Buy American Act, direct federal construction): a domestic construction material needs domestic components over 65% of cost for items delivered 2024 through 2028 and over 75% from 2029; COTS items are exempt from the component test; iron and steel items must have less than 5% foreign iron and steel by cost.
buy_american_domestic_content.x-bdr-overlap: Should flag BDR vendor RFQs (General Material, Switchgear, Generator & Equipment, Lighting, Low Voltage) to ask for domestic content certification.

sales_use_tax.title: Sales and use tax treatment
sales_use_tax.description: How the documents treat sales and use tax on materials: included in the price, stated separately on the bid form, or an owner direct purchase of materials, plus whether the documents claim that an owner's exemption covers contractor purchases. WHY: Tax on materials is a large direct cost. In Nevada the contractor is the consumer and pays tax on materials, and an owner's exemption does not pass to contractors, so any document text claiming otherwise is a trap that would underprice the bid. WHERE: Instructions to Bidders, bid form tax line, Supplementary Conditions, owner-furnished material provisions.

treatment.description: How tax on materials is treated

bid_form_tax_line.description: True when the bid form has its own tax line

contractor_exemption_claimed.description: True when the documents claim an owner's exemption covers contractor purchases

value.description: Sales and use tax treatment as the documents state it

sales_use_tax.x-extraction-notes: Never infer an exemption. Text claiming that an owner's exemption reaches G3's purchases sets contractor_exemption_claimed, gets verify_action legal_review, and can never lower tax in pricing. owner_direct_purchase_stated means the owner itself buys the material; who receives and installs it is scope_responsibility.owner_furnished_equipment.
sales_use_tax.x-reference-facts: NAC 372.200: a construction contractor is the consumer of all tangible personal property bought for a construction contract and pays tax on its cost. The Department of Taxation says exemptions held by government, religious, charitable or educational entities do not extend to their contractors or subcontractors. NRS 372.325 exempts only sales made directly to the US, the State or a political subdivision. NRS 338.1423 bars Nevada public bodies from owner-furnished-material arrangements on public works unless the contract requires payment of the tax otherwise due (narrow exceptions only). Materials tax belongs in G3's cost unless the owner itself buys and furnishes the material.
sales_use_tax.x-bdr-overlap: BDR Receive Quotes records a tax attestation per vendor quote and compares tax-inclusive cost; quotes stay tax-inclusive unless this field reports owner_direct_purchase_stated.

compliance_rule_checks.title: Compliance rule checks
compliance_rule_checks.description: Results of the maintained reference rules run against this record: for each rule, whether it is triggered, the record fields it used, the reference entries it applied, a one-line detail and the action it implies. Rules cover the prevailing wage threshold, the wage book rollover and 36-month rate lock, DBRA coverage, the GC payroll deadline against the safe harbor, apprentice request timing, State Fire Marshal fire alarm licensing and other license scope checks, the Clark County dust permit trigger and Dust Control Class, summer heat exposure, the federal PLA threshold, bidder's preference flow-down, DBE goal suspension and any claimed contractor tax exemption. WHY: Statutory facts must never be written into document fields, but the team still needs to see when a statute bites this bid. This field is where the reference table meets the extracted record, with its inputs shown, so the bid brief and disqualification checklist cite a rule instead of a model's guess. WHERE: Computed by code from record fields (project_profile.owner and published_budget_or_estimate, schedule_and_site.contract_time, power_distribution.site_electrical, low_voltage_life_safety.systems_inventory, scope_responsibility.responsibility_matrix and this section) and the maintained reference table.

input_fields.description: Record field keys the rule read

reference_ids.description: Reference table entry ids the rule applied

detail.description: One line: what was found, or which input was missing

compliance_rule_checks.x-extraction-notes: Nothing here is read by the model. Each rule lives in the maintained reference table with its statute, threshold and effective dates, runs when its inputs change, and reports cannot_evaluate naming the missing input. pw_book_rollover fires when bid opening is on or after October 1 and the cited book is the prior year; pw_rate_lock_36_months fires when contract time runs past 36 months after opening. certified_payroll_gc_deadline sets G3's internal deadline to the earlier of the GC deadline and 10 days after month end. sfm_fire_alarm_license reads fire alarm scope from low_voltage_life_safety.systems_inventory and scope_responsibility.responsibility_matrix; G3's license holdings come from company data. heat_summer_outdoor_exposure uses contract_time dates against a team-set summer window and site or trench scope. dust_permit_trigger stays disabled until its threshold is verified (see needs_verification). The bid brief reads triggered rows into top_risks and disqualification_checklist.
compliance_rule_checks.x-reference-facts: Rules cite: NRS 338.080 ($100,000 prevailing wage threshold); the October 1 wage book cycle and NRS 338.030(9)-(10) (36-month rate lock); DBRA ($2,000 coverage, weekly payroll); NRS 338.070(7) (sub safe harbor 10 days after month end); NRS 338.01165 as amended by AB 502 (apprentice requests no earlier than 30 days before start and no later than 5 days after, then every 30 days); NAC 477.300 (SFM fire alarm firm license and certificate holder on site) and NAC 624.200 (a full C-2 covers all C-2 subclasses); Clark County AQR 94.10 (Dust Control Class every 3 years); Nevada OSHA R131-24AP (heat illness); FAR subpart 22.5 ($35 million federal PLA); NRS 338.1389 and 338.0117 (preference affidavit and 1% sub penalty); 49 CFR 26.51(h) and 26.55(i) (DBE goal suspension); NAC 372.200 (contractor is the consumer).
compliance_rule_checks.x-bdr-overlap: none; the maintained reference table should be shared with the Certified Payroll module's rate data.

contract_terms.title: Contract terms and commercial risk
contract_terms.description: Captures the prime and subcontract terms G3 must price, qualify on the proposal, or escalate as walk-away items before submitting a number: contract documents in hand, delay damages, changes and claims, payment and retainage, bonds, insurance, indemnity, the general warranty, escalation and long-lead release, disputes and termination. Because G3 bids one project to several GCs, most values are rows tagged with source_level and gc_name: owner documents set project-wide terms, while each GC's subcontract or invitation can set different terms for that GC. Statutory Nevada rules attach from the reference table and are never written into values.

subcontract_form_status.title: Subcontract form in bid package
subcontract_form_status.description: For each inviting GC, whether its subcontract is in the bid package and in what form: full text with exhibits, exhibits or excerpts only, named but not attached, offered on request, or not mentioned. Captures the form family (AIA A401, ConsensusDocs 750, the GC's own form, an owner-mandated form), title and edition, whether a standard form is modified by a rider, and which exhibits are attached. WHY: Every other term in this section is priced blind when the subcontract is missing: the team either requests it before bid day or carries a 'subject to mutually acceptable subcontract terms' qualification. The form family also changes how other clauses read: A401-2017 flows rights down with obligations and limits LD pass-through to sub-caused delay, while GC proprietary forms are where one-sided terms usually live. WHERE: GC invitation email or portal message; GC bid instructions; subcontract and exhibit files attached to the invitation; Division 00 table of contents (00 52 00 Agreement Form, 00 72 00 General Conditions) when the owner mandates a subcontract form.

gc_name.description: Inviting GC this row describes, as named in BDR; null only when the owner documents mandate one subcontract form for every GC.

availability.description: How much of this GC's subcontract G3 can read at bid. not_mentioned when this GC's invitation and files were read and say nothing about a subcontract.

form_family.description: Form family as the text shows it. A GC form that borrows AIA numbering but rewrites clauses is gc_proprietary.

form_title.description: Exact title of the form or document as printed.

form_edition.description: Edition or revision as printed, for example '2017' or 'Rev. 03/2024'.

modified_by_rider.description: Whether a standard form is changed by a rider, amendment or exhibit.

exhibits_included.description: Exhibits actually in the package (insurance, safety, billing, scope, schedule).

cite.description: Envelope citation ids for this row.

subcontract_form_status.x-extraction-notes: This field's subject is availability, so a subcontract that is named but not attached is status found with availability named_not_attached, not referenced_not_provided; the term fields that form would govern take referenced_not_provided instead. Write one row per inviting GC so the page shows which GCs gave G3 nothing. Check the invitation text as well as the files: GCs often write 'our standard subcontract will apply' without attaching it. Never fill other contract_terms fields from a named form's standard text; they are filled only from text that is actually in the package.
subcontract_form_status.x-reference-facts: When the A401-2017 text is actually the contract: Art. 2 makes flow-down mutual (rights and obligations), sec. 3.4.1 limits LD assessment to delay the sub caused, sec. 6.4 is a GC-sub mutual consequential damages waiver with an LD carve-out (fact-checked 2026-09-23 against the form text).
subcontract_form_status.x-bdr-overlap: BDR stores several GCs per project with per-GC proposal sends, so rows key on the BDR GC name. BDR file categories (drawings, specifications, addenda, rfp, marked plans) have no contract category; subcontract files usually land under rfp or specifications.

prime_contract_availability.title: Prime contract in bid package
prime_contract_availability.description: Whether the owner-GC agreement and its general and supplementary conditions are in the bid package, partly included (conditions without the agreement), or only referenced; the prime form (AIA A101/A201, ConsensusDocs 200, a public agency form, a design-build form); agreement blanks left unfilled in the bid set (LD rate, contract time); and which parts are missing. WHY: Flow-down binds G3 to prime terms (LD rate, notice windows, insurance limits, dispute forum) whether or not G3 has read them. When the prime is missing or its blanks are empty, those terms are priced blind, so the team requests it or qualifies the proposal to exclude unseen prime obligations. WHERE: Bid package file list; Division 00 table of contents (00 52 00, 00 72 00, 00 73 00); Instructions to Bidders; GC bid instructions stating the subcontract incorporates the prime by reference.

availability.description: How much of the owner-GC contract is in the package.

blanks_unfilled.description: Agreement terms printed as blanks in the bid set, for example 'liquidated damages rate', 'contract time'.

missing_parts.description: Prime documents referenced but not in the package.

prime_contract_availability.x-extraction-notes: Same rule as subcontract_form_status: availability is the value, so a referenced but missing prime is found with availability referenced_not_included. GCs commonly withhold the prime until award; public packages usually include general and supplementary conditions but leave agreement blanks unfilled. List blanks in blanks_unfilled so liquidated_damages and schedule_and_site.contract_time can show why they are empty. A missing prime also appears in document_control.referenced_documents_not_provided; keep the two consistent.
prime_contract_availability.x-bdr-overlap: BDR file categories have no contract category; prime contract files usually land under rfp or specifications.

flow_down_clause.title: Flow-down clause
flow_down_clause.description: How far the subcontract binds G3 to the prime contract: full flow-down of every obligation the GC owes the owner, only listed provisions, or none; whether the GC's matching rights and remedies (time extensions, claim rights, payment protections) flow to G3 too or only the obligations do; which documents are incorporated by reference; and any prime provisions expressly not flowed down. WHY: A one-directional full flow-down imports the owner's LD rate, notice windows, insurance limits and dispute forum into G3's deal while withholding the relief the GC gets. It decides whether the prime must be read before pricing and whether 'rights flow down with obligations' goes on the proposal. The trap lives in GC-drafted subcontracts and riders; the AIA A401-2017 form itself is mutual. WHERE: Subcontract 'Contract Documents', 'Mutual Rights and Responsibilities' or 'Scope' article; GC bid instructions ('subcontract will incorporate the prime contract by reference'); owner General or Supplementary Conditions requiring the GC to bind its subcontractors (A201 sec. 5.3 style).

flow_down_clause.x-extraction-notes: Rows per source layer: owner documents, and each GC's subcontract or invitation (see section purpose). A GC row that differs from the owner row is not a conflict; conflicting is for two current texts at the same layer. Read the words, never the form name: rights_flow_down is mutual only when the text gives G3 the benefit of the GC's rights, remedies and redress against the owner. GC forms and riders often keep the obligations half of A401 Art. 2 and drop the rights half. When the subcontract is not in the package the envelope is referenced_not_provided with a request_document action. A full flow-down to a prime that is missing (prime_contract_availability) is a request_document or qualification row in contract_term_actions.
flow_down_clause.x-reference-facts: AIA A401-2017 Art. 2 is bidirectional: the GC assumes toward the sub the obligations the owner assumes toward the GC, and the sub gets the benefit of all rights, remedies and redress the GC has against the owner (fact-checked 2026-09-23 against the form text). One-directional flow-down is a feature of custom GC subcontracts, not of A401.

contract_exceptions_allowed.description: For each GC, whether bidders may take exceptions to the subcontract terms with the bid, whether submitting a price accepts the GC's subcontract without exception, or whether terms are negotiated after award. WHY: This decides how every risky term in this section is handled. If the bid is acceptance, a bad indemnity, LD or pay-if-paid clause must be priced or the bid declined; if exceptions are allowed they ride as proposal qualifications. Taking exceptions a GC forbids can get the number set aside in leveling. WHERE: GC invitation email or portal message; GC bid instructions; GC bid form fine print ('bidder agrees to execute the Contractor's standard subcontract'); Instructions to Bidders (00 21 13) when the owner sets the rule for sub bids.

liquidated_damages.title: Liquidated damages
liquidated_damages.description: Each LD rate in the contract documents: what it applies to (contract completion, substantial or final completion, an interim milestone, a building or phase), whether the amount is stated, left blank in the bid set or held in a document not provided, the amount and unit (per calendar day, per working day, per occurrence), and any cap. WHY: Electrical sits on the critical path for permanent power, gear energization, life safety and final inspections. A daily rate that reaches G3 can exceed the whole electrical fee within weeks of a gear slip, so rate times a realistic delay drives schedule contingency, a cap or apportionment qualification, or a no-go. WHERE: Owner-GC Agreement (00 52 00) or Supplementary Conditions (00 73 00) LD article; bid form; 01 10 00 Summary or 01 32 00 when milestones carry their own rate; GC invitation when the GC restates the rate; addenda.

This applies only when the A401 text is the contract.

delay_damages_exposure.title: Delay damages reaching G3
delay_damages_exposure.description: How delay costs reach G3 at each layer: whether owner LDs pass through in full or only to the extent G3 caused the delay; which actual delay costs the GC may also charge (GC extended general conditions, other trades' costs, the owner's actual damages); whether LDs are stated as the sole and exclusive remedy for delay or are in addition to actual damages; and any cap on G3's delay liability. WHY: LDs plus actual damages is the worst-case stack, and uncapped actual damages is exposure no margin can cover. A high but exclusive LD rate limited to sub-caused delay is often safer than a low non-exclusive one passed through in full. It drives the 'LDs only to the extent caused by G3, as the sole remedy' qualification or an executive-review flag. WHERE: LD article in 00 52 00 or 00 73 00 ('in addition to', 'not a penalty', 'sole and exclusive remedy'); subcontract 'Time', 'Delay', 'Damages' or 'Claims' article; GC backcharge rights for other trades' delay costs.

no_damages_for_delay.title: No-damages-for-delay clause
no_damages_for_delay.description: Whether G3 is limited to a time extension (no money) for delays caused by the owner, GC or other trades, and which exceptions are kept (active interference, bad faith, unreasonable length, delays not contemplated at signing). WHY: Electrical is routinely stacked behind late framing, ceilings and utility energization. Without delay compensation, extended supervision, remobilization and idle crews come out of margin, so the bid needs float in general conditions or a qualification carving out GC-caused delay. WHERE: General Conditions delay or time-extension article (00 72 00, 00 73 00); subcontract 'Delays' or 'Extensions of Time' article.

acceleration_without_compensation.title: Acceleration and resequencing without pay
acceleration_without_compensation.description: Whether the GC can order G3 to add crews, work overtime or extra shifts, or resequence work to meet the GC's schedule as revised, and whether that is paid when G3 did not cause the delay (fully, premium time only, or never). WHY: Overtime and shift premiums, especially at prevailing-wage rates, erase margin at trim-out and energization when schedules compress. A clause that makes acceleration free regardless of cause must be priced as contingency or qualified ('acceleration for delays not caused by G3 is extra work'). WHERE: Subcontract 'Schedule', 'Progress' or 'Time' article ('furnish sufficient manpower', 'at no additional cost'); 01 32 00 schedule requirements; GC schedule exhibit.

notice_deadlines.title: Notice deadlines for claims, changes and delays
notice_deadlines.description: Each written-notice deadline set for G3 or the GC: delay, changed or extra work, differing site conditions, claims, force majeure and backcharge disputes, with the time limit and its unit, the triggering event, whether notice must be written, whether late notice waives the claim, and any follow-up documentation deadline. WHY: Courts routinely enforce these as conditions precedent; one reported case denied a subcontractor more than $3M for missing a 5-day delay notice. Windows of 48 hours to a few days must be known by the PM and foreman on day one, and a subcontract window shorter than the prime's is a proposal qualification. WHERE: General Conditions 'Claims' and 'Changes' articles (00 72 00, 00 73 00); 01 26 00; subcontract 'Notice', 'Claims', 'Changes' and 'Delays' articles; force majeure article.

change_order_markup.title: Change order pricing: markups and T&M basis
change_order_markup.description: The overhead and profit allowed on change work by who marks up (GC, G3's tier, lower-tier subs), whose forces did the work and the cost category, with any change-size condition; plus how change work is priced: whether bond and insurance cost may be added, how deductive changes are credited, whether T&M uses fixed rates submitted at bid, actual cost plus markup or an owner or GC rate table, whether T&M rates may escalate, the small-tools and consumables percent, and the equipment rate source. WHY: Field changes are where electrical recovers margin on incomplete or renovation designs. A low cap, 'credit full OH&P on deducts', or a fixed labor-rate table with no escalation on a multi-year prevailing-wage job changes the go/no-go math on any job likely to generate changes and belongs in contingency or a qualification. WHERE: 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures Part 1; 00 73 00 changes article; subcontract 'Changes in the Work' article and T&M exhibit; bid form attachments (00 41 13) when rates are required with the bid.

change_order_authorization_and_pass_thro.title: Change authorization and pass-through terms
change_order_authorization_and_pass_thro.description: Whether extra work is paid only with a change order signed before the work starts, whether verbal or field directions are compensable, the deadline to submit change pricing, whether G3 must proceed with disputed work, and whether G3's recovery on owner-caused changes is limited to what the GC recovers from the owner (pass-through or liquidating terms). differing_site_conditions_relief.title: Differing site conditions relief
differing_site_conditions_relief.description: Whether the contract gives a price and time adjustment for concealed or unknown conditions (subsurface rock or caliche, unmarked utilities, hidden conditions in existing buildings) or makes G3 represent it examined the site and accepts all conditions; whether the geotechnical report is a contract document or information only; and whether excavation is unclassified (rock included) or rock is paid separately. WHY: Trenching and duct bank work in the Las Vegas valley regularly hits caliche and unmarked lines. With no relief, a 'for information only' geotech report and unclassified excavation, rock and utility conflicts are unrecoverable, so the bid carries a rock contingency or a qualification (exclude rock or caliche, offer a unit rate). WHERE: 00 72 00 or 00 73 00 concealed or unknown conditions article; 00 31 32 Geotechnical Data; Instructions to Bidders site-examination clause; subcontract 'Site Examination' article; 31 23 00 Excavation and Fill ('unclassified excavation').

payment_contingency.title: Pay-if-paid or pay-when-paid
payment_contingency.description: Whether G3's payment is conditioned on the GC being paid by the owner (pay-if-paid: owner credit risk moves to G3), timed to it with an outside time limit (pay-when-paid), or due on a fixed schedule regardless of owner payment. WHY: A true pay-if-paid clause can leave G3 unpaid for finished work if the owner fails, which matters most on private developer work. It drives which owner and GC pairings G3 accepts, whether to ask for owner financing information, and whether to qualify the proposal. WHERE: Subcontract 'Payment' or 'Progress Payments' article; GC bid instructions summarizing payment terms; 00 73 00 payment article when the owner documents govern sub payment.

payment_timing.x-reference-facts: NRS 624.624(1): with a written payment schedule, the GC pays on the scheduled date or within 10 days after it receives payment, whichever is earlier; without one, within 30 days after the sub's request or 10 days after GC receipt, whichever is earlier. Public works, NRS 338.550: GC pays subs within 10 days after receiving payment (fact-checked 2026-09-23).

WHY: Retainage is held-back cash: on a thin-margin job 5 to 10 percent held for months is a financing cost to model per project. retainage_terms.x-reference-facts: Public works: NRS 338.515 (public body to prime) withholds 5 percent until 50 percent complete, then may release; if it keeps withholding it may hold at most 2.5 percent of each later payment and must first release half the retainage held; interest is paid quarterly. NRS 338.555 (GC to sub) caps retention at 5 percent before 50 percent of the subcontract work with the same step-down, and the GC must pass the sub's share of retainage interest within 10 days. Governing range is NRS 338.400 to 338.645; 'NRS 338.5455' does not exist. Private: NRS 624.609(2)(a)(1) and 624.624(2)(a)(1) cap retention at 5 percent of each payment (SB 254, 2015; contracts from January 1, 2016 per secondary source) (fact-checked 2026-09-23).

sub_bond_requirement.x-reference-facts: NRS 339.025 (not NRS 338): public-works contracts over $100,000 (other than NDOT chapter 408 work) need a performance bond and a payment bond, each at least 50 percent of the contract, and the contracting body may set more; on State Public Works Division contracts each sub whose work exceeds $50,000 or 1 percent of the project, whichever is greater, must furnish a bond to the Division in an amount it sets (NRS 339.025(2)). NRS 338.141(5)(b)(3): a listed sub that cannot furnish P&P bonds may lawfully be substituted. AIA A701-2018 sec. 7.1.4 and 7.2.2: P&P bonds default to 100 percent of the contract sum on AIA A312 unless the bidding documents state otherwise (fact-checked 2026-09-23).

bonding_capacity_check.description: For each GC, a computed comparison of what this bid would commit against G3's surety program: the bid bond amount, the performance and payment penal sum as stated (or, when a bond form is named with no amount, the form default as a labeled reference), any State Public Works Division sub bond attached by rule, against G3's single-job limit and remaining aggregate capacity after backlog, with whether surety approval or a capacity letter is needed before bid. WHY: Teams check the bid bond but miss the penal sum: a P&P bond at 100 percent of the subcontract uses far more capacity than a 5 percent bid bond. indemnity_terms.description: Which indemnity form applies: broad (G3 covers the GC or owner even for their sole negligence), intermediate (shared fault), or comparative (only to the extent of G3's fault); when the duty to defend triggers; whether attorney fees are included; whether it reaches beyond third-party injury and property damage; any cap; and the indemnitees named. WHY: Broad-form indemnity and an immediate duty to defend make G3 insure other parties' negligence, a largely uninsurable and uncapped exposure. Nevada's anti-indemnity statute is narrow and residential only, so on commercial work the contract words decide. It is a walk-away or executive-review term unless the proposal can limit it to 'the extent caused by G3's negligence'. WHERE: Subcontract 'Indemnification' article; 00 72 00 or 00 73 00 indemnification article; GC bid instructions.

consequential_damages_waiver.title: Consequential damages waiver
consequential_damages_waiver.description: The consequential damages waiver at each contract level, read separately: owner-GC (A201 sec. 15.1.7 style) and GC-sub (A401 sec. 6.4 style or the GC's form). For each: whether it is mutual or one-sided, whether LDs are carved out, other carve-outs, and any overall cap on G3's liability in the subcontract. WHY: The GC-sub waiver need not mirror the prime. A one-sided subcontract waiver strips G3's recovery for extended overhead and lost productivity while leaving the GC free to pass through the owner's lost revenue, a large risk on resort, casino and data-center work where owner downtime dwarfs the electrical contract. A mutual waiver is a standard proposal ask. WHERE: 00 72 00 General Conditions (A201 sec. 15.1.7 style); 00 73 00; subcontract 'Waiver of Claims' or 'Limitation of Liability' article.

long_lead_early_release.title: Early release and funding for long-lead equipment

WHY: A single daytime shift on a schedule that assumes more hours changes crew-day counts directly, and a night-only requirement adds shift premium and lower productivity that must be in the labor rate. working_hours.x-extraction-notes: Times stay as written in 24-hour local time. The GC invitation or Instructions to Bidders can differ from the spec; the envelope records conflicting and the working value is the more restrictive window. working_hours.x-reference-facts: Clark County prevailing-wage book 2025-2026 (Amendment 07), Electrician Wireman and Communication Technician pages: swing shift (8 consecutive hours, 5 consecutive days, between 4:30 pm and 1:00 am) pays +15 percent; graveyard shift (8 consecutive hours, 5 consecutive days, between 12:30 am and 9:00 am) pays +30 percent; all hours on Saturday, Sunday and recognized holidays, midnight to midnight, are double time. Bids opening on or after October 1, 2026 fall under the 2026-2027 book (rates at bid opening govern, NRS 338.030), so re-check these against the new book. Premium pay on the same pages: 1.5x for the first 4 hours before or after 8 hours in a day or shift, 2x after 12 hours. Recognized holidays: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and the Friday after, Christmas.
working_hours.x-bdr-overlap: Overlaps BDR labor_time (day_work|night_work) and labor_note; the documents add the exact window and weekend and holiday rules. Flag any mismatch with labor_time.

WHY: Most Las Vegas remodels are mixed: part of the work at night at a premium and lower output, the rest on days. Pricing the whole job at one rate either loses the bid or loses money, and a continuing night shift is priced differently from a handful of weekend tie-ins. WHERE: 01 14 00 Work Restrictions, phasing sheets, electrical demolition and one-line notes, owner property rules, healthcare ICRA exhibits, pre-bid minutes, GC invitation.

Healthcare after-hours-only areas and resort gaming-floor windows are rows here. Kept separate from working_hours so a mostly-day job with night tie-ins is visible.
off_hours_work_items.x-reference-facts: Clark County prevailing-wage book 2025-2026 (Amendment 07), Electrician Wireman and Communication Technician pages: swing shift (8 consecutive hours, 5 consecutive days, between 4:30 pm and 1:00 am) pays +15 percent; graveyard shift (8 consecutive hours, 5 consecutive days, between 12:30 am and 9:00 am) pays +30 percent; all hours on Saturday, Sunday and recognized holidays, midnight to midnight, are double time. off_hours_shift_classification.description: For the base window and each off-hours row: the wage-book shift class the window falls in (day, swing, graveyard, weekend or holiday), whether the stated pattern can meet the shift-premium conditions, the rate basis (prevailing-wage book or G3's own labor agreement), and the reference-table rule that sets the premium. WHY: BDR's labor_time is only day_work or night_work, but the Clark book prices swing and graveyard differently and pays shift premiums only for 8 consecutive hours on 5 consecutive days; a sustained graveyard program and a few single-night tie-ins cost very different amounts per hour. off_hours_shift_classification.x-extraction-notes: Code fills this, not the model. A window is swing or graveyard only when it holds 8 consecutive hours inside that shift's band; meets_shift_premium_conditions is yes only when the source row's pattern is continuous_shift and the text supports 5 consecutive days, no for individual_events, otherwise not_determinable. rate_basis is clark_prevailing_wage_book when prevailing_wage_basis is state or federal (Nevada now uses one rate schedule for both), company_labor_agreement on private work. Premium percentages come from the reference table by reference_rule_id and are never written into the value. The record classifies; the estimator prices.
off_hours_shift_classification.x-reference-facts: Clark County prevailing-wage book 2025-2026 (Amendment 07), Electrician Wireman and Communication Technician pages: swing shift (8 consecutive hours, 5 consecutive days, between 4:30 pm and 1:00 am) pays +15 percent; graveyard shift (8 consecutive hours, 5 consecutive days, between 12:30 am and 9:00 am) pays +30 percent; all hours on Saturday, Sunday and recognized holidays, midnight to midnight, are double time. The energized-work policy itself is outage_shutdown_windows; this field records the permit procedure and lead time. Fire watch for fire alarm impairments is low_voltage_life_safety; fire watch here is only the hot-work kind. Who staffs a fire watch is scope_responsibility row fire_watch.

scope_responsibility.title: Who does what
scope_responsibility.description: Records who furnishes, installs, wires, terminates, programs and pays for every boundary item between electrical and the GC, other trades, the owner and the utility, from the owner documents and from each GC's own trade package, so every silent, conflicting or GC-specific item becomes a priced line, an exclusion or an RFI before bid day. It is the single owner of responsibility answers (including who carries each low-voltage system and every delegated design), and its derived fields turn those answers into exclusion candidates, lower-tier sub needs and BDR RFQ decisions.

responsibility_matrix.title: Scope responsibility matrix
responsibility_matrix.description: One row per standard item code on every project, even when the documents are silent, plus 'other' rows for any further boundary item found. Each row records whether the item exists here, the responsible party, who furnishes, installs, wires, terminates, programs and pays where those differ, where our work stops, attached conditions, any printed dollar amount and the addendum that set the answer. Rows come from the owner documents, addenda and pre-bid answers; each GC's own scope sheet is recorded against these rows in gc_trade_package_by_gc. WHY: Furnish, install and pay boundaries with the GC, site and concrete subs, Divisions 07, 09, 10, 14, 21 and 23, owner vendors and NV Energy are the most common source of unpriced scope and post-award disputes. GCs level bids against these same items and plug a number against us for anything we leave silent, and a subcontractor has lost in court over excavation that an addendum assigned to it. Answering one fixed list on every bid turns each silent or conflicting item into a priced line, an exclusion or an RFI before bid day, and the matrix is the single authority for who carries each low-voltage system. WHERE: Division 01 (01 10 00 Summary and Work by Owner, 01 21 00 Allowances, 01 41 00 Regulatory Requirements, 01 45 00 Quality Control, 01 50 00 Temporary Facilities, 01 73 00 Cutting and Patching, 01 74 00 Waste, 01 91 00 Commissioning), General and Supplementary Conditions, 26 05 00 'Work by Others' and 'Coordination' articles, 'Related Sections' and furnished-by language in Divisions 03, 07 (07 84 00 firestopping, roofing), 08 (access doors, door hardware, overhead doors), 09 90 00 (items to be painted), 10, 11, 12, 14, 21, 22, 23 (23 05 13, 23 09 00, 23 33 00, equipment schedules), 27, 28 and 31 to 33; civil, site, landscape and E-series general and keyed notes; NV Energy standard detail callouts; pre-bid RFI answers; every addendum, including answer-only addenda.

item_code.description: Standard item code, or other for a boundary item with no standard code.

item.description: Short label; for other rows, what the item is.

applies_to.description: Area, building, phase, trench segment or equipment tag this row covers; null when project-wide.

applicable.description: Whether the item exists on this project.

responsible_party.description: Party the owner documents, addenda or pre-bid answers make responsible for the item.

other_trade.description: Named trade or division when a party is other_trade (for example Div 23 controls, site civil sub, foodservice contractor, sign vendor).

furnish_by.description: Who furnishes, only when it differs from responsible_party; else null.

install_by.description: Who installs or sets, only when it differs from responsible_party; else null.

wire_by.description: Who provides raceway and wiring, only when it differs; else null.

terminate_by.description: Who makes final terminations, only when it differs; else null.

program_by.description: Who programs or commissions the device or system, only when it differs; else null.

pay_by.description: Who pays (fees, energy, rentals, agency costs), only when it differs; else null.

boundary_detail.description: Where our work stops, as the documents describe it (for example conduit and pull string to 5 ft outside the building).

conditions.description: Conditions attached to the assignment (UL system submittals for firestopping, roofer-of-record rule, escort required).

stated_amount.description: Dollar amount printed for this item (allowance, fee), never estimated.

set_by_addendum.description: Addendum number that set or last changed this row; null when the base documents govern.

inferred_rule.description: Name of the rule when the row is inferred rather than stated (for example nve_standard_detail_callout); null when stated.

doc_role.description: Kind of document taking this position.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

conflict_positions.description: Every current position when responsible_party is conflicting; empty otherwise.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

anyOf.description: One row per standard item code (plus other rows), repeated with applies_to when the answer differs by area or equipment.

responsibility_matrix.x-extraction-notes: Fill one routed section, sheet set or addendum at a time: each returns only the rows it addresses (item_code, party values, cite). Code merges rows by item_code and applies_to, sets responsible_party=conflicting with conflict_positions when current sources disagree, and adds a not_stated row for every standard code no routed location addressed (the envelope searched list proves it). Never fill a habitual default. Record ec only when the text of Divisions 26 to 28, an addendum or a pre-bid answer assigns the work to electrical: 'Contractor' in Division 01 usually means the GC, 'provide' means furnish and install, and 'install' used loosely is flagged in furnish_install_language_map. Fill furnish_by, install_by, wire_by, terminate_by, program_by and pay_by only when they differ from responsible_party. Set applicable=no and responsible_party=not_applicable when the item does not exist (no kitchen, no generator), with a cite or a computed reason. Repeat an item_code with applies_to when the answer differs by area, building, phase, segment or equipment (utility trench by the site sub, site-lighting trench by EC). inferred_rule is set only for a named rule; today the one standing rule is nve_standard_detail_callout: a drawing callout of an NV Energy standard detail supports customer (not utility) responsibility for trench, conduit and risers, pads, vaults and boxes (see utility_point_of_demarcation reference facts), but never says which customer-side trade does the work, which stays not_stated unless the documents say. Scan every addendum sentence for 'responsible for' or 'shall include' next to a trade name and record the addendum in set_by_addendum. stated_amount only when a dollar figure is printed. Summary rows must agree with their detail fields (validator): starters_vfds with starter_vfd_split_by_tag, ofci_receive_store_install with owner_furnished_equipment, delegated_design with delegated_design_items, the utility rows with utility_point_of_demarcation. Low-voltage rows are the authority for who carries each system; A5 systems_inventory.scope_model is a summary a validator checks against them. Mapping from the A5 system list: structured_cabling and wireless_lan to structured_cabling; fire_alarm and a combined mass_notification to fire_alarm; access_control, intrusion_detection and intercom_entry to access_control_intrusion; video_surveillance; audio_visual to av_systems; errcs_bda; cellular_das; nurse_call; area_of_refuge_two_way and emergency_call_stations to two_way_emergency_communication; paging_sound and master_clock to paging_intercom_sound_clock; anything else (catv_iptv, rtls, standalone mass notification) is an other row naming the system. This field records WHO only: requirements stay with their owners (temp power detail in temp_power_requirements; testing, Cx, BIM, badging, escorts and site logistics in A3; NV Energy facility specs, duct bank and backfill specs in A4; system content in A5). GC scope-sheet adds and removes go to gc_trade_package_by_gc, not here. Badging, parking and site access rules are project-document items only: do not assume a statewide or county rule or a processing lead time. Standard codes by group. temporary_facilities: temp_power_distribution (temp service, panels, spider boxes, GFCI and upkeep for all trades; applies_to per phase when it differs), temp_lighting (task and egress lighting for all trades), temp_power_energy_bill, temp_power_during_outages (temporary generators or feeds that keep occupied or existing areas live during shutdowns), dumpsters_debris_removal, lifts_and_access_equipment (shared vs self-provided lifts and scaffolds), crane_hoisting_rigging (setting gear, generators, transformers, rooftop equipment), storage_and_laydown (secure containers, gear storage, off-site storage), parking_and_site_access_costs (crew parking, shuttles, badging, background checks and escort charges), fire_watch (while fire alarm is impaired), infection_control_barriers (ICRA barriers, HEPA and negative-air units around electrical work), traffic_control_barricades (incl. trench plates in drives or right-of-way), dust_control_permit_and_measures (permit holder, water truck and track-out for electrical trenching), survey_layout_staking. site_civil: trenching_excavation (incl. boring; applies_to by segment), rock_caliche_excavation, utility_locating_potholing, backfill_compaction (incl. imported bedding sand), compaction_testing, sawcut_paving_patch (exterior asphalt or concrete cut, removal and patch), duct_bank_concrete (encasement concrete and rebar), equipment_pads (gear, generator, transformer and housekeeping pads), light_pole_bases (excavation, forms, rebar, anchor bolts, concrete), protective_bollards (bollards guarding gear, transformers, generators, EV chargers), offsite_streetlights_traffic_signals (public right-of-way streetlights, traffic signal work and offsite conduit built to agency standards). building_construction: core_drilling, slab_scanning (GPR or x-ray before coring or cutting), slab_sawcut_trench_patch (interior slab on grade), cutting_patching (existing construction incl. finish patch and paint match), firestopping (UL system submittal needs in conditions), roof_penetrations_flashing (roofer-of-record warranty rules in conditions), access_panels (furnish vs install vs locate), painting (exposed conduit, boxes, panels and gear per Div 09 items to be painted), blocking_backing, demo_make_safe (disconnect and make safe for others' demolition; electrical demolition and disposal), hazmat_abatement_and_disposal (asbestos or lead abatement, PCB ballasts, lamp recycling). trade_interfaces: div23_controls_line_voltage, div23_controls_low_voltage (incl. BAS conduit), starters_vfds (project default; per tag in starter_vfd_split_by_tag), mech_equipment_disconnects, fire_smoke_dampers (power and FA interface; 24V vs 120V actuators usually decide it), duct_smoke_detectors (furnish, mount in duct, wire), sprinkler_flow_tamper_monitoring, fire_pump_power_and_controller (incl. controller and transfer switch), elevator_shunt_trip_recall (EC power and wiring vs FA relay or module vs elevator controller terminations, each in boundary_detail), elevator_equipment_power (mainline and cab disconnects, pit and machine room lights and receptacles), kitchen_equipment_connections (final connections vs foodservice contractor), hood_suppression_interlock, electrified_door_hardware (locks, power transfer, operators), overhead_doors_gates_dock_equipment (coiling and sectional doors, gate operators, dock levelers: power, controls, interlocks), motorized_shades_screens_partitions (motorized shades, projection screens, operable partitions), systems_furniture_power (base feeds, whips and poles vs furniture vendor), signage_power_connections (pylon, monument, marquee, building and wayfinding signs: circuits, boxes and controllers vs sign vendor), landscape_lighting_and_irrigation_power (landscape and water-feature lighting, irrigation controller power), ev_chargers (EVSE units vs make-ready), pv_bess (arrays, inverters, storage; the utility interconnection application as its own applies_to row), lightning_protection, gaming_equipment_connections (slot bases, table games). utility: utility_service_application (application, load letters, NV Energy coordination), utility_trench_conduit, utility_transformer_pad_vaults (pads, vaults, enclosures, handholes and boxes), service_transformer (utility-owned vs customer-furnished, for example on primary services), utility_service_conductors (conductors or bus from the utility transformer or vault to the service equipment: furnish, pull, terminate), utility_fees_charges (line extension, design fees, deposits, outage and reconnect fees), utility_relocation_undergrounding (relocating or undergrounding existing lines and poles), telecom_carrier_entrance (entrance conduit, carrier coordination, demarc extension). permits_fees: permit_electrical (incl. plan check), permit_fire_alarm, permit_low_voltage, permit_row_encroachment (offsite trenching). testing_design: special_inspections, neta_acceptance_testing (incl. infrared scans), retest_costs (who pays;
