split rows when the contractor collects data and the engineer runs the study), mv_third_party_review_inspection (who hires and pays third-party peer review and inspection of 1000V-and-over systems when A4 southern_nevada_amendment_triggers shows 110.30 triggered), delegated_design. low_voltage_life_safety: fire_alarm (design, devices, panel, wiring, programming; rough-in-only splits in boundary_detail), fire_alarm_monitoring, lv_primary_pathway (tray, sleeves, conduit through rated assemblies), lv_device_rough_in (backboxes, stub-ups, J-hooks), structured_cabling (incl. the telecom bonding backbone as an applies_to row when Div 26 and 27 split it), access_control_intrusion, video_surveillance (cameras, licenses and PoE switches in boundary_detail), av_systems, errcs_bda, cellular_das, nurse_call, two_way_emergency_communication, paging_intercom_sound_clock. generator: generator_furnish_install, generator_fuel_and_initial_fill, generator_fuel_piping (piping, vents and fills to a remote tank; gas piping), generator_startup_load_bank (factory startup and load bank rental), generator_air_permit (Clark County DAQ air permit and fire-code fuel storage permit). owner_furnished: ofci_receive_store_install.
responsibility_matrix.x-reference-facts: NV Energy Rule 9 (South) A.12: the applicant provides trenching, backfill, conduits and risers, transformer pads, vaults, enclosures and boxes at no cost to NVE (full rule in utility_point_of_demarcation). NAC 477.300: fire alarm installers need a State Fire Marshal firm license and worker certificates of registration in addition to the NSCB license (applies to the permit_fire_alarm and fire_alarm rows). Clark County Fire guideline 105.7.16 (ERRCS): permit plans must show the contractor's license number, classification and monetary limit. Clark County AQR 94.10: the site superintendent and the foremen of every on-site contractor and subcontractor must complete the Dust Control Class at least once every 3 years.
responsibility_matrix.x-bdr-overlap: Partial. BDR's vendor RFQ categories (Switchgear, Generator & Equipment, Low Voltage, saw-cut and trench markups), pricing sections (underground, low_voltage) and go/no-go answers (subs_needed, scope_fit) assume what is ours but store no per-item who-provides; bid_notes may hold GC scope text as free text only.

scope_of_work_narrative.title: Electrical scope-of-work summary
scope_of_work_narrative.description: A short summary of the electrical scope the owner documents define: about 120 words of plain text, the core-and-shell versus tenant-improvement boundary when there is one, and one row per major scope area marked in scope, rough-in or pathway only, install only, by others or NIC, alternate only, not in the project, not stated or conflicting. It reflects the owner documents and addenda; each GC's changes to it live in gc_trade_package_by_gc. WHY: It is the one-screen answer to 'what are we bidding' and the first defense against a scope gap: the invitation may say 'power and lighting' while the spec also carries temp power, fire alarm or site underground. Checking it against BDR's vendor RFQ categories and pricing sections before pricing prevents both unpriced scope and pricing work that is not ours, and it lets $/SF and win rate be compared on like-for-like scope. WHERE: Division 01 Summary of Work (01 10 00 / 01 11 00) and Work by Owner, 26 00 00 and 26 05 00 scope articles, Division 27 and 28 scope articles, drawing sheet index by discipline, E-series general notes, bid form, addenda.

summary.description: About 120 words of plain text built only from the scope_areas rows.

shell_ti_boundary.description: Where core and shell work ends and tenant-improvement work begins, as written; null when not a shell/TI split.

applies_to.description: Building, phase or area when the status differs within the project; null when project-wide.

status.description: What the owner documents make of this area for the electrical bid.

matrix_item_codes.description: responsibility_matrix item codes that decide this status, when any.

note.description: One line on the basis (for example FA by owner's separate FA contractor, pathway only).

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

scope_areas.description: One row per scope area found in the documents; areas absent from the project may be omitted or marked not_in_project.

anyOf.description: Owner-document view of the electrical scope.

scope_of_work_narrative.x-extraction-notes: Fill scope_areas first, section by section; write the summary last and only from the rows. Status meanings: in_scope (we furnish and install), rough_in_or_pathway_only (boxes, conduit, sleeves or pathway only), install_only (others furnish), by_others_or_nic, alternate_only (the area appears only in an alternate; A1 bid_submission.alternates holds the alternate), not_in_project, not_stated (the area exists but no document says whose it is), conflicting (current documents disagree; the matching matrix row or A7 document_conflicts entry holds both positions). Each area's status must agree with the matrix rows in matrix_item_codes and, for low-voltage areas, with the matrix low-voltage rows (validator). Invitation-versus-documents disagreements are not stored here: GC scope sheets go to gc_trade_package_by_gc and other invitation conflicts to A7 document_conflicts (conflict_type invitation_vs_documents). Use applies_to for building, phase or area splits (core and shell vs TI, Building A vs B). A7 bid_brief.brief_summary may quote this summary but does not restate it.
scope_of_work_narrative.x-bdr-overlap: Overlaps BDR's vendor RFQ categories, pricing sections (materials, gear, underground, low_voltage), go/no-go scope_fit and file categories by discipline; this adds a document-backed status per scope area.

gc_trade_package_by_gc.title: Trade package scope by GC
gc_trade_package_by_gc.description: For each GC inviting us: the trade package name or number, whether a scope exhibit or scope sheet is attached, and each item that GC's package adds to electrical, removes from electrical or splits differently from the owner documents (a GC adds temp power and equipment pads, or carves fire alarm out to a separate package), keyed to responsibility_matrix item codes. This is the only home for GC scope-sheet differences. WHY: Different GCs split the same project differently and their scope exhibit usually becomes the subcontract scope. Sending one number to every GC when one includes fire alarm or pads and another does not either loses the low number or leaves scope unpriced, so each per-GC proposal has to match that GC's package. WHERE: GC invitation email or portal message, attached scope-of-work exhibit or trade package description, GC bid form or leveling sheet, GC pre-bid clarifications and addenda to subs.

gc_name.description: GC company name as written in the invitation.

trade_package.description: Trade package name or number the GC uses (for example 26-00 Electrical, BP-16).

scope_exhibit.description: Whether the GC's scope exhibit or scope sheet is in hand.

exhibit_title.description: Title and date of the scope exhibit as written.

item.description: Item as the GC describes it.

change.description: How the GC package differs from the owner-document answer.

gc_assigns_to.description: Party the GC package assigns the item to.

detail.description: Boundary or condition the GC states (for example pads by EC, rebar by GC).

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

deltas.description: Only differences from responsibility_matrix; empty when the GC's sheet matches the owner documents.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

anyOf.description: One row per GC inviting G3.

gc_trade_package_by_gc.x-extraction-notes: One row per GC on the project, read from that GC's invitation, portal message and attachments (cited by sender and date). Record only differences from the owner-document answer in responsibility_matrix; an empty deltas list with scope_exhibit=provided means the GC's sheet matches the owner documents. When the owner documents are silent (matrix row not_stated) and a GC's sheet assigns the item, record adds_to_electrical or changes_split with gc_assigns_to. Use scope_exhibit=none when the invitation only says 'electrical'. Submission and commercial instructions (forms, required breakdowns, bonds, clean-bid rules, cutoff) belong to A1 bid_submission.gc_instruction_deltas, and alternates a GC asks subs to price belong to A1. The effective scope for each GC's proposal is the matrix answer overlaid with that GC's deltas, computed in default_exclusions_and_clarifications.
gc_trade_package_by_gc.x-bdr-overlap: Joins to BDR's list of GCs bidding, per-GC proposal amounts and GC bid contacts; BDR bid_notes holds GC instructions only as free text.

furnish_install_language_map.title: Furnish, install and by-others language map
furnish_install_language_map.description: Every place in the drawings, the whole spec book and the addenda where a responsibility term ties a specific item to a party: furnish, install, furnish and install, provide (outside Division 26 or naming a trade), by others, NIC, by owner, by utility, by a named trade, OFCI, OFOI, CFCI, CFOI, future (provisions only) and 'responsible for'. Each hit gives the item, the literal term, the furnishing and installing party it implies, whether the reading is ambiguous, and the matrix item code it supports. WHY: These words are where scope gaps start, and GC bid leveling checks every sub's furnish and install treatment against them. The list is the evidence behind each matrix row and catches items two divisions both claim or both omit, where a single miss can be a five-figure gap. WHERE: General notes, keyed notes and equipment schedules on all disciplines (E, M, P, FP, A, C, L); Part 1 'Work by Others', 'Related Sections', 'Coordination' and 'Furnished by / Installed by' articles across Divisions 01, 08, 10, 11, 12, 14, 21, 22, 23, 26, 27, 28 and 31 to 33; Division 01 Summary 'Work by Owner'; addenda and pre-bid answers.

item.description: The item the term is tied to, as written.

furnish_party.description: Party the term makes furnish the item.

install_party.description: Party the term makes install the item.

applies_to.description: Area, building, sheet area or equipment tag the note covers; null when general.

ambiguous.description: True when the reading is uncertain ('install' possibly meaning furnish and install, Division 01 'Contractor', 'by others' with no party).

ambiguity_note.description: Why it is ambiguous and which readings are possible; null when not ambiguous.

matrix_item_code.description: responsibility_matrix item code this hit supports, or other.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

anyOf.description: One row per responsibility-term hit.

furnish_install_language_map.x-extraction-notes: Hunt the entire document set one section or sheet at a time; keyed notes are identified by sheet and note number in the citation. Record the literal term and do not resolve ambiguity silently (some designers write 'install' meaning furnish and install; Division 01 'Contractor' usually means the GC). A plain 'provide' on an E-sheet with no party named is our default scope and is not a hit. Notes that add cost without a responsibility term (verify in field, coordinate with, test, demolish or relocate, 'provide new 200A panel here') belong to A7 document_control.scope_bearing_notes, which no longer records furnish or install obligations. Whether a hit sits outside Divisions 26 to 28 is derived by code from the citation. Every hit that assigns work must be reflected in a responsibility_matrix row (validator); hits with no standard code create other rows. future_provisions_only records items shown for the future (conduit and box for a future charger) so the item itself is not priced.

owner_furnished_equipment.title: Owner-furnished and other-furnished equipment
owner_furnished_equipment.description: Every item furnished by the owner, an owner vendor, the GC or another trade that electrical must receive, set, connect or rough in for: procurement model (OFCI, owner-furnished and owner-installed with our connection, owner pre-purchased gear assigned to us, other-trade or GC furnished and EC installed), tag and quantity as printed, who receives and stores it, who sets it, who connects it, the connection type, delivery or lead-time notes, and the incidental material that stays ours (whips, disconnects, terminations). WHY: OFCI removes our equipment markup but leaves labor, incidentals and storage or damage risk with us, and owner pre-purchased switchgear or generators assigned to us hand us vendor and lead-time risk without the margin. Missing an item leaves labor unpriced; reading one as ours prices equipment we will never supply and can lose the bid. WHERE: Division 01 Summary 'Owner-Furnished Products' (01 10 00, 01 64 00), OFCI schedule or appendix, equipment schedules marked N.I.C., OFCI, 'by owner' or 'by vendor', Division 26 to 28 Parts 1 and 2, foodservice, gaming and signage schedules, GC invitation, addenda.

tag.description: Equipment tag or schedule mark; null when none.

quantity.description: Quantity only as printed; null when not printed.

procurement_model.description: How the item is procured and what electrical does with it.

furnished_by_name.description: Named vendor, trade or division when stated.

receive_store_by.description: Who receives, unloads and stores it.

set_by.description: Who sets or mounts it in place.

ec_incidentals.description: Incidental material that stays ours (whips, disconnects, lugs, terminations).

delivery_note.description: Delivery date, lead time or release note as written.

applies_to.description: Building, area or phase when relevant.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

anyOf.description: One row per owner-furnished or other-furnished item.

owner_furnished_equipment.x-extraction-notes: OFCI items are often listed once in the Division 01 Summary or an OFCI appendix and never repeated in Division 26, and 'N.I.C.' on E-sheets often points to a schedule elsewhere. Re-check every addendum, since owners move gear to direct purchase late for lead time. quantity only as printed. Return an empty list when no owner-furnished article or schedule exists, with the envelope searched list. This is the single home for owner-furnished items; the matrix row ofci_receive_store_install summarizes it (validator). Owner-direct low-voltage systems that need only our pathway stay in the matrix low-voltage rows unless they also need our power connection. Electrical data (HP, FLA, voltage) stays in A4 power_distribution.equipment_connection_schedule; join on tag. On Nevada public works an owner-furnished materials arrangement is restricted (reference facts); when one appears, check A1 labor_and_compliance.sales_use_tax.
owner_furnished_equipment.x-reference-facts: NRS 338.1423: Nevada public bodies generally may not use owner-furnished material arrangements on public works unless the contract requires payment of the taxes that would otherwise be due; never assume tax-exempt owner-furnished materials on a Nevada public job.
owner_furnished_equipment.x-bdr-overlap: None stored; decides whether BDR's Switchgear and Generator & Equipment RFQs go out for furnish-and-install or install only.

starter_vfd_split_by_tag.title: Starter and VFD split by equipment tag
starter_vfd_split_by_tag.description: For each mechanical or plumbing equipment tag with a starter, VFD or disconnect: who furnishes and mounts it, who wires the line side, load side and controls, what Division 22/23 says, what Division 26 says, and whether they agree, both claim it, both stay silent or disagree. WHY: VFDs and starters are often bought with the mechanical unit but mounted and wired by electrical, and the split often varies unit to unit on the same job. Each division commonly assumes the other furnishes them, a classic Div 23/26 gap that moves tens of thousands of dollars of equipment and labor between trades. WHERE: Mechanical and plumbing equipment schedules (furnished-by and remarks columns), electrical equipment connection schedule, 23 05 13 and 23 29 23, 26 29 13 and 26 29 23 Part 1, one-line diagram, M/E coordination notes, addenda.

load_side_wiring_by.description: Who wires the load side to the motor.

control_wiring_by.description: Who provides control and interlock wiring.

div23_position.description: Short paraphrase of what Division 22/23 or the mechanical schedule says; null when silent.

div26_position.description: Short paraphrase of what Division 26 or the electrical schedule says; null when silent.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

anyOf.description: One row per equipment tag and device.

starter_vfd_split_by_tag.x-extraction-notes: One row per tag and device, never one blanket answer. Read the mechanical schedules, 23 05 13 and 23 29 23, and 26 29 13 and 26 29 23 separately and record each division's position as a short paraphrase in div23_position and div26_position (quotes live in the citations). both_claim, both_silent and disagree rows become RFIs through default_exclusions_and_clarifications; never pick a side. Electrical data (HP, FLA, voltage, phase, VFD options) stays in A4 power_distribution.equipment_connection_schedule; join on equipment_tag. The matrix row starters_vfds holds the project default and must agree (validator).

temp_power_requirements.title: Temporary power requirements
temp_power_requirements.description: What the documents require of construction power and lighting where it touches electrical: temp service size and voltage as written, distribution for other trades (spider boxes, GFCI, cord reach), lighting levels, duration and hours of upkeep, whether an allowance carries it, the standards cited, removal, and whether permanent equipment may be energized for construction use and on what conditions. WHY: Temp power is often a one-line obligation that becomes rental gear, months of upkeep and back-charges on a larger job. Sizing it from 'provide temp power' alone risks an upsize mid-project, and early construction use of permanent gear can add cleaning, replacement and warranty exposure. WHERE: 01 50 00 Temporary Facilities and Controls Parts 1 and 2 ('Electric Power Service', 'Lighting'), 01 21 00 Allowances, 26 05 00 temporary power article, general notes, phasing and demolition notes, GC invitation.

temp_service_size.description: Temp service size and voltage exactly as written.

distribution_requirements.description: Distribution for other trades as written (spider boxes, GFCI, maximum cord reach, outlets per floor).

lighting_level.description: Temporary lighting level as written (for example 5 footcandles in work areas).

duration.description: How long temp power must be provided, when stated as a length of time.

duration_text.description: Duration or end point as written when it is a milestone (for example until permanent power is energized).

maintenance_hours.description: Hours temp power must be attended or maintained, as written.

allowance_funded.description: Whether temp power is carried by an allowance (amount lives in A1 allowances).

standards_cited.description: Standards cited exactly as printed (NEC Article 590, OSHA 1926 Subpart K, a NECA standard).

removal_required.description: Whether the temporary system must be removed by the provider.

permanent_equipment_use.description: Whether permanent equipment may be energized for construction use.

permanent_use_conditions.description: Conditions on construction use of permanent equipment (cleaning, filter or lamp replacement, owner approval).

anyOf.description: Requirement detail for construction power and lighting.

temp_power_requirements.x-extraction-notes: Who provides temp power and temp lighting, who pays the energy bill and who covers outages are responsibility_matrix rows; this field holds the requirement detail. It often lives only in 01 50 00; still capture drawing notes that point there. Record sizes, levels and durations exactly as written; use duration only for a stated length of time and duration_text for a milestone end point. Record cited standards exactly as printed and never supply a standard number the text does not print. Allowance amounts live in A1 bid_submission.allowances; here only whether temp power is allowance-funded. Warranty-start effects of early permanent-equipment use stay with A2.

utility_point_of_demarcation.title: Utility point of demarcation
utility_point_of_demarcation.description: For each utility service: where the serving utility's work ends and customer-side work begins, stated as the physical point of delivery (transformer secondary terminals, vault bus, weatherhead), the service arrangement that governs the split (padmount, vault or equipment room, overhead drop, primary service), who furnishes the service conductors, the items the documents say the utility furnishes or installs, the utility standard details cited, and whether the utility's layout drawing is in the package. WHY: Misreading the boundary either prices utility-side work that is not ours or misses the customer-side trench, conduit, pads, vaults and service conductors NV Energy expects the customer to provide at its own cost. Service conductors alone are a large line on a big service, and the boundary is where the utility lead-time chain starts, which drives the energization date our startup and testing pricing assumes. WHERE: One-line diagram utility interface notes, site electrical and civil utility plans, NV Energy layout drawing or will-serve letter when included, NV Energy standard details reproduced or cited on the drawings (RS and RE series), 26 05 00 and 26 27 13 service and metering articles, addenda.

applies_to.description: Service or building this row covers; null when the project has one service.

service_arrangement.description: Utility service arrangement that governs the split.

point_of_delivery.description: Physical point of delivery as written (NVE transformer secondary terminals, vault bus, weatherhead).

service_conductors_furnished_by.description: Who furnishes the service conductors or bus from the utility equipment to the service equipment.

utility_furnishes.description: Items the documents say the utility furnishes or installs.

utility_standards_cited.description: Utility standard details or rules cited (for example NVE RS-19, RE-4), as written.

utility_layout_drawing.description: Whether the utility's layout or design drawing is in the package.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

anyOf.description: One row per utility service.

utility_point_of_demarcation.x-extraction-notes: One row per service (applies_to names the service or building). Record the point of delivery as written; when the drawings give none, leave it null with a verify_action to obtain the NV Energy layout drawing. Recognize bare callouts such as 'per NVE RS-19' as utility standards. service_conductors_furnished_by records what the documents say; when they are silent, inferred status is allowed only when a commercial padmount or vault service is shown and cited, under the rule nve_commercial_customer_owned_service_cables (RE-4 15.2, RS-19 note), with a check_reference verify action; line-extension and overhead services stay not_stated. Never infer that utility-side items are ours. Who applies for service, who builds the customer-side trench, conduit and pads, who pulls the service conductors and who pays utility fees are matrix utility rows that must agree with this field (validator). What the customer facilities must be (pad specs, conduit counts, pre-backfill inspection, lead time) is A4 power_distribution.nv_energy_service_requirements; serving utility, voltage, amperage and overhead vs underground are A4 power_distribution.service_entrance, and service_arrangement must agree with it.
utility_point_of_demarcation.x-reference-facts: NV Energy Rule 9 (South) A.12: the applicant provides, at no cost to NVE, trenching, excavation, backfill, pavement removal and repaving, conduits and risers, transformer pads, vaults, enclosures and boxes; these become NVE property after inspection and acceptance. NVE ESR RT-G: on commercial work the applicant furnishes and installs the ducts (on residential NVE furnishes ducts and the applicant installs them); the applicant also furnishes and installs pads, handholes, pull boxes, manholes or vaults and grounding; NVE furnishes and installs transformers, cable, cabinets, switches, pole risers and connections, and sets the meter. Service conductors depend on the service type: commercial padmount and vault services in the Southern Nevada ESR use customer-owned service cables that NVE terminates on the transformer (RE-4 15.2, RS-19 note), while Rule 9 A.8 treats line-extension service conductors as utility-furnished at the applicant's cost; the NVE layout drawing sets the point of delivery. On overhead service drops NVE owns and installs the conductors to the point of attachment and the customer provides the service insulator or periscope.
utility_point_of_demarcation.x-bdr-overlap: None; feeds BDR's underground pricing section and trench markup.

delegated_design_items.title: Delegated design and contractor engineering
delegated_design_items.description: The single register of every system where the documents make a contractor responsible for design or engineered submittals instead of the engineer of record: the system, the design level (full delegated design, design-build, design-assist, engineered shop drawings, calculations only), which contractor it lands on, the stamp or credential the documents require, and whether the EOR's performance criteria are clear, vague or missing. WHY: Delegated design moves engineering fees, design time and liability onto us and is often hidden in a prescriptive-looking spec ('contractor shall provide complete engineered shop drawings'). A design-build fire alarm, a stamped seismic bracing design or pole foundation calculations are real money and schedule, and vague criteria produce designs that pass review but fail in the field. WHERE: Division 01 delegated design or professional certification article, Part 1 'Design Requirements', 'Delegated Design', 'Performance Requirements' or 'Quality Assurance' in 26 05 29 and 26 05 48 (supports and seismic), 26 56 00 (poles and foundations), 26 32 13 and 26 36 00 (paralleling), 26 41 00 (lightning protection), 26 31 00 (PV), 26 09 23 (lighting controls), 28 31 00 or 28 46 00 (fire alarm) and ERRCS sections; E-series and FA notes such as 'design-build by contractor'; code sheet deferred-submittal lists.

system.description: System whose design or engineering is placed on a contractor.

applies_to.description: Area, building or equipment the delegation covers; null when the whole system.

design_level.description: How much design the contractor carries.

assigned_to.description: Which contractor the documents put the design on.

credential_required.description: Stamp or credential the documents require on the design.

criteria_quality.description: Whether the EOR's performance criteria are clear, vague or missing.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

anyOf.description: Single register of delegated and contractor-engineered systems.

delegated_design_items.x-extraction-notes: Collect from every Division 26, 27 and 28 section's Part 1, not only Division 01. Treat design-assist and engineered shop drawings as real engineering effort. 'Contractor' in Division 01 is usually the GC: assigned_to=ec only when Divisions 26 to 28, an addendum or a pre-bid answer put the design on electrical. credential_required records only what the documents print; statutory credential rules (NAC 477.300 for fire alarm designers) are reference facts attached by rule and never written into a row. This is the single register: A4 power_distribution.lightning_protection design_basis, pv_and_battery_storage design_basis, seismic_restraint delegated_design_stamp_required and wiring_and_lighting.exterior_site_lighting delegated_foundation_design, and the delegated reading of A5 fire_alarm_design_basis, are read-throughs of these rows, and any delegated design found while extracting A4 or A5 must create a row here (validator). A5 keeps the technical content (riser shown on bid drawings, calculations required, NICET levels). Power system studies are the matrix row power_system_studies, not this list. The matrix row delegated_design summarizes this list and must agree.
delegated_design_items.x-reference-facts: NAC 477.300: a firm installing or servicing fire alarm or detection systems needs a State Fire Marshal license and each worker an SFM certificate of registration; a certificate holder must be on every job site and directly supervise unregistered workers; fire alarm designers must hold NICET Level II (or equivalent) or a Nevada PE license. This is in addition to the NSCB license (C-2, C-2c, or C-41/C-41c). Clark County enforces NFPA 72 as adopted and amended by the Clark County Fire Code, and the Clark County Fire Chief may require a PE wet stamp on fire alarm submittals.

cutting_patching_conditions.title: Cutting, coring and patching conditions
cutting_patching_conditions.description: Conditions attached to cutting into existing or new construction, by area when they differ: whether written owner or architect consent is required before cutting, the restoration standard (match existing, ready for finish, rough patch only), whether finish paint is part of the patch, and whether GPR or x-ray scanning is required before coring or saw-cutting. WHY: 'Match existing' restoration and paint matching cost far more than a rough patch, consent waits hit the schedule, and coring a post-tensioned slab without a scan is a major liability event. On resort and casino renovation these conditions set the price of every penetration. WHERE: General Conditions cutting and patching article (AIA A201 3.14 or the project's equivalent), 01 73 00 Execution 'Cutting and Patching', 26 05 00 penetrations article, structural general notes (post-tension warnings), owner renovation standards.

applies_to.description: Area the conditions cover (guest areas, back of house, existing building); null when project-wide.

consent_required.description: Whether written owner or architect consent is required before cutting.

finish_paint_included.description: Whether finish paint is part of the patch.

scan_required_before_coring.description: Whether GPR or x-ray scanning is required before coring or saw-cutting.

cite.description: Ids of the envelope citations that support this row.

anyOf.description: One row for the project, plus rows where conditions differ by area.

cutting_patching_conditions.x-extraction-notes: One project-wide row, plus rows with applies_to when conditions differ by area (guest areas match existing, back of house rough patch). Who cuts, cores, scans, patches and firestops are matrix rows (cutting_patching, core_drilling, slab_scanning, firestopping). Post-tensioned slab identification is A4 wiring_and_lighting.structural_constraints. Clause numbers differ between AIA, ConsensusDocs and owner forms; cite the form this project uses. Return an empty list only for ground-up work with no cutting article.

default_exclusions_and_clarifications.title: Scope exclusion and clarification candidates
default_exclusions_and_clarifications.description: A rules-based list built from the matrix, each GC's package differences, the starter and VFD split, owner-furnished items and G3's standard exclusion list: for each item that is not stated, assigned to others, conflicting, referenced but not provided, assigned to us against usual practice, or changed by a GC package, a suggested action (exclude, clarify, send an RFI, or price it and do not exclude), the reason, draft wording and the GCs it applies to. WHY: GCs read exclusions before price and treat a bid with loose exclusions as a higher number with a question mark, so a clean list matched to the documents is a competitive edge. It also stops the costly habit of excluding something the documents clearly give us (saw-cut, firestopping, temp power), which makes the bid non-conforming or leaves us holding the scope anyway. WHERE: Derived from responsibility_matrix, gc_trade_package_by_gc, starter_vfd_split_by_tag, owner_furnished_equipment and utility_point_of_demarcation, plus a team-maintained G3 standard exclusion list; not read from any document.

applies_to.description: Area, building or equipment tag when the item is split; null when project-wide.

applies_to_gcs.description: GC names this row applies to; empty means every GC.

source_refs.description: Field keys and item codes the row came from (for example responsibility_matrix:firestopping).

anyOf.description: One row per suggested exclusion, clarification, RFI or do-not-exclude flag.

default_exclusions_and_clarifications.x-extraction-notes: Compute after the matrix and gc_trade_package_by_gc; never re-read the documents. The effective answer for each GC is the matrix row overlaid with that GC's deltas. When the documents or a GC's package assign an item to EC the action is always price_do_not_exclude, never exclude. When A1 bid_submission.exclusions_qualifications_allowed says a clean bid is required, turn exclude and clarify items into rfi before the A1 RFI cutoff. A7 bid_brief.exclusions_and_qualifications_to_carry and rfis_to_send take their scope items from this list and are the versions shown on the brief. The G3 standard exclusion list and the list of items G3 expects to be by others are team configuration.
default_exclusions_and_clarifications.x-bdr-overlap: No structured equivalent; candidate input for the wording of BDR's per-GC proposals.

lower_tier_subs_needed.title: Lower-tier subs needed for our scope
lower_tier_subs_needed.description: Items the matrix (with each GC's differences) puts on electrical that G3 normally buys from a lower-tier sub, rental vendor or engineer (trenching or boring, concrete pads and pole bases, saw-cut and paving, core drilling and scanning, firestopping, crane, NETA testing, fire alarm, ERRCS, lightning protection, PV, security, PE stamps), each with the item codes that trigger it, the license classes the sub must hold from the reference table, and the team's check of the licenses on the quotes received. WHY: Tells the team on day one which sub quotes to chase so they arrive before bid day, supplies evidence for BDR's go/no-go subs_needed answer, and keeps G3 compliant: Nevada makes G3 confirm that every lower-tier bidder whose quote it considers is properly licensed, with no small-job exception for electrical work. WHERE: Derived from responsibility_matrix, gc_trade_package_by_gc and delegated_design_items using a team-maintained self-perform list and a maintained license reference table; license_check is a team entry.

sub_trade.description: Lower-tier trade, rental vendor or engineer G3 must buy.

item_codes.description: responsibility_matrix or delegated_design_items entries that trigger it.

applies_to.description: Area or GC when the need is limited to one; null otherwise.

required_license_classes.description: License classes the sub must hold, attached by rule from the maintained reference table (NSCB classifications, State Fire Marshal license); never model-generated.

license_check.description: Team entry: whether the licenses of the subs whose quotes G3 is considering were checked; null until entered.

note.description: One line of context (for example directional bore under the drive only).

anyOf.description: One row per lower-tier trade needed.

lower_tier_subs_needed.x-extraction-notes: Include only items whose effective responsible_party, furnish_by or install_by is ec and that are on the team's buy-out list (the self-perform list is team configuration, not extraction). required_license_classes comes from a maintained reference table keyed by sub_trade (NSCB classifications, plus the State Fire Marshal license for fire alarm), never from the model. license_check is a team entry, null until someone records it; the per-vendor license number and check date belong with the vendor record in BDR. Delegated design rows add engineering_pe.
lower_tier_subs_needed.x-reference-facts: NAC 624.640(6): a licensee must confirm that anyone whose bid it considers is appropriately licensed. NRS 624.220(4)(b): the under-$1,000 incidental-work exception cannot be used for electrical work. NRS 624.700: bidding or contracting in Nevada without an active license is unlawful and such a bid is void. NAC 477.300: fire alarm installers need a State Fire Marshal firm license and worker certificates of registration in addition to the NSCB license.
lower_tier_subs_needed.x-bdr-overlap: Supplies evidence for BDR's go/no-go subs_needed answer; license data would live on BDR vendor contact records.

rfq_category_implications.title: Vendor RFQ and pricing-section impact
rfq_category_implications.description: For each BDR vendor RFQ category and the saw-cut and trench markups: whether this project needs it given the responsibility answers (an owner-furnished generator means install only and no Generator & Equipment RFQ; fire alarm by a separate FA sub comes out of the Low Voltage RFQ; EC trenching means the trench markup applies), with the item codes that drive it. WHY: Sending RFQs for equipment we will not furnish wastes vendor goodwill and estimator time, and missing one for scope that is ours leaves a hole in the number. Tying RFQs to the responsibility answers keeps the price and the scope the same thing. WHERE: Derived from responsibility_matrix, gc_trade_package_by_gc, owner_furnished_equipment and scope_of_work_narrative.

rfq_category.description: BDR vendor RFQ category or markup.

needed.description: Whether the project needs this RFQ or markup given the responsibility answers.

scope_note.description: What is in or out (for example install only, owner-furnished generator; FA by separate sub); names the GC when packages differ.

driven_by_item_codes.description: Item codes or owner_furnished_equipment tags that drive the answer.

anyOf.description: One row per RFQ category, every time.

rfq_category_implications.x-extraction-notes: One row per RFQ category every time. partial means some items in the category are ours and some are furnished by others; list them in scope_note. When GC packages differ, answer for the broadest package and name the GCs in scope_note. Substitution and sole-source limits per RFQ category are A4 specified_products.sourcing_restriction_by_rfq_category, not this field.
rfq_category_implications.x-bdr-overlap: Maps directly onto BDR's vendor RFQ categories (General Material, Switchgear, Generator & Equipment, Lighting, Low Voltage, saw-cut and trench markups) and pricing sections (materials, gear, underground, low_voltage).

scope_clarity_metrics.title: Scope clarity score
scope_clarity_metrics.description: Counts from the matrix and GC packages: standard rows, rows answered, inferred rows, not_stated rows, conflicting rows, rows changed by addendum, items assigned to electrical that are usually by others, and the number of GC package differences. WHY: A quick signal of how much contingency and RFI effort a bid needs; over time it shows which architects, EORs and GCs produce ambiguous scope, which belongs in the go/no-go conversation. WHERE: Derived from responsibility_matrix and gc_trade_package_by_gc.

standard_rows.description: Number of standard item codes evaluated.

answered_rows.description: Rows with a stated or inferred party.

inferred_rows.description: Rows answered by a named inference rule.

not_stated_rows.description: Rows where the item exists or may exist and no document assigns it.

addendum_changed_rows.description: Rows set or changed by an addendum.

ec_nonstandard_rows.description: Rows assigned to electrical that the team list says are usually by others.

gc_package_delta_count.description: Total deltas across all GC trade packages.

anyOf.description: Counts computed from responsibility_matrix and gc_trade_package_by_gc.

scope_clarity_metrics.x-extraction-notes: Computed by code, never extracted. ec_nonstandard_rows compares against the team-maintained list of items G3 expects to be by others.

power_distribution.title: Power distribution and site electrical
power_distribution.description: Captures the service and NV Energy customer-side facilities, gear, panels, feeders and transformers, standby and emergency power, studies, site, subsurface and off-site electrical, equipment connections, demolition, long-lead items and the Southern Nevada amendment checks: the inputs to the Switchgear, Generator & Equipment, Trenching and underground numbers.

service_entrance.title: Electrical service entrance
service_entrance.description: One row per electrical service to the project: the building or area it feeds, new, upgrade or existing to remain, utility secondary or customer-owned medium-voltage primary, voltage, phase and wires, main amps and main device, overhead or underground entry, serving utility, future capacity noted, and the load calculation figures when the set prints them (method, connected kVA, demand kVA, calculated amps). WHY: Service size and voltage set the gear class, feeder sizes and lead-time bracket for the largest cost block in the bid, and they are the cleanest cross-project comparable (price per service amp, price per SF by service size). A service sized far off its printed demand, or no load calculation at all, is a design flag worth an RFI before gear pricing is locked. WHERE: One-line or riser diagram (E-5xx / E-6xx), service gear elevation, load calculation sheet or table (often E-001 or on the one-line), electrical site plan, utility coordination notes, 26 24 13; the utility name is sometimes only on civil utility sheets.

service_tag.description: Service designation as printed (e.g., 'Service A', 'MSB-1'); null if unnamed.

applies_to.description: Building, area or phase this service feeds.

status.description: New service, upgrade of an existing service, or existing service left in place.

service_type.description: Utility secondary service or customer-owned medium-voltage primary service.

voltage.description: Normalized service voltage; same enum as quantities_rollup.service_size.

voltage_text.description: Voltage, phase and wires exactly as printed (e.g., '480Y/277V 3PH 4W', '12.47kV').

main_amps.description: Main device or bus rating in amps as printed.

utility_name_if_other.description: Utility name when not NV Energy (e.g., Valley Electric Association, Overton Power District).

load_calculation.description: Load calculation figures for this service exactly as printed; null when the set has no load calculation.

method_text.description: Calculation method or basis as printed (e.g., 'NEC 220 standard method').

connected_kva.description: Connected load in kVA as printed.

demand_kva.description: Demand load in kVA as printed.

future_capacity_text.description: Future capacity, spare ampacity or future service provisions as written.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

service_entrance.x-extraction-notes: One row per service; a campus with two NV Energy services gets two rows. Record load calculation figures exactly as printed and never recompute demand factors; when the set has no load calculation leave load_calculation null (document_control.design_completeness records the absence). For a TI with no service work, add one row with status existing_to_remain from the existing one-line when shown. A one-line rating that differs from a utility letter or an addendum is an envelope conflict. The serving utility is recorded here and the NV Energy standards cited in nv_energy_service_requirements; scope_responsibility.utility_point_of_demarcation keeps only the physical demarcation point and the utility_furnishes list and references these keys. Merged from the former load_calculation field.
service_entrance.x-bdr-overlap: quantities_rollup.service_size copies from this field (voltage enum matches); the related vendor quote lands in the BDR gear pricing section.

available_fault_current.title: Available fault current and AIC ratings
available_fault_current.description: Available short-circuit current at the service and at each downstream bus when shown, the interrupting or short-circuit rating called for on each switchboard, panel and breaker, any spec minimum AIC rule by voltage, and whether a utility available-fault letter is in the package. WHY: Gear and breaker prices step up with interrupting rating, and underrated equipment fails plan review or inspection and is replaced at our cost; a missing fault value means vendors cannot quote gear correctly, so it is a pre-bid RFI. WHERE: One-line fault-current callouts or table, panel schedule AIC column, 26 05 73 study section, 26 24 xx Part 2 ratings, utility fault-current letter.

value.description: Fault current and equipment ratings as printed.

utility_available_fault_ka.description: Available fault current at the service from the utility, kA, as printed.

utility_fault_letter.description: Whether a utility available-fault letter is in the package, cited but missing, or not mentioned.

spec_minimum_aic_text.description: Spec minimum interrupting-rating rule as written (e.g., 'min 22 kAIC at 208V, 65 kAIC at 480V').

per_equipment.description: Per-bus fault values and ratings as printed.

available_fault_ka.description: Available fault current at this bus, kA, as printed.

specified_rating_ka.description: Interrupting or short-circuit rating called for, kA.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

available_fault_current.x-extraction-notes: Extract values as printed; never compute them. Cross-check panel schedule AIC against the one-line and send mismatches to document_control.document_conflicts. Fault current can change by addendum when the utility transformer size changes. Fully rated vs series rated is recorded in distribution_equipment_construction.

nv_energy_service_requirements.title: NV Energy service facilities
nv_energy_service_requirements.description: What NV Energy's service requirements make the customer side build on this project, as shown or cited in the documents: the service configuration (padmount transformer, customer equipment room per RE-4, overhead, customer-owned primary), the customer-built facilities with sizes, counts and NVE detail numbers (conduits and risers, handholes, pull boxes, vaults, transformer pad, meter and CT enclosures, grounding, bollards), the service conductors or bus the customer provides, every NV Energy standard cited, the pre-backfill inspection, NVE design review before permit, equipment-room construction (rated doors, locksets, suppression), post-energization access terms, line-extension agreement or advance notes, application status, and any energization timing the documents state. WHY: Under NV Energy Rule 9 (South) the applicant builds the trench, conduit, pads, vaults and boxes at no cost to NV Energy, so a bare 'per NVE RS-19' callout carries customer-side work nobody priced unless someone reads it. Equipment-room services add rated doors, suppression, customer-furnished conductors or bus and an NVE design review that must come before the permit; backfilling before the NVE inspection means reopening the trench. WHERE: Civil and site utility drawings, electrical site plan, the NVE layout drawing (point of delivery), NV Energy standard details reproduced on drawings (RS-, RE-, RT- series), electrical room plans, Div 26 underground sections, Div 01 utility coordination, pre-bid RFI answers.

value.description: NV Energy customer-side service facilities for this project.

nve_standards_cited.description: Every NV Energy standard or detail cited, as printed (e.g., 'RS-19', 'RE-4', 'RT-G').

facilities.description: Customer-built NV Energy facilities shown or cited. Trench length for the NVE run is in site_electrical, not here.

quantity.description: Quantity as shown (count, or LF for conduit when tabulated).

size_or_spec.description: Size, count per run or specification as printed (e.g., '4-5in PVC Sch 40 + 1-2in').

nve_detail_ref.description: NVE standard or detail number tied to this item.

applies_to.description: Service, run or location this row covers.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

customer_service_conductors_or_bus_text.description: Service conductors or bus the documents have the customer provide, size as stated (e.g., '4 sets 750 kcmil Cu').

prebackfill_inspection.description: Whether the documents require NVE inspection before backfill.

nve_review_before_permit_text.description: NVE design review or approval step the documents place before permit, as written.

equipment_room_construction_text.description: Equipment room or vault construction requirements (door rating, locksets, suppression, access).

post_energization_access_text.description: Terms for customer access after energizing (NVE escort, standby billing, notice).

line_extension_or_advance_text.description: Line-extension agreement, advance or contribution notes as written.

application_status.description: Whether the documents say the NVE service application is filed.

nve_job_number.description: NV Energy work order or job number when printed.

stated_energization_timing_text.description: Any energization date or NVE lead time the documents state; never a market figure.

nv_energy_service_requirements.x-extraction-notes: Record facilities only from the documents. When a sheet calls out an NVE standard detail with no other description, list the customer-built facilities that detail shows and set status inferred with the rule 'NV Energy Rule 9 (South) A.12: the applicant provides trench, conduit, pads, vaults and boxes'. Do not infer service conductors: whether the customer provides them depends on the service type and the NVE layout drawing. The trench length for the NVE run goes in site_electrical trench segments with serves = utility_service; NVE handholes and vaults go here, not in handholes_pull_boxes_vaults. Who performs and pays for the customer-side work, NVE fees and the application are scope_responsibility utility rows; scope_responsibility.utility_point_of_demarcation keeps the physical demarcation point and references nve_standards_cited here (this field absorbed A6 utility_standards_cited and metering.utility_standard_ref). Never invent a lead time or apply the Northern Nevada CI0001M guidance to a Southern Nevada job.
nv_energy_service_requirements.x-reference-facts: NV Energy Rule 9 (South) A.12: the applicant provides, at no cost to NVE, trenching, backfill, excavation, pavement removal and repaving, conduits and risers, transformer pads, vaults, enclosures and boxes; they become NVE property after inspection and acceptance. ESR RT-G: on commercial work the applicant furnishes AND installs the ducts (residential: NVE furnishes, applicant installs); the applicant furnishes and installs pads, handholes, pull boxes, manholes or vaults and grounding; NVE furnishes and installs transformers, cable, cabinets, switches, pole risers and connections, and NVE sets the meter. Service conductors depend on the service type: commercial padmount and vault services in the Southern Nevada ESR use customer-owned service cables that NVE terminates on the transformer (RE-4 15.2, RS-19 note), while Rule 9 A.8 treats line-extension service conductors as utility-furnished at the applicant's cost; the NVE layout drawing shows the point of delivery. On overhead drops the customer provides the service insulator or periscope. RE-4 equipment rooms: at least 10 business days of NVE design review, and NVE approval should come before applying for the city or county permit (RE-4 5.2, 5.5, 5.7); 3-hour rated doors with Best locksets and gaseous fire suppression are typical; primary ducts are concrete-encased (1.5 in between ducts, 3 in overall) with 12 ft sweeps and no elbows; the customer furnishes the service conductors (250, 500 or 750 kcmil) or bus; customer access after energizing requires an NVE escort, billed as standby time, with 7 days' notice. NVE inspects service conduit in the open trench before backfill. The 'apply for service prior to bid' guidance is from NV Energy's Northern Nevada standard CI0001M (Rev 8, 2011), not the Southern Nevada ESR.
nv_energy_service_requirements.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR underground pricing section and the Trenching RFQ, Saw-cut Markup and Trench Markup categories.

metering.description: Utility meter configuration (self-contained sockets, CT cabinet, meter center with tenant meter count, switchboard CT compartment, primary metering) and owner submetering required (tenant, EV, PV, energy-code end use, BMS monitoring) with quantities and communication method. WHY: Multi-tenant meter stacks and owner submeters add device and gear cost that is easy to leave off the takeoff, and meter equipment that does not match the utility requirements is rejected at inspection. WHERE: One-line metering notes, gear elevations, meter center schedules, 26 27 13 Electricity Metering, utility standard details, energy-code compliance sheets.

tenant_meter_count.description: Tenant meter positions shown on a meter center schedule or elevation.

quantity.description: Submeters of this purpose as printed.

communication.description: Communication method as written (e.g., 'Modbus TCP to BAS').

applies_to.description: Panel, area or tenant space covered.

metering.x-extraction-notes: NV Energy standards cited for metering are recorded in nv_energy_service_requirements.nve_standards_cited, not here. Record owner submetering only from the documents; do not add energy-code minimums.
metering.x-reference-facts: NV Energy ESR RT-G: NVE sets the meter.

switchgear_lineup.title: Switchgear, switchboard and MCC lineup
switchgear_lineup.description: Each major distribution assembly (MV switchgear, LV switchgear, switchboard, MCC): tag, type, voltage, main device amps and type, bus amps, short-circuit rating, section count, NEMA enclosure, indoor or outdoor, service-entrance rated, draw-out, main-tie-main, ground-fault protection, and arc energy reduction method when shown. WHY: Gear is usually the biggest single vendor quote and often the longest lead; getting the configuration right (draw-out vs fixed, outdoor NEMA 3R, main-tie-main) is what makes the Switchgear RFQ comparable across vendors and keeps the submittal from blowing up our number. WHERE: One-line diagram, gear elevations and schedules, equipment schedule sheet, 26 13 xx, 26 23 00, 26 24 13, 26 24 19.

value.description: One row per switchgear, switchboard or MCC assembly.

short_circuit_rating_ka.description: Short-circuit or interrupting rating of the assembly, kA.

sections.description: Number of vertical sections when shown.

nema_enclosure.description: NEMA enclosure type as printed (e.g., '1', '3R walk-in').

service_entrance_rated.description: Service-entrance rated; null if not shown.

draw_out.description: Draw-out breakers required; null if not shown.

main_tie_main.description: Main-tie-main configuration; null if not shown.

ground_fault_protection.description: Ground-fault protection of equipment shown; null if not shown.

arc_energy_reduction.description: Arc energy reduction method when shown (e.g., 'maintenance switch', 'ZSI').

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

switchgear_lineup.x-extraction-notes: All panelboards, including distribution panelboards, go in panelboard_schedule. Manufacturer and basis of design go in specified_products. Every MV assembly and large LV assembly should also appear in long_lead_equipment. Do not record or infer lead times here: the fact-check found published 2026 figures vary too much by voltage class and month to use, so lead times come from vendor quotes (long_lead_schedule_check, history_and_outcome). Check addenda for revised elevations. If the project has no gear beyond panelboards, status not_applicable with the one-line cited.
switchgear_lineup.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR Switchgear RFQ category and the gear pricing section.

distribution_equipment_construction.title: Gear and panel construction rules, including SPDs
distribution_equipment_construction.description: Spec rules that apply across classes of switchboards and panelboards, one row per class the rule is written for: bus material (copper required or aluminum allowed), fully rated vs series-rated, required spare breakers and spare bussed space, bolt-on breakers, door-in-door trim, surge protective devices (where required, Type 1 or 2, surge rating, integral or external), and other construction requirements. WHY: Spare capacity, copper bus and 'SPD in every panel' rules have no code trigger, so estimators working from habit miss them, and each is a per-panel adder repeated across every panel and switchboard in the Switchgear quote. WHERE: 26 24 13 and 26 24 16 Part 2, 26 43 13 Surge Protective Devices, panel schedule general notes, one-line SPD symbols, owner design standards bound into the specs.

value.description: One row per equipment class a construction rule applies to.

applies_to.description: Equipment class the rule covers, as written (e.g., 'all panelboards', 'switchboards', '480V distribution').

spare_breaker_pct.description: Required spare breakers as a percent, when stated that way.

spare_space_pct.description: Required spare bussed space as a percent, when stated that way.

spare_rule_text.description: Spare breaker or space rule when not a clean percent (e.g., 'min six 20A/1P spares per panel').

bolt_on_breakers_required.description: Bolt-on breakers required; null if silent.

door_in_door_required.description: Door-in-door (hinged) trim required; null if silent.

spd_required.description: Whether an SPD is required on this equipment class.

spd_surge_rating_ka.description: SPD surge current rating as printed (state per phase or per mode in the envelope note).

spd_mounting.description: Integral to the gear or external.

other_requirements.description: Other construction rules for this class (e.g., copper ground bus, feed-through lugs, sub-feed breakers, SPD monitoring).

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

distribution_equipment_construction.x-extraction-notes: Search panel schedule notes for spare percentages and SPD rules even when 26 24 16 and 26 43 13 are silent; notes often extend an SPD from the service to every panel. Spare (breaker installed, unused) and space (empty bussed position) are never merged. Record what the spec says about series rating; do not judge whether series rating is usable on a motor-heavy building. Merged from the former surge_protection field.

panelboard_schedule.title: Panelboard schedule inventory
panelboard_schedule.description: Every panelboard (distribution and branch): tag, class, voltage, phase and wires, main breaker or MLO and rating, bus amps, pole spaces, breakers, spares and spaces counted separately, AIC, mounting, location, fed-from, normal or emergency branch, and connected and demand kVA from the schedule footer. WHY: Panel count and size is a direct line in the gear quote and a fast cross-project check (panels per SF); a connected load far off the panel or feeder size is a design flag worth an RFI, and the emergency branch column is what the separation rules key off. WHERE: Panel schedule sheets, schedule footers, load summary tables, one-line.

panel_class.description: Distribution (feeds other panels) or branch panel.

main_type.description: Main breaker or main lugs only.

system_branch.description: Normal, emergency, standby or NFPA 99 branch the panel serves.

connected_kva.description: Connected load from the footer, kVA.

demand_kva.description: Demand load from the footer, kVA.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

panelboard_schedule.x-extraction-notes: Spare means a breaker installed but unused; space means an empty position. Never merge them. Extract loads as printed without recomputing demand. Addenda often revise panel schedules without updating the sheet index. Construction rules that apply to all panels (bus material, spares percent, SPD) are in distribution_equipment_construction.
panelboard_schedule.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR Switchgear RFQ and gear pricing section.

feeder_schedule.title: Feeder schedule
feeder_schedule.description: Each feeder: tag, from and to, amps, parallel sets, phase conductors per set and size, neutral and ground size, material (including an aluminum alternative size when shown), conduit size and type, and length with its basis. WHY: Feeders are one of the largest material and labor lines and the most exposed to copper price; this is the takeoff check for wire quotes and the test of the conductor material rule. WHERE: One-line feeder schedule table, riser diagram, panel schedules, floor and site plans for run length.

phase_conductor_size.description: Phase conductor size as printed (e.g., '500 kcmil').

material.description: Conductor material shown for this feeder.

aluminum_alternate_size.description: Aluminum alternate size when the schedule shows both.

length_basis.description: Tabulated on the schedule, dimensioned, or scaled by the model (first pass, verify).

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

feeder_schedule.x-extraction-notes: When the schedule shows both copper and aluminum sizes, capture both. Scaled lengths are first-pass estimates marked scaled_verify and are never priced without the estimator's takeoff. Check that one-line feeder tags match the floor plans. The project-wide copper vs aluminum rule is in conductor_material.
feeder_schedule.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR General Material RFQ (wire and conduit) and the materials pricing section.

transformers.title: Transformers
transformers.description: Each transformer: tag, kVA, primary and secondary voltage, type (dry-type, liquid-filled padmount, liquid-filled substation, utility-owned), K-factor, efficiency level, electrostatic shield, temperature rise, mounting and indoor or outdoor. WHY: K-rated, low-temperature-rise and customer-owned liquid-filled units cost far more than standard dry types, and a customer-owned padmount brings pad, grounding and containment work that is easy to under-scope. WHERE: One-line, transformer schedule, 26 22 00 Part 2, 26 12 xx for liquid-filled units, site plan, utility standard details.

electrostatic_shield.description: Electrostatic shield required; null if silent.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

transformers.x-extraction-notes: Cross-check the mechanical VFD schedule when a K-rating is implied but not stated, and note it rather than filling it. Utility-owned transformers are listed so the one-line is complete but are not priced. Who furnishes a padmount (utility vs contractor) is a scope_responsibility row.

busway.title: Busway and bus duct
busway.description: Feeder or plug-in busway runs: tag, type, amps, voltage, copper or aluminum, length with basis, number of plug-in units, and enclosure rating. WHY: Busway is quoted by gear vendors, is long lead, and replaces large parallel feeders; leaving it out of the Switchgear RFQ or pricing it as cable changes the number materially. WHERE: One-line and riser diagrams, 26 25 00 Enclosed Bus Assemblies, electrical room and riser plans.

busway.x-extraction-notes: Record only runs shown or specified. Manufacturer goes in specified_products. Busway runs also appear in long_lead_equipment.

disconnects_and_enclosures.title: Disconnects and enclosure ratings
disconnects_and_enclosures.description: Safety switch and enclosed breaker rules: default duty rating, fused or non-fused rule, fuse class, and required NEMA enclosure and material by location (1, 3R, 4X stainless, 12, hazardous). WHY: NEMA 4X stainless and heavy-duty fusible switches cost several times a general-duty NEMA 1 or 3R unit; the wrong assumption on rooftop, pool, kitchen or wash-down areas is a quiet miss repeated across dozens of units. WHERE: 26 28 16 Enclosed Switches and Circuit Breakers, 26 28 13 Fuses, equipment connection schedule, drawing general notes.

default_duty.description: Required duty rating of safety switches.

fusing_rule_text.description: Fused vs non-fused rule as written.

applies_to.description: Location or equipment the enclosure rule covers (e.g., 'roof', 'kitchen', 'pool equipment').

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

disconnects_and_enclosures.x-extraction-notes: Pair with equipment_connection_schedule so each disconnect gets the right enclosure. Who furnishes mechanical disconnects is scope_responsibility.

generators.title: Generators
generators.description: Each generator: kW and kVA, voltage, fuel, NEC use (emergency, legally required standby, optional standby), fuel tank type, capacity and required runtime, enclosure with sound level at a stated distance, emissions tier, location, paralleling, portable generator docking station, and loads served. WHY: The generator package is its own vendor RFQ and one of the longest-lead items; sound-attenuated enclosures, extended-runtime sub-base tanks and emissions tier move the quote as much as kW, and the NEC use decides the wiring rules downstream. WHERE: One-line, generator schedule, 26 32 13 Part 2, life-safety and code plan sheets, site plan.

runtime_hours.description: Required runtime in hours at the stated load.

sound_distance_ft.description: Distance the sound limit applies at, feet.

emissions_tier.description: Emissions tier or certification as printed.

docking_station.description: Portable generator docking station required; null if silent.

loads_served.description: Loads or branches served, as listed.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

generators.x-extraction-notes: NEC use is often only on the code or life-safety sheet; cross-check. When no standby source exists, status not_applicable citing the one-line or code sheet; silence is not_stated. Load bank testing is testing_commissioning_closeout; who pulls air-quality and fuel permits is scope_responsibility; transfer switches are transfer_switches. Do not judge whether a tank size meets fire-code limits.
generators.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR Generator & Equipment RFQ category (gear pricing section).

transfer_switches.title: Automatic transfer switches
transfer_switches.description: Each ATS: amps, poles, transition (open, closed, delayed or programmed), bypass-isolation, service-entrance rated, withstand rating, branch served, and remote annunciator. WHY: Bypass-isolation and closed-transition units cost far more than a basic open-transition ATS; reading only 'ATS' off the one-line underprices the Generator & Equipment quote. WHERE: 26 36 23 Part 2, one-line, ATS schedule.

remote_annunciator.description: Remote annunciator required; null if silent.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

transfer_switches.x-extraction-notes: Check the spec type even when the one-line shows a plain ATS symbol.
transfer_switches.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR Generator & Equipment RFQ.

emergency_power_systems.title: Emergency system classification and wiring rules
emergency_power_systems.description: Which systems are emergency (NEC 700), legally required standby (701), optional standby (702) or healthcare essential electrical system branches (NFPA 99), and the wiring rules that follow: separate raceways and boxes, fire-rated or survivability protection for emergency feeders and its rating, selective coordination and its scope, emergency lighting source, and whether UL 924 relays or transfer devices are required. WHY: Emergency separation, two-hour rated feeder protection and selective coordination drive large costs on resort, casino, high-rise and healthcare work and are rarely visible from the one-line alone; missing them is both a margin hit and a failed life-safety inspection. WHERE: One-line emergency branches, life-safety and code sheets, 26 05 19, 26 32 13, 26 36 23, 26 52 00 emergency lighting, 26 05 73 selective coordination.

value.description: Emergency and standby classification and wiring rules.

systems.description: One row per classified system or branch.

system_name.description: System or branch name as printed.

separate_raceways_required.description: Separate raceways and boxes required; null if silent.

feeder_fire_protection.description: Fire protection method required for the feeders.

applies_to.description: Feeders, areas or buildings the rule covers.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

selective_coordination_scope_text.description: Scope of selective coordination as written (e.g., 'emergency and legally required, down to 0.1 s').

ul924_devices_required.description: UL 924 relays or transfer devices required.

emergency_power_systems.x-extraction-notes: Classification often appears only on the code or life-safety sheet. Flag a one-line that shows emergency and normal circuits sharing raceways. Record only what the documents require; do not assert that a code trigger applies. Generator and ATS hardware are in generators and transfer_switches; UL 924 device counts are takeoff; the local Article 700/701 amendments are evaluated in southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.
emergency_power_systems.x-reference-facts: SNV 2023 NEC amendments modify 700.1, 700.10(D)(1), 700.10(D)(2)(5), 700.12(B), 700.12(D)(5), 700.32(C) and 701.32(C); other subsections of those sections remain unchanged.
emergency_power_systems.x-bdr-overlap: Affects the Switchgear and Generator & Equipment RFQs and General Material (rated cable).

ups_and_central_inverters.title: UPS and central lighting inverters
ups_and_central_inverters.description: UPS and central lighting inverter systems: application, kVA, topology, runtime at the stated load, battery type, battery cabinet count and maintenance bypass. WHY: Online double-conversion and lithium systems cost far more, and runtime drives battery cabinet count, room space and floor loading. WHERE: 26 33 xx, 26 52 00 for central lighting inverters, one-line, equipment schedules.

value.description: One row per UPS or central inverter.

runtime_load_text.description: Load the runtime applies to (e.g., 'full load', '80 kW').

maintenance_bypass.description: Maintenance bypass required; null if silent.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

ups_and_central_inverters.x-extraction-notes: Capture runtime with the load it applies to.
ups_and_central_inverters.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR Generator & Equipment RFQ.

fire_pump_power.title: Fire pump power
fire_pump_power.description: The fire pump's electrical requirements: HP, voltage, power source (dedicated utility tap, separate service, on-site generator, multiple), whether the controller and transfer switch are shown, and the feeder routing or protection requirement as written. WHY: Fire pump feeders carry special routing and protection rules and sometimes a separate service tap; they are expensive, often shown only on fire protection or code sheets, and a classic unpriced item. WHERE: One-line, fire protection (FP) drawings, 21 30 00 Fire Pumps, Div 26 fire pump sections, code sheet.

controller_and_transfer_switch_shown.description: Controller and transfer switch shown on the electrical drawings; null if unclear.

feeder_protection_text.description: Feeder routing or protection requirement as written (e.g., '2-hour encased, outside the building').

fire_pump_power.x-extraction-notes: No fire pump: status not_applicable citing the FP drawings or code sheet. Record the routing and protection rule as the documents state it; do not supply a method from NFPA 20 or NEC 695. Who furnishes the controller and transfer switch is a scope_responsibility row.

power_system_studies.title: Power system studies and arc flash
power_system_studies.description: Which studies the documents require (short circuit, coordination, arc flash, load flow, harmonic, and existing-load recording before adding load to an existing service), the IEEE 1584 and NFPA 70E editions cited, equipment scope, PE stamp, whether field settings must be made by an independent testing agency, arc-flash labels, timing, and on renovations any existing study provided with its date and edition. WHY: A contractor-furnished study plus independent-agency settings is commonly a five-figure line no vendor quote carries by default, study scope drives the fee and label count, and an old study reused on a renovation may have to be redone before labels can be trusted. A 30-day load recording before adding load to an existing service is a renovation cost that is easy to miss. WHERE: 26 05 73 / 26 05 73.13 / .16 / .19 Part 1 and Part 3, 26 05 53 label articles, gear sections, existing-conditions notes on renovation one-lines.

ieee_1584_edition.description: IEEE 1584 edition cited; edition_not_given when cited without a year.

pe_stamp_required.description: PE-stamped study required; null if silent.

independent_agency_settings.description: Settings must be made by an independent testing agency; null if silent.

labels_required.description: Arc-flash labels required; null if silent.

timing_text.description: Timing as written (e.g., 'submit before gear release for manufacture').

existing_study_provided.description: Existing study provided or cited on a renovation; null when none.

power_system_studies.x-extraction-notes: When the documents require no study, status not_applicable only if they say so; silence is not_stated. existing_load_recording means the specs require a NEC 220.87 style 30-day recording or 12-month demand data before adding load to an existing service. Whenever any study is required, scope_responsibility must carry a power_system_studies row for who performs and pays; some specs split it (contractor collects field data, engineer runs the study). SNV 110.12(F) settings documentation is evaluated in southern_nevada_amendment_triggers; the label format is identification_and_labeling.
power_system_studies.x-reference-facts: IEEE 1584-2018 replaced the 2002 edition's arc-flash model and validated ranges; incident energy under the 2018 model can differ materially from a 2002-basis study. SNV 2023 NEC amendment 110.12(F): PE-selected settings for adjustable protective equipment documented, displayed at the equipment and retained.
power_system_studies.x-bdr-overlap: none (study cost is carried by the estimator or a study engineer; no BDR RFQ category)

lightning_protection.title: Lightning protection
lightning_protection.description: Whether a lightning protection system is required, the standard cited (NFPA 780, UL 96A), UL Master Label or certified installer requirement, and whether it is designed or left to delegated design. WHY: Master-labeled systems need a certified specialty installer, so the scope needs a sub quote; leaving it in the base bid unpriced or unflagged is a straight loss. WHERE: 26 41 13 Part 1, roof plan, grounding details.

ul_master_label_required.description: UL Master Label required; null if silent.

certified_installer_required.description: UL-listed or LPI-certified installer required; null if silent.

design_basis.description: Designed by the engineer of record or delegated.

lightning_protection.x-extraction-notes: No system: status not_applicable only when the documents say so or no section, roof-plan callout or detail exists (list them in searched). When required it is normally a specialty subcontract: add a specified_products row with rfq_category specialty_subcontract. Who designs a delegated system is scope_responsibility.delegated_design_items.
