seismic_restraint.title: Seismic restraint of electrical systems
seismic_restraint.description: Whether electrical equipment, conduit, cable tray and fixtures need seismic bracing and anchorage, the seismic design category and component importance factor as printed, delegated bracing design with a PE stamp, special seismic certification of equipment, and any stated exemption. WHY: Bracing hardware, anchorage calcs, a stamped delegated design and certified equipment all cost money when required; the requirement depends on the site's seismic design category, which only the structural notes state. WHERE: 26 05 48, structural general notes (seismic design category), equipment sections Part 2 seismic qualification articles.

required.description: Whether seismic restraint of electrical work is required; 'no' only when the documents say so.

seismic_design_category.description: Seismic design category as printed on the S-sheets or specs.

component_importance_factor.description: Component importance factor Ip as printed.

delegated_design_stamp_required.description: Stamped delegated bracing design required; null if silent.

equipment_certification_required.description: Special seismic certification of equipment required; null if silent.

exemption_text.description: Any exemption stated (e.g., 'conduit under 2-1/2 in exempt').

seismic_restraint.x-extraction-notes: Read the seismic design category from the structural general notes and 26 05 48; never assume a Las Vegas site is exempt or covered. Who hires the delegated-design engineer is scope_responsibility.delegated_design_items. Hangers and ordinary supports are in raceway_general_requirements.
seismic_restraint.x-reference-facts: Clark County enforces the 2024 IBC with Southern Nevada amendments for new permit applications from 2026-01-11.

site_electrical.title: Site electrical and trenching
site_electrical.description: Site electrical content from the site plans: the utility point of connection, trench and duct bank segments (what each serves, length with basis, duct count and size, surface), site equipment pads, and other utilities crossed or paralleled with required clearances. WHY: Trench LF, surface type and duct counts drive G3's Trenching RFQ, saw-cut and trench markups and the underground pricing section; crossings and paved surfaces are where hand digging, saw cutting and patching blow up the trench unit price. WHERE: Electrical site plan, civil utility plans, utility standard details, site lighting plan, duct bank schedules.

poc_text.description: Utility point of connection location as described.

trench_segments.description: One row per trench or duct bank segment.

segment_id.description: Segment label or a short route description.

length_basis.description: Tabulated, dimensioned, or scaled by the model (first pass, verify).

applies_to.description: Route or area (from, to).

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

pad_for.description: Equipment the pad supports (transformer, switchboard, generator).

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

utility_type.description: Crossed or paralleled utility (gas, water, sewer, storm, telecom).

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

site_electrical.x-extraction-notes: Site plans rarely dimension runs, so most lengths are scaled_verify first-pass estimates that are never priced without the estimator's takeoff. The electrical site plan often omits other utilities; read the civil utility sheets for crossings. The NVE service run is a segment with serves = utility_service (its conduits, boxes and pad specs are in nv_energy_service_requirements). Who trenches, backfills and patches is scope_responsibility; duct bank construction is duct_bank_encasement; soil and caliche are subsurface_conditions_for_trenching; public right-of-way work is offsite_electrical_improvements; pole bases are exterior_site_lighting; EV stubs are ev_charging. TI or interior-only work: status not_applicable citing the scope.
site_electrical.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR Trenching RFQ (underground pricing section) and the Saw-cut Markup and Trench Markup categories.

subsurface_conditions_for_trenching.title: Subsurface conditions for trenching
subsurface_conditions_for_trenching.description: What the geotechnical report and Division 31 say that changes how G3's trenches are dug and backfilled: caliche or cemented soil and its depth range, whether excavation is unclassified or rock is classified and paid separately, the rock definition, groundwater depth, corrosive or sulfate soils and the cement type or conduit protection they require, whether native backfill may be used, trench compaction requirements, and other findings such as collapsible or expansive soils. WHY: Caliche is the largest unknown in Las Vegas valley trenching, and hoe-ram or rock-saw work can double the cost of the same run of duct bank. The catalog records who digs rock and whether the report is a contract document, but without this field nothing records what the report actually says. WHERE: Geotechnical report (often a project manual appendix or 'available for review'), boring logs, 31 23 16 Excavation and 31 23 33 Trenching and Backfilling (rock definition, compaction), civil general notes.

value.description: Subsurface conditions that affect electrical trenching.

caliche_or_cemented.description: Whether the report or Div 31 reports caliche or cemented soil; not_reported only when a report exists and is silent or says none was encountered.

caliche_depth_text.description: Depth range and locations as written (e.g., 'caliche at 2 to 6 ft in B-3 and B-5').

excavation_classification.description: Whether all excavation is unclassified (rock in the lump sum) or rock is classified and paid separately.

rock_definition_text.description: Rock definition as written (equipment test, volume, refusal criteria).

corrosive_or_sulfate_soil.description: Whether corrosive or sulfate soils are reported.

corrosion_protection_required_text.description: Cement type, coating or conduit protection required because of soil (e.g., 'Type V cement', 'PVC-coated RGS below grade').

native_backfill.description: Whether native soil may be used as trench backfill.

trench_compaction_text.description: Trench compaction requirement as written (e.g., '95 percent under paving, 90 percent elsewhere').

other_findings_text.description: Other findings that affect trenching (collapsible or expansive soil, over-excavation, moisture conditioning).

subsurface_conditions_for_trenching.x-extraction-notes: Record depths and locations as printed; never generalize valley conditions or fill from other projects. When the report is only cited and Div 31 is silent, status referenced_not_provided (document_control.referenced_documents_not_provided lists the report). Ownership: whether the report is a contract document or information only is contract_terms.differing_site_conditions_relief; who excavates rock and caliche is the scope_responsibility rock_caliche_excavation row; any rock unit price is bid_submission.unit_prices; Div 26 bedding around conduit is underground_raceway_installation.

WHERE: EV spec section, site and parking plans, one-line, Div 01 sustainability sections, code sheets.

Slot and table-game connections, signage, irrigation controllers, gates and dock equipment and showroom stage power are scheduled on non-MEP sheets; read them. WHY: Relocate-and-reconnect is several times the labor of simple removal, reused gear of unknown condition or rating is a field-risk cost, and removing abandoned cable above ceilings is a real labor item on resort and office renovations that is rarely priced unless called out. long_lead_equipment.description: Equipment on this project of a long-lead type (MV and LV switchgear, switchboards, large transformers, generators, transfer switches, busway, UPS, lighting and lighting-control packages), with any delivery or lead-time requirement, owner pre-purchase or early-release requirement, and required-on-site date or milestone the documents tie to that equipment. WHY: Gear and generator lead times often exceed GC schedule assumptions; spotting it at bid lets us qualify the lead time, ask for early release or propose a faster manufacturer before carrying liquidated-damages exposure on a firm price. WHERE: One-line and equipment schedules, gear and generator sections Part 1 delivery articles, Div 01 procurement and schedule sections, ITB milestone dates, owner pre-purchase notes.

long_lead_equipment.x-extraction-notes: Rows come from the equipment inventories (switchgear_lineup, transformers, generators, transfer_switches, busway, ups_and_central_inverters, lighting schedules) by the long-lead type list; membership is inferred by that named rule, spec text is found. Never store market lead-time numbers here. GC or owner early-release commitments are contract_terms.long_lead_early_release; early submittal deadlines are testing_commissioning_closeout.submittal_timing_and_review; the date comparison is long_lead_schedule_check.
long_lead_equipment.x-reference-facts: Fact-check 2026-09-23: published 2026 lead times for switchboards, MV switchgear, generators and transformers vary widely by voltage class, manufacturer, source and month (from about 52 weeks for commodity switchboards to more than 160 weeks for power transformers), so no published figure is a benchmark; lead times come from vendor quotes or BDR history.

long_lead_schedule_check.title: Long-lead schedule check
long_lead_schedule_check.description: For each long_lead_equipment row, a computed check of whether the equipment can arrive when the schedule needs it: required-on-site date and its basis, lead time in weeks and where it came from (spec, vendor quote, BDR history), latest purchase-order date, and a conflict flag. WHY: The flag has to rest on a real lead time, not model memory; tying it to the vendor quote or BDR's own delivery history tells the estimator whether to qualify the schedule, ask for early release or push a faster manufacturer. WHERE: Derived from power_distribution.long_lead_equipment, schedule_and_site.interim_milestones and baseline_schedule_exhibit, contract_terms.long_lead_early_release, BDR vendor quotes, and history_and_outcome.gear_lead_time_quoted_vs_actual.

The likely vs possible threshold (weeks between latest PO date and the expected award-to-PO date) is a G3 setting. bid_brief.top_risks and bid_brief.vendor_pricing_risks read this field instead of re-deriving it.
long_lead_schedule_check.x-reference-facts: Fact-check 2026-09-23: published 2026 lead times for switchboards, MV switchgear, generators and transformers vary widely by voltage class, manufacturer, source and month (from about 52 weeks for commodity switchboards to more than 160 weeks for power transformers), so no published figure is a benchmark; lead times come from vendor quotes or BDR history.

southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.title: Southern Nevada NEC amendment checks
southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.description: For each 2023 NEC Southern Nevada amendment that changes design or cost, whether this project triggers it, the basis, and whether the drawings and specs comply or conflict: 110.30 third-party review for 1000V and above, 110.12(F) settings documentation, Article 700/701 amendments, 210.8(B)(16) food and beverage GFCI, 230.70 service disconnect location, 352.10(G) exposed PVC Schedule 80, 358.12 no EMT in earth or earth-contact concrete, 800.24(C) low-voltage cable in concealed Type I/II spaces, 250.50 concrete-encased electrode, 250.120(D) wire EGC in exterior compression-fitting raceways, 705.12(A)(4) PV tap box, and 210.23(F) dwelling outlet limits. WHY: These rules sit outside the base NEC, so a design or estimate built from base code misses them; MV third-party review, settings documentation, rated electrical rooms, Schedule 80 PVC, rigid in slab-on-grade, plenum cable and extra EGCs are all real cost on typical G3 work, and a drawing that conflicts with an amendment is a change waiting to happen. WHERE: Code sheet or code analysis, one-line (voltage classes, adjustable-trip breakers, service disconnect location), electrical room plans, raceway notes and details, life-safety sheets, kitchen and bar plans, grounding details, PV sheets, dwelling unit plans; 26 05 33, 26 05 26, 26 05 73, 26 32 13, 26 36 23.

value.description: One row per amendment; every listed amendment is answered on projects whose AHJ adopted the Southern Nevada Amendments.

other_amendment_ref.description: Section number when amendment is other.

triggered.description: Whether this project triggers the amendment.

trigger_basis.description: Short basis (e.g., '12.47kV customer-owned loop on E-601', 'no kitchens or bars').

drawings_comply.description: Whether the drawings and specs comply when triggered.

conflict_detail.description: The conflicting sheet or spec item (e.g., 'EMT shown in slab-on-grade, E-101 note 4').

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.x-extraction-notes: Answer every listed amendment when project_profile.ahj and code_editions show a jurisdiction that has adopted the Southern Nevada Amendments and a permit application on or after its effective date; otherwise status not_applicable (for example State Public Works Division or federal sites, which have their own building officials) or, when adoption or the permit date is unknown, triggered = not_determinable. The amendment rules come from the reference table, attached by rule; triggered and drawings_comply are inferred from this project's documents with the amendment named as the rule. Read the actual amended text: many subsections inside an amended section 'remain unchanged'. Useful conflicts: EMT in slab-on-grade or below grade, Schedule 40 PVC shown exposed, service disconnect in a room without direct exterior access, no concrete-encased electrode detail on a new building with footings, exterior compression-fitting raceways without a wire EGC, non-plenum low-voltage cable in concealed spaces of a Type I or II building (construction type from project_profile.building_type). Who pays for MV third-party review is a scope_responsibility row; the amendment places it on the property owner.
southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.x-reference-facts: 2023 NEC Southern Nevada Amendments, developed by the Southern Nevada Building Officials NEC Committee; they are not code until each jurisdiction adopts them. Clark County adopted them 2025-07-15, effective 2026-01-11 for new permit applications; the City of Las Vegas approved them 2025-07-16, effective 2026-01-05 (projects submitted earlier could use the prior codes). 110.30: systems 1000V and above need third-party peer review before AHJ approval and AHJ-approved third-party inspection and testing, at the property owner's expense. 110.12(F): PE-selected settings for adjustable equipment (GFPE, arc energy reduction, adjustable trips, relays and selective coordination, series-rated combinations) documented, displayed at the equipment and retained. Articles 700/701 amended at 700.1, 700.10(D)(1), 700.10(D)(2)(5), 700.12(B), 700.12(D)(5), 700.32(C) and 701.32(C); other subsections remain unchanged. 210.8(B)(16): GFCI for 125-250V receptacles in Health District regulated food and beverage prep or serving areas. 230.70: service disconnect outdoors within 12 ft of the building, or in a dedicated electrical room with 1-hour separation, direct exterior access, a yellow 1 sq ft sign and a yellow floor stripe. 352.10(G): exposed PVC must be Schedule 80. 358.12: no EMT underground, in earth fill, or in concrete in contact with earth. 800.24(C): low-voltage cable in concealed spaces of Type I or II buildings must be plenum-rated or in metal raceway. 250.50: a concrete-encased electrode is required in new buildings with concrete footings. 250.120(D): a wire EGC is required in exterior raceways with compression fittings. 705.12(A)(4): PV feeder taps in a dedicated labeled box of at least 100 cu in. 210.23(F): dwellings limited to 12 outlets per 15/20A circuit, with dedicated 20A circuits for dishwasher, compactor and microwave.

wiring_and_lighting.title: Wiring, raceway and lighting
wiring_and_lighting.description: Captures the conductor, MV cable, wiring method, raceway, underground installation, duct bank, grounding, device, labeling, lighting schedule, controls, site lighting and ceiling rules that drive General Material, Lighting and labor pricing.

conductor_material.title: Conductor material (copper vs aluminum)
conductor_material.description: Whether copper is required or aluminum is allowed, stated separately for service entrance, feeders and branch circuits, with the minimum size at which aluminum is allowed, any narrower rules for specific applications (for example feeders 100A and larger, MV, site feeders), alloy or termination requirements, and whether copper-clad aluminum is prohibited. WHY: Copper-only vs aluminum-allowed is one of the biggest single swings in feeder cost; pricing aluminum where the spec says copper gets rejected at submittal, and pricing copper where aluminum is allowed loses the bid. WHERE: 26 05 19 Part 2, feeder schedule notes on the one-line, GC bid instructions, addenda.

service.description: Copper vs aluminum rule for service-entrance conductors.

service_aluminum_min_size.description: Smallest service conductor size at which aluminum is allowed, as printed.

branch_circuits.description: Copper vs aluminum rule for branch circuits.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

aluminum_alloy_termination_text.description: Alloy (e.g., AA-8000), connector or termination requirements for aluminum, as written.

conductor_material.x-extraction-notes: Never infer aluminum is allowed because the NEC permits it; silence is not_stated per class. Feeders and branch circuits are often treated differently; never collapse them. Addenda frequently flip this rule; the envelope's superseded_by_addendum carries the change. A drawing note that disagrees with 26 05 19 is an envelope conflict with the most-stringent working value until answered.
conductor_material.x-bdr-overlap: Drives the BDR General Material RFQ (wire) and the materials pricing section.

branch_circuit_wiring_rules.title: Branch circuit wiring rules
branch_circuit_wiring_rules.description: Minimum conductor size for power, lighting and control circuits; voltage-drop upsizing rules (for example upsizing homeruns beyond a stated length); dedicated vs shared neutral; maximum circuits per homerun; and separate or isolated ground conductor requirements. WHY: A dedicated-neutral rule or a larger minimum on long homeruns multiplies wire and conduit fill across the whole building, and these rules often live only in drawing general notes where a quick read misses them. WHERE: 26 05 19 Part 3, electrical drawing general notes, panel schedule notes, homerun notes on plans.

min_lighting_awg.description: Minimum lighting circuit conductor size as printed.

min_control_awg.description: Minimum control conductor size as printed.

neutral_rule.description: Neutral rule for multiwire branch circuits.

max_circuits_per_homerun.description: Maximum circuits per homerun or raceway.

ground_conductor_rule_text.description: Separate or isolated ground conductor requirement as written.

branch_circuit_wiring_rules.x-extraction-notes: Check both the spec and the drawing general notes; they often disagree or only one states the rule. Do not fill a minimum from code; silence is not_stated.

conductor_specifications.description: Required insulation types by location (THHN/THWN-2, XHHW-2, wet, underground, high temperature), maximum single conductor size before paralleling and parallel-set rules, the conductor color code by voltage system, factory-colored insulation vs field taping, and compression lug or splice requirements, for low-voltage (600V) power conductors. WHY: Wrong insulation or colors means re-pull or re-tape labor, and a maximum conductor size or compression-lug rule changes lug, conduit and labor counts on every large feeder. medium_voltage_cable.description: Customer-owned medium-voltage cable on the project, one row per cable type or circuit group: voltage class, conductor size and material, insulation type and level, shield, jacket, termination and splice types, splices shown, and whether certified splicers are required. VLF or hi-pot testing is testing_commissioning_closeout.field_testing_requirements; the Cable Splicer wage classification is labor_and_compliance.craft_classifications; MV third-party review is southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.

wiring_method_permissions.title: MC cable and flexible wiring allowances
wiring_method_permissions.description: Where MC cable is allowed, by area or use (allowed, concealed only, fixture and equipment whips only, prohibited) and whether MC homeruns are allowed; maximum MC whip, FMC and LFMC lengths; separate equipment grounding conductor in flex; and AC and NM cable rules. raceway_type_by_location.description: The required raceway for each installation location (concealed dry, exposed interior, exposed exterior, wet or damp, corrosive, electrical and mechanical rooms, parking structures, in slab, below slab on grade, underground site, underground elbows and stub-ups, hazardous classified areas, kitchens, pools and fountains, final connections) and the alternatives allowed. WHY: Rigid and PVC-coated rigid cost far more in material and labor than EMT; misreading the location matrix is one of the most cited electrical estimating misses. WHERE: 26 05 33 Part 3 (often scattered prose), 26 05 43, drawing general notes, hazardous area plans.

Hazardous classified areas get their own rows. Underground elbows and stub-ups are rows here (installation depth and bedding are underground_raceway_installation). Conflicts with the local Schedule 80 and EMT amendments are evaluated in southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.
raceway_type_by_location.x-reference-facts: SNV 2023 NEC amendments: 352.10(G) exposed PVC must be Schedule 80; 358.12 no EMT underground, in earth fill or in concrete in contact with earth; 250.120(D) a wire EGC is required in exterior raceways with compression fittings.

raceway_general_requirements.title: Conduit size, fittings, tray and supports

strut_finish_text.description: Strut and hardware finish as written (e.g., 'stainless in wet areas').

raceway_general_requirements.x-extraction-notes: Low-voltage pathway sizing belongs to low_voltage_life_safety; record only the Div 26 rule and any exception it states. Seismic bracing is seismic_restraint. Merged from the former hangers_and_supports field.
raceway_general_requirements.x-bdr-overlap: Affects the BDR General Material RFQ.

structural_constraints.title: Structural constraints on raceway
structural_constraints.description: Post-tensioned slabs, whether conduit may be embedded in slabs or topping, coring and scanning restrictions, and sleeve and embed requirements. WHY: PT slabs need scanning and engineer review before coring and can ban in-slab conduit, which moves raceway overhead and adds labor; missed sleeves become field cost. WHERE: Structural general notes (S-series), slab details, electrical general notes.

in_slab_conduit.description: Conduit embedded in slabs or topping.

coring_restrictions_text.description: Coring, scanning and engineer-approval rules as written.

sleeves_embeds_text.description: Sleeve and embed requirements as written.

structural_constraints.x-extraction-notes: Treat a note prohibiting field-cut penetrations as a must-show item. Who cores, scans and pours pads is scope_responsibility.

underground_raceway_installation.title: Underground raceway installation
underground_raceway_installation.description: How below-grade raceway must be installed: minimum cover by area (non-traffic, under drives, MV), trench width, Div 26 bedding and backfill around conduit, spacers, required separation from gas, water, sewer and other utilities, and warning tape type, depth and count. WHY: Depth, bedding and separations set the cost of every foot of trench, and utility separations can force hand digging or separate trenches that a standard trench unit price does not cover. WHERE: 26 05 43 Part 2 and 3, 26 05 33, civil and site details, utility trench standards referenced.

cover_requirements.description: Minimum cover by area or run type.

applies_to.description: Area or run type (e.g., 'non-traffic', 'under drives', 'MV duct banks').

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

bedding_backfill_text.description: Div 26 bedding and backfill around conduit as written (e.g., '3 in sand all sides').

spacers_required.description: Conduit spacers required; null if silent.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

warning_tape_text.description: Warning tape type, depth and count rule as written.

underground_raceway_installation.x-extraction-notes: Depths are often only on civil or utility details; when the spec cites a utility standard without numbers, say so in the note and set verify_action check_reference. Raceway type below grade, elbows and stub-ups are raceway_type_by_location; soil, caliche and trench compaction are subsurface_conditions_for_trenching; who excavates and backfills is scope_responsibility. Any example depth in research is one project's clause, never a default.

duct_bank_encasement.title: Duct bank concrete encasement
duct_bank_encasement.description: Where duct banks must be concrete encased and where direct burial is allowed (all runs, under paving only, MV and service only), the red color method (integral pigment, red top dye, red warning planks), minimum concrete cover and duct spacing, rebar and concrete strength. WHY: Encasement adds concrete, rebar, forming, pumping and extra excavation to every foot of duct bank; assuming direct-buried PVC when the spec says encased is a large and common underground miss. WHERE: 26 05 43 Part 2 and 3, duct bank sections and details on site sheets, NV Energy standards for utility runs.

value.description: One row per duct bank rule.

applies_to.description: Runs the rule covers (e.g., 'all MV', 'under paving', 'all site feeders').

min_concrete_cover_in.description: Minimum concrete cover around ducts, inches.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

duct_bank_encasement.x-extraction-notes: Integral red concrete and red warning planks over direct-buried duct are very different costs; never conflate them. NV Energy duct encasement is recorded with the NVE facilities in nv_energy_service_requirements. Duct counts per segment are site_electrical; who furnishes encasement concrete is the scope_responsibility duct_bank_concrete row.

handholes_pull_boxes_vaults.title: Handholes, pull boxes and manholes
handholes_pull_boxes_vaults.description: Underground structures on project-owned runs: type, size, material, load rating, quantity with its basis, lid marking, and where each type is used. WHY: Traffic-rated precast structures are significant line items that are often undercounted from a site plan. WHERE: 26 05 43 Part 2, site electrical plan, structure schedule or details.

type.description: Structure type as printed (handhole, pull box, manhole).

applies_to.description: Where this type is used (drives, landscape, MV runs).

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

handholes_pull_boxes_vaults.x-extraction-notes: Quantities come from a schedule or labels when possible; symbol counts are first-pass only. NV Energy boxes and vaults go in nv_energy_service_requirements; ROW pull boxes go in offsite_electrical_improvements.
handholes_pull_boxes_vaults.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR underground pricing section.

grounding_system.title: Grounding and bonding system
grounding_system.description: Grounding electrodes required (ground ring and length, rods with count and spec, concrete-encased electrode, building steel, water pipe), resistance targets stricter than code by system, the grounding electrode conductor size shown, exothermic vs mechanical connections, and supplemental grounding (generator, electrical rooms, lightning protection bonding, separately derived systems). WHY: A ground ring, a rod field to meet a tight ohm target, or exothermic welds throughout are real trenching, material and labor a quick one-line read misses; GEC size is a quiet under-count on large services, and a concrete-encased electrode has to be placed before the footing pour. WHERE: 26 05 26 Part 2 and 3, grounding plan and details, grounding riser, one-line grounding notes.

electrodes.description: Electrodes the drawings or specs require.

ground_ring_length_ft.description: Ground ring length, feet, when printed.

rod_spec_text.description: Rod size, length and spacing as written.

applies_to.description: System the target covers (service, generator, lightning).

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

gec_size_shown.description: Grounding electrode conductor size as shown on the one-line or grounding riser.

grounding_system.x-extraction-notes: Read gec_size_shown from the drawings; never compute it from NEC 250.66. If the spec only says 'per NEC', leave resistance_targets empty; never infer a number. concrete_encased in electrodes means the documents show it; whether a new building with footings lacks it is evaluated in southern_nevada_amendment_triggers (250.50). Flag the concrete-encased electrode pour coordination in the note. Telecom grounding (TIA-607) is low_voltage_life_safety; ground resistance testing is testing_commissioning_closeout.
grounding_system.x-reference-facts: NEC 250.66 sizes the GEC from the largest ungrounded service-entrance conductor (Table 250.66, 8 AWG Cu minimum to 3/0 Cu maximum); a GEC that is the sole connection to rod electrodes need not exceed 6 AWG Cu. SNV 2023 NEC amendment 250.50: a concrete-encased electrode is required in new buildings with concrete footings.
grounding_system.x-bdr-overlap: Affects the BDR General Material RFQ and labor.

wiring_devices.title: Wiring devices and floor box types
wiring_devices.description: Device grade (spec, hospital, industrial) and where exceptions apply, tamper-resistant and weather-resistant scope, GFCI, AFCI and dual-function scope beyond base code, self-test or USB devices, device color and plate material, and floor box and poke-through types. WHY: Hospital-grade or 'TR everywhere' clauses multiply device cost across every receptacle, and floor boxes and poke-throughs are expensive units in office, ballroom and convention space. WHERE: 26 27 26 Part 2, device legend, floor plans, kitchen and bar plans.

grade_exceptions_text.description: Areas with a different grade, as written.

gfci_afci_scope_text.description: GFCI, AFCI or dual-function scope beyond base code as written.

special_devices_text.description: Self-test GFCI, USB or other special devices required.

floor_box_types.description: Floor box and poke-through types specified (counts are quantities_rollup.wiring_device_totals).

wiring_devices.x-extraction-notes: Check room-by-room exceptions on the drawings. Device and floor box counts are takeoff quantities in quantities_rollup.wiring_device_totals. The local food and beverage GFCI and dwelling outlet rules are evaluated in southern_nevada_amendment_triggers.
wiring_devices.x-reference-facts: SNV 2023 NEC amendments: 210.8(B)(16) GFCI for 125-250V receptacles in Health District regulated food and beverage prep or serving areas; 210.23(F) dwellings limited to 12 outlets per 15/20A circuit, with dedicated 20A circuits for dishwasher, compactor and microwave.
wiring_devices.x-bdr-overlap: Affects the BDR General Material RFQ.

identification_and_labeling.title: Identification and labeling
identification_and_labeling.description: Nameplate type (engraved, color by system), typed panel directories, conductor and raceway identification, junction box color coding, and arc-flash label format. WHY: Labeling is per-device labor and material across hundreds of items and is usually priced as an afterthought. WHERE: 26 05 53.

nameplate_spec.description: Nameplate type and color scheme as written.

typed_directories.description: Typed panel directories required; null if silent.

raceway_marking_text.description: Raceway and conductor identification rules as written.

lighting_fixture_schedule.title: Lighting fixture schedule
lighting_fixture_schedule.description: Every fixture type on the schedule: tag, description, interior, exterior building-mounted or site, source and lumens, watts, voltage, mounting and height, dimming protocol, emergency means, quantity per schedule, a first-pass plan count, and a schedule vs plan mismatch flag. WHY: Lighting is often one of the largest material lines and its own RFQ; schedule-vs-plan count disagreements are among the most common estimating errors, and a clean type list is what makes the lighting package quote comparable. WHERE: Lighting fixture schedule sheet, lighting plans, 26 51 00, 26 56 00, addenda.

source_lumens.description: Source and delivered lumens as printed.

qty_plan_count_first_pass.description: First-pass plan symbol count; never priced without takeoff.

count_mismatch.description: Schedule quantity and plan count disagree.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

lighting_fixture_schedule.x-extraction-notes: Always use the latest addendum schedule. Reconcile the drawing schedule against 26 51 00 and flag types present in one but not the other. Manufacturers, catalog numbers, approved equals and substitution policy go only in specified_products, one row per type when the schedule names them (drawing_tags = type_tag). Plan counts are first-pass estimates for estimator review.
lighting_fixture_schedule.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR Lighting RFQ category and the materials pricing section.

lighting_controls.title: Lighting controls
lighting_controls.description: Control system type by area (standalone sensors and switches, room-based, networked, relay panels, centralized dimming), daylight harvesting, dimming, occupancy or vacancy sensing, BMS integration, whether a sequence of operations is provided, and whether manufacturer startup and programming must be included in the controls package. WHY: Networked controls carry hardware, programming and manufacturer startup far beyond switch-leg wiring; missing that in the Lighting quote is a common miss. WHERE: 26 09 23, 26 09 43, lighting control narrative or sequence of operations, control riser diagram, energy-code compliance sheets.

applies_to.description: Area or building the system covers.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

daylighting.description: Daylight harvesting required; null if silent.

dimming.description: Dimming controls required; null if silent.

bms_integration.description: BMS integration required; null if silent.

factory_startup_programming_required.description: Manufacturer startup and programming required in the package; null if silent.

sequence_of_operations_provided.description: Sequence of operations provided in the documents.

lighting_controls.x-extraction-notes: Drawings often say only 'per 26 09 23'; follow it. Energy-code acceptance and functional testing are testing_commissioning_closeout. Nevada does not use California's Title 24 acceptance-technician program; do not assume CALCTP.
lighting_controls.x-reference-facts: Clark County enforces the 2024 IECC for new permit applications from 2026-01-11.

exterior_site_lighting.title: Exterior and site lighting, poles and photometrics
exterior_site_lighting.description: Site lighting poles by type (count with basis, height, material, base type, base dimensions, delegated foundation design), bollard count, exterior lighting control method, whether a photometric plan is included, and light trespass or dark-sky limits. WHY: Pole bases are concrete and rebar hidden inside the electrical scope, a delegated foundation design adds engineering we would not otherwise expect, and trespass limits can force fixture or pole changes after bid. WHERE: 26 56 00, site lighting plan, pole base details, photometric plan (sometimes a separate consultant PDF), local lighting ordinance notes.

base_dimensions_text.description: Base diameter, depth and reinforcing as printed.

delegated_foundation_design.description: Contractor-designed foundation required; null if silent.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

control_method.description: Exterior lighting control method as written.

photometric_plan_included.description: Photometric plan included in the package.

trespass_or_dark_sky_text.description: Light trespass or dark-sky limits as written.

exterior_site_lighting.x-extraction-notes: Who furnishes and installs pole bases is the scope_responsibility light_pole_bases row; streetlights in the public right-of-way are offsite_electrical_improvements. Fixture types are in lighting_fixture_schedule. Merged from the former photometric_criteria field; per-area footcandle targets were dropped as not pricing-relevant.
exterior_site_lighting.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the BDR Lighting RFQ and the underground pricing section for bases and site feeders.

ceiling_types_by_area.title: Ceiling types by area
ceiling_types_by_area.description: Ceiling type (open structure, lay-in ACT, hard-lid gypsum, specialty or decorative, high bay) and height by area, read from the architectural reflected ceiling plans and room finish schedules. WHY: Hard-lid and high or vaulted ceilings add large labor premiums over lay-in; a labor estimate that assumes lay-in access everywhere underbids resort, hotel and retail interiors. WHERE: Architectural reflected ceiling plans, room finish schedules, building sections.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

ceiling_types_by_area.x-extraction-notes: Electrical sheets rarely state ceiling types; read the A-series RCPs and finish schedules. Record type and height only; the share of fixtures per ceiling type is not extracted because it would rest on symbol counts.
ceiling_types_by_area.x-bdr-overlap: Affects labor pricing (BDR labor_note is the free-text companion).

specified_products.title: Specified products and sourcing
specified_products.description: One list of every Division 26, 27 and 28 product with its basis of design, approved manufacturers, substitution and dealer restrictions, mapped to the BDR RFQ category that should quote it, plus a computed per-category sourcing roll-up.

products.title: Specified products and approved manufacturers
products.description: One row per Division 26, 27 and 28 product or system that names a manufacturer, a basis of design or a performance standard: spec section and title, product type, drawing tags covered, basis of design (manufacturer and model or catalog), approved manufacturers, substitution policy, the section's own prior-approval text when it has one, sole-source, owner-standard or dealer restriction with any named dealer or integrator, and the BDR RFQ category that should quote it. WHY: The manufacturer and substitution rule is the spec fact that best predicts material cost swing; sole-source, dealer-only or closed lists force us to price one vendor, open lists let us shop, and rfq_category lets BDR route the right RFQs without anyone re-reading the spec. WHERE: Part 2 'Manufacturers' article of every Div 26 / 27 / 28 section, fixture and equipment schedules on drawings, 26 05 00 / 01 25 00 / 01 60 00 general product clauses, owner standards, addenda.

value.description: One row per specified product or system.

spec_section.description: Spec section number (e.g., '26 24 16'), or the schedule sheet when the product is only on drawings.

product_type.description: Product or system (e.g., 'panelboards', 'fixture type A1', 'fire alarm control panel').

drawing_tags.description: Drawing tags or fixture types this row covers.

basis_of_design.description: Basis of design; null when none is named.

model_or_catalog.description: Model or catalog number as printed.

approved_manufacturers.description: Every manufacturer named as acceptable, as printed.

section_prior_approval_text.description: Prior-approval deadline or procedure stated in this section itself, when it differs from bid_submission.substitution_prior_approval.

sole_source_or_owner_standard.description: Sole-source, owner-standard, match-existing or dealer restriction.

named_dealer_or_integrator.description: Dealer or integrator named as the only authorized source, when stated.

rfq_category.description: BDR RFQ category that should quote this product.

cite.description: Citation ids for this row.

products.x-extraction-notes: Manufacturers named without 'or equal' language are named_list_closed (status inferred, rule 'named list without or-equal means no substitution'). When a section is silent, apply the governing Div 26 or Div 01 product clause and cite it; if none, not_stated. Qualifiers ('or equal, subject to prior approval') are carried by the enum plus the cited quote; the bid-wide substitution deadline and procedure are bid_submission.substitution_prior_approval. rfq_category maps to BDR material categories: general_material = General Material (wire, conduit, boxes, devices, fittings), switchgear = Switchgear (gear, panels, busway, dry-type transformers), generator_equipment = Generator & Equipment (generators, ATS, UPS), lighting = Lighting (fixtures, lighting controls, poles), low_voltage = Low Voltage (Div 27 / 28), ev_chargers = EV Chargers (EVSE units); lightning protection, PV and similar go to specialty_subcontract. This is the only home for dealer-restricted and proprietary Div 27/28 systems (absorbed from low_voltage_life_safety.proprietary_or_dealer_restricted_systems): extensions of an existing proprietary panel are extend_existing_proprietary, systems only a factory-authorized dealer may supply or program are factory_authorized_dealer_only, closed-protocol devices are closed_protocol_devices. Startup, witness testing, training, warranties and spare parts are joined by spec_section from testing_commissioning_closeout, not repeated here. Addenda often add or remove manufacturers late; the cite points at the addendum.
products.x-bdr-overlap: Drives BDR vendor RFQ categories (General Material, Switchgear, Generator & Equipment, Lighting, Low Voltage, EV Chargers).

sourcing_restriction_by_rfq_category.title: Sourcing restriction by RFQ package
sourcing_restriction_by_rfq_category.description: For each BDR RFQ category the project needs, a roll-up of the products rows: the most restrictive substitution policy, the sections that are closed, sole-source, owner-standard or dealer-restricted, whether a pre-bid prior approval would be needed to use an unnamed vendor, and a rep-control signal computed from the policy and BDR's own RFQ response history for that package. WHY: One flag per package tells the estimator on day one whether the lighting or gear number can be shopped or is locked to one rep or dealer, which changes outreach timing and how much contingency to carry. WHERE: Derived from specified_products.products, scope_responsibility.rfq_category_implications and BDR RFQ history (late, declined or single-source quotes by category).

value.description: One row per RFQ category with products.

most_restrictive_policy.description: Most restrictive substitution policy among this category's rows.

restricted_sections.description: Sections whose policy is basis_of_design_only or named_list_closed.

sole_source_or_dealer_items.description: Products with a sole-source, owner-standard, match-existing or dealer restriction.

prior_approval_needed_to_shop.description: A pre-bid prior approval is needed to price an unnamed vendor.

rep_control_signal.description: Computed from the restriction plus BDR RFQ history for this category; never from model knowledge of local reps.

sourcing_restriction_by_rfq_category.x-extraction-notes: Code computes this; the model does not. Include every RFQ category that has at least one products row, plus categories scope_responsibility.rfq_category_implications marks needed with not_stated policy. Restrictiveness order: basis_of_design_only, named_list_closed, or_equal_with_prior_approval, named_or_equal, performance_spec. rep_control_signal: likely when the policy is basis_of_design_only or named_list_closed and BDR history shows late, declined or single-rep quotes for this category from the named manufacturers; possible when only one of those holds; no_history when BDR has no RFQ history for the category. bid_brief.vendor_pricing_risks reads this field (and long_lead_schedule_check) rather than re-deriving sole-source or rep-controlled status.
sourcing_restriction_by_rfq_category.x-bdr-overlap: Drives BDR vendor RFQ categories and reads BDR rfq_sends reply history.

low_voltage_life_safety.title: Low voltage and life safety systems
low_voltage_life_safety.description: Records, system by system, which Division 27/28 and life-safety systems the bid package contains and what our electrical bid carries for each; the certifications, installer programs and dealer restrictions that can disqualify us or hand pricing to one dealer; the technical requirements that swing low-voltage and fire alarm cost (cable type, pathway, fire alarm design completeness and wiring, ERRCS, two-way communication); and the device and drop counts we benchmark against. Who furnishes, installs and pays lives in scope_responsibility and manufacturers in specified_products; this section records what the systems require. System detail fields carry high or medium priority, and the review queue escalates them to critical when systems_inventory puts that system in our scope (intrusion and mass notification also when project_profile.owner is federal), so reviewers are not swamped on jobs where the system is someone else's.

systems_inventory.title: Low-voltage and life-safety systems and our scope model
systems_inventory.description: One row for every Division 27/28 or life-safety system that appears anywhere in the bid package (structured cabling, wireless LAN, fire alarm, mass notification, ERRCS/BDA, cellular DAS, access control, video surveillance, intrusion, intercom/entry, area-of-refuge two-way communication, emergency call stations, nurse call, paging/sound, AV, master clock, CATV/IPTV, RTLS, guest room management, casino slot data network), with its spec sections, drawing sheets and the one scope model the documents give the electrical bid for it, split by building or area when the model differs. WHY: Shows at a glance which systems we price as full systems, which as cable and pathway, and which as empty conduit and boxes for someone else's vendor. Conduit and backboxes for owner-direct systems is the gap GCs catch most often in bid leveling, and pricing a full install where the documents only ask for rough-in makes us the high number. It decides whether BDR opens the Low Voltage RFQ and pricing section, and it is the switch that escalates this section's detail fields to critical for the systems we actually carry. WHERE: Div 27/28 Part 1 Summary, Work by Others and Related Sections articles; Div 26 05 00 coordination article; T, TY, FA and security sheet series with legends and risers; code summary on the cover sheet; GC scope matrix or bid-package exhibit attached to the invitation (often outside the CSI sections entirely).

anyOf.description: One row per system (and per area when the scope model differs).

system_other_name.description: Name as written when system is other.

applies_to.description: Building, area or phase when the scope model differs within the project; null when project-wide.

spec_sections.description: CSI section numbers that cover the system, e.g. 28 31 00; empty when only drawings or the code sheet mention it.

drawing_sheets.description: Sheet numbers that show the system.

scope_model.description: What the documents ask the electrical bid to carry for this system.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

systems_inventory.x-extraction-notes: Emit a row even for systems marked by others or N.I.C. so their presence is explicit. Trigger words: 'provide empty conduit with pull string and box' = pathway_and_rough_in_only; 'install owner-furnished devices' = install_only_owner_furnished; 'by others' or 'N.I.C.' with no party named = by_others_unspecified. Division 01 'Contractor' usually means the GC, so do not read it as electrical. A missing fire alarm riser does not mean fire alarm is out of scope (design-build fire alarm leaves the riser to the installer). A system that appears only on the code or cover sheet with an empty spec_sections list is the between-the-specs gap signature; keep the row. If a system is shown but no document says who does it, use not_stated so it becomes an RFI or qualification. guest_room_management is keycard energy management and room control units (the line-voltage lighting-control side is wiring_and_lighting.lighting_controls); casino_slot_data_network is slot data system cabling and devices on the gaming floor (slot base power is the scope_responsibility row gaming_equipment_connections). scope_model is the per-system summary of the scope_responsibility.responsibility_matrix low-voltage rows (fire_alarm, structured_cabling, access_control_intrusion, video_surveillance, av_systems, errcs_das, lv_primary_pathway, lv_device_rough_in); a validator checks that they agree, and the furnish, install, terminate and program split lives only in the matrix. If no system appears, return an empty list with the sheet and spec indexes in searched.
systems_inventory.x-bdr-overlap: Feeds the Low Voltage vendor RFQ category, the low_voltage pricing section and the go/no-go scope_fit answer; the per-system scope model is new detail the app does not store.

device_counts.title: Low-voltage device and drop counts
device_counts.description: Counts of low-voltage and fire alarm devices, one row per device type, count source and area: horizontal cable drops, data outlet locations, wireless AP drops, voice drops, cameras, access-controlled doors, card readers (including elevator cab readers), intrusion points, fire alarm initiating devices, notification appliances, modules and power supplies, speakers, nurse call stations, intercom and area-of-refuge stations, ERRCS antennas, guest room controllers and telecom rooms, reconciled to the latest addendum. WHY: These counts drive every low-voltage and fire alarm number we send and are the best cross-project benchmark we have (cost and hours per drop, camera, door and FA device). A count taken from the original set instead of the latest addendum is a clean under- or over-bid. AI symbol counts are a check against the estimator's takeoff, never a priced quantity. WHERE: Device and outlet schedules on T, FA and security sheets; symbol legends and floor plans; FA riser; occasionally a spreadsheet exhibit; addenda reissuing those sheets.

anyOf.description: One row per device type, count source and area.

device_other_name.description: Name as written when device_type is other.

applies_to.description: Building, area, floor, phase or equipment tag this row applies to; null when project-wide.

count.description: Count as shown by this source.

count_source.description: Where the count came from; plan_symbol_count_ai is a first-pass machine count.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

device_counts.x-extraction-notes: Emit no row for a count that is not shown; never estimate. When a schedule total and a plan count disagree, keep both rows (different count_source); code flags the mismatch and never averages. Drops are cables and outlets are locations: when only outlets are shown, record data_outlet_location rows and let code compute drops from outlet_configuration_standard. plan_symbol_count_ai rows are labeled first-pass estimates (vision models count symbols poorly) and never reach pricing without the estimator's takeoff. Reconcile to the latest addendum; a reissued T, FA or security sheet makes earlier counts stale. Per-type detail (camera types, FA interfaces, door device sets) lives in the system fields; quantities_rollup.low_voltage_device_totals reads its totals from here.
device_counts.x-bdr-overlap: None stored today; A7 quantities_rollup.low_voltage_device_totals copies its totals from here.

owner_technology_standards_referenced.title: Owner IT, security or fire alarm standards referenced
owner_technology_standards_referenced.description: Each owner design or technology standard the documents require compliance with (casino or resort corporate IT or surveillance standard, school district, university or hospital system telecom standard, federal agency criteria), the systems it governs, and whether the standard is actually in the bid set. WHY: Cable category, labeling scheme, RCDD requirement, manufacturer lock and camera platform often live in an owner standard nobody attached. Bidding without it means pricing blind while the owner enforces it at submittal; catching it lets us RFI for the document or write a qualification before bid day. WHERE: Div 27/28 Part 1 References and Quality Assurance articles; Div 01 references; general notes on T and security sheets; invitation attachments.

anyOf.description: One row per owner standard referenced.

standard_name.description: Title as written, or the phrase used (e.g. 'Owner's IT Standards').

issuer.description: Owner, operator or agency that issues the standard.

included_in_bid_set.description: Whether the standard itself is in the package.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

owner_technology_standards_referenced.x-extraction-notes: Record the standard even when the spec says only 'per Owner's standards'. Do not infer what an unattached standard requires. Every row with referenced_not_included must also appear in document_control.referenced_documents_not_provided (validator), which drives the request. Gaming surveillance rules that come from regulation rather than the owner are flagged in video_surveillance_system.regulated_surveillance.
owner_technology_standards_referenced.x-bdr-overlap: Relates to go/no-go owner_type; no stored field for owner standards.

system_power_provisions.title: Power and backup for low-voltage and life-safety equipment
system_power_provisions.description: Circuits, power equipment and backup the documents require for low-voltage and life-safety equipment (FACP, NAC extender panels, BDA and battery cabinets, access control and lock power supplies, telecom room receptacles and UPS circuits, AV racks, nurse call head-ends, security head-ends): circuit count, voltage, power source (normal, emergency, standby, UPS), breaker lock or marking, whether a matching circuit is on the panel schedules, and the stated battery or UPS backup type and runtime. WHY: These circuits often appear only on T, FA or security sheets or in Division 28 text, not on the panel schedules we price homeruns from; NAC extender counts grow with delegated FA design, anything on an emergency branch adds generator and ATS load, and long security backup runtimes need larger UPS and battery banks. Missing them is unpriced copper, labor and equipment. WHERE: Division 28 Part 2 power supply and power requirement articles (28 13 00, 28 16 00, 28 23 00, 28 31 00); FA riser; enlarged MDF/IDF plans; BDA details; panel schedules for cross-check.

system_power_provisions.x-extraction-notes: Cross-check each row against power_distribution.panelboard_schedule and set on_panel_schedule no where no matching circuit exists; those rows are the gaps. Runtime and backup type only as stated, never a default; code-set standby durations attach from the reference table, not here. ERRCS battery runtime lives in errcs_design_and_acceptance (leave backup_runtime_hours null on errcs_bda rows); central UPS systems themselves are power_distribution.ups_and_central_inverters. Absorbs the former security_backup_power field.

certified_installer_programs.title: Manufacturer certified-installer programs and the system warranties that require them
certified_installer_programs.description: For each system (copper and fiber cabling, fire alarm, access control, video, nurse call, ERRCS), any requirement that the installer be a manufacturer-certified, accredited or factory-authorized partner, stated outright or implied by a required manufacturer system warranty: manufacturer, program, tier, the warranty term and type that drive the tier, when proof is due, minimum certified staff on site, and any local service office requirement. WHY: If G3 is not in the named program we cannot issue the specified warranty, so the bid is nonconforming or we pay a partner sub. Joining takes time, so this is a go/no-go gate that must surface before estimating hours are spent. Specs often never say 'certified installer' and imply it through a 15 to 25 year channel or application warranty; bidding a lower tier than the warranty needs is nonconforming, and a higher tier overprices us. WHERE: Part 1 Qualifications and Warranty articles of 27 10 00 / 27 15 00, 27 13 00, 28 31 00, 28 13 00, 28 23 00 and 27 52 23; Part 2 Manufacturers; manufacturer program named in the warranty clause; prequalification questionnaires.

anyOf.description: One row per system and manufacturer program required.

program_name.description: Program name as written, e.g. a certified installer or partner program.

tier_required.description: Program tier or level as written.

system_warranty_type.description: Type of manufacturer system warranty required.

proof_due.description: When proof of certification is due.

min_certified_staff_onsite.description: Stated minimum certified staff on site, as written.

local_service_office.description: Stated local service office or response requirement, as written.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

certified_installer_programs.x-extraction-notes: implied_by_system_warranty applies the named inference rule 'a 15 to 25 year cabling system warranty implies a manufacturer-certified installer'; name the rule in the envelope note. Record the warranty term only as written (15, 20 or 25 are all common; never default). The brand in the warranty clause can differ from the drawings or bill of materials and addenda swap it; use the latest and log the disagreement as a conflict. Collect from the Part 1 Qualifications and Warranty articles of every Division 27/28 section, not only Division 01. Approved manufacturers and substitution policy live in specified_products.products; the general warranty in contract_terms; other equipment warranties in testing_commissioning_closeout.extended_warranties; warranty registration paperwork is a row in testing_commissioning_closeout.closeout_deliverables_checklist. G3's program status is company data compared by rule, never extracted. Return an empty list with the sections in searched when none. Absorbs the former cabling_system_warranty field.

proprietary_or_dealer_restricted_systems.title: Proprietary or dealer-restricted systems
proprietary_or_dealer_restricted_systems.description: Systems that can only be bought, programmed or serviced through one manufacturer's authorized dealer or a single named integrator: sole-source fire alarm panels, extensions of an existing proprietary panel, owner-standard access control or VMS platforms, proprietary nurse call, campus-standard systems and closed-protocol devices, with the restriction type and any dealer or integrator the documents name. WHY: When one dealer controls the equipment, that dealer sets our price or refuses to quote us while favoring another bidder. Knowing it early decides whether we bid the system, carry an allowance or qualify it, and stops us from pricing a brand we cannot buy. WHERE: Part 2 Manufacturers articles in 28 31 00, 28 13 00, 28 23 00, 27 52 23; 'no substitutions' or 'match existing' language; addenda narrowing or-equal lists; owner standards.

anyOf.description: One row per restricted system.

manufacturer_or_platform.description: Manufacturer or platform label that links to the specified_products row.

restriction_type.description: How supply, programming or service is restricted.

named_dealer_or_integrator.description: Dealer or integrator named in the documents; null when not named.

applies_to.description: Building, area, floor, phase or equipment tag this row applies to; null when project-wide.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

proprietary_or_dealer_restricted_systems.x-extraction-notes: Record only systems where the restriction limits who can supply, program or service. The approved-manufacturer list, basis of design and or-equal policy live in specified_products.products; a validator checks that the linked products row shows sole_source, owner_standard or match_existing. Fill named_dealer_or_integrator only from the documents, never from market knowledge of who the local dealer is. An existing proprietary panel that must be extended also appears in existing_fire_alarm_conditions with approach extend_existing. An addendum that removes 'or equal' in favor of one brand is a strong signal. Return an empty list with the sections in searched when none.

cabling_installer_qualifications.title: Structured cabling RCDD and installer credentials
cabling_installer_qualifications.description: Whether a BICSI RCDD is required and in what role (on the installing contractor's staff, to sign submittals, shop drawings or test reports, or on the design team only); BICSI credentials required of the cabling foreman, installers, technicians or test personnel; manufacturer training; and minimum experience required of the cabling installer. WHY: An RCDD requirement on the installer that G3 cannot meet in house either disqualifies the bid or forces a paid consultant just to sign documents, and crew credentials we lack mean training, certifying or hiring before mobilizing. Both are priced or qualified before bid day or they become margin loss. WHERE: 27 05 00 Part 1 Quality Assurance / Qualifications; warranty article; owner design standards (university, hospital, government, casino IT).

rcdd_requirement.description: Role in which a BICSI RCDD is required.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

bicsi_requirements.description: One row per role and BICSI credential required.

manufacturer_training_required.description: True when installers must hold manufacturer training.

min_experience.description: Stated cabling-installer experience requirement, as written.

cabling_installer_qualifications.x-extraction-notes: RCDD is a design credential and BICSI installer levels are crew credentials; never conflate them. An RCDD requirement is often silent in the base spec and imposed by an owner standard or a warranty tier; cross-check owner_technology_standards_referenced and certified_installer_programs, but set rcdd_requirement from text only (not_stated when silent). Firm-wide minimums (years in business, similar projects) are bid_submission.qualification_minimums. Review-queue escalation: treat as critical when systems_inventory gives structured_cabling a scope_model of full_turnkey, cable_and_pathway_only or install_only_owner_furnished. Absorbs the former rcdd_requirement field.

fire_alarm_personnel_qualifications.title: Fire alarm designer and technician qualifications
fire_alarm_personnel_qualifications.description: Qualifications the documents require for the fire alarm designer (NICET Fire Alarm level, or a Nevada PE accepted instead), the installing, programming and testing technicians (NICET level or factory training), State Fire Marshal certificate of registration for installers, a certificate holder on site, and on-site supervision. WHY: Without a qualified designer we cannot self-perform delegated fire alarm design and must sub it out; without qualified or registered technicians we must price outside labor. The State Fire Marshal layer (firm license, per-installer registration, a certificate holder on every site) is a staffing and disqualification risk that NICET levels alone do not capture. WHERE: 28 31 00 / 28 31 11 Part 1 Quality Assurance / Qualifications; local fire code amendments.

designer_nicet_level.description: Minimum NICET Fire Alarm Systems level for whoever prepares the design or shop drawings.

designer_pe_accepted.description: True when a Nevada PE is stated as acceptable in place of the NICET level.

technician_nicet_level.description: Minimum NICET level for installing, programming or testing technicians.

technician_nicet_applies_to.description: Which technicians the NICET level applies to.

factory_trained_alternative.description: True when manufacturer factory training is accepted instead of NICET.

sfm_certificate_of_registration_required.description: State Fire Marshal certificate of registration as stated in the documents.

certificate_holder_onsite_required.description: True when the documents require a registered certificate holder on site.

supervision_requirement.description: Stated on-site supervision requirement, as written.

anyOf.description: Fire alarm personnel requirements as stated in this project's documents.

fire_alarm_personnel_qualifications.x-extraction-notes: Capture whichever qualification path the spec allows (NICET, PE, factory-trained, or NFPA 72 qualification language, quoted) so the field does not over-flag. Record SFM registration and an on-site certificate holder only when the documents state them; the statewide NAC 477.300 rule attaches from the reference table and is never written into this value. The delegated-design stamp is scope_responsibility.delegated_design_items; NSCB classifications (C-2, C-2c, C-41) are bid_submission.required_license_classifications. Review-queue escalation: treat as critical when systems_inventory gives fire_alarm a scope_model of full_turnkey, cable_and_pathway_only or install_only_owner_furnished.
fire_alarm_personnel_qualifications.x-reference-facts: NAC 477.300 (Nevada State Fire Marshal): a firm that installs or services fire alarm or detection systems needs an SFM license; each employee doing the work needs an SFM certificate of registration; a certificate holder must be on every job site and directly supervise unregistered workers; fire alarm designers must hold NICET Level II (or equivalent) or a Nevada PE license. This is on top of the NSCB license (C-2, C-2c or C-41/C-41c). Attached by rule whenever systems_inventory puts fire_alarm in our scope (full_turnkey, cable_and_pathway_only or install_only_owner_furnished).

horizontal_cable_category.title: Horizontal cable type by use (category, shielding, jacket)
horizontal_cable_category.description: Required copper horizontal cable by use and area: category (Cat5e, Cat6, Cat6A), shielded or unshielded, and jacket rating (plenum, riser, general purpose, indoor/outdoor or wet location for underground or exterior runs); the plenum rule; and the spaces the documents identify as return-air plenums. WHY: Cat6A costs materially more than Cat6 in cable, connectors, pull labor and pathway fill; missing a Cat6A requirement for APs or cameras is a common under-bid, and pricing 6A everywhere when only some drops need it loses the job. Shielded cable adds shield bonding and termination labor, plenum jacket where it is not needed overbids, riser jacket where plenum is required fails inspection, and wet-location cable for underground runs is easy to miss. WHERE: 27 15 00 / 27 15 13 Part 2 Products; outlet and cabling schedules and notes on T sheets (including notes near switchgear, generator, elevator and imaging rooms); mechanical drawings and RCPs for return-air plenum ceilings; site plans for exterior devices; addenda.

cable_types.description: One row per distinct cable requirement by use and area.

use.description: Use the requirement applies to; default is the general rule.

use_other.description: Use as written when use is other.

applies_to.description: Area, room type or run (e.g. 'near switchgear', 'underground to site devices'); null when everywhere.

shielding.description: Whether shielded (F/UTP, S/FTP) cable is required.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

return_air_plenum_spaces.description: Spaces identified as return-air plenums, as stated on M or A sheets.

anyOf.description: Horizontal copper cable requirements.

horizontal_cable_category.x-extraction-notes: Emit a default row for the general rule and extra rows only where use or area differs (APs, cameras, rooms near switchgear, generator or elevator rooms, imaging suites, underground or exterior runs). Owners often upgrade to 6A by addendum after IT review; check the latest addendum, the outlet schedule and T-sheet notes, not only the narrative spec. Area-specific shielding and wet-location notes often appear only as a sheet note near a room. Whether a ceiling is a return-air plenum is a mechanical or architectural fact; read the M sheets (ceiling types themselves are wiring_and_lighting.ceiling_types_by_area). When cable runs through underground or below-slab raceway and no jacket rule is stated for it, add a row for that run with jacket_rating not_stated so it becomes an RFI; do not infer. Review-queue escalation: treat as critical when systems_inventory gives structured_cabling a scope_model of full_turnkey, cable_and_pathway_only or install_only_owner_furnished. Absorbs the former copper_cable_shielding and cable_jacket_rating fields.

outlet_configuration_standard.title: Typical outlet makeup (cables per outlet)
outlet_configuration_standard.description: The standard makeup of each outlet symbol or type: cables per outlet, jack color and faceplate, including special outlets (wireless AP, camera, floor box, wall phone, AV). WHY: Drop counts are usually outlet symbols times cables per outlet; a two-cable versus three-cable typical outlet swings cable, jacks, patch panel ports and labor by half again. Getting the multiplier right is the difference between a correct and a badly wrong low-voltage number. WHERE: T sheet symbol legend and outlet schedule; typical outlet details; 27 15 00 Part 3 Execution.

outlet_configuration_standard.x-extraction-notes: Legend symbols often encode the count (a triangle with a number); read the legend text literally. A disagreement between the legend and the typical outlet detail is an envelope conflict. Cable category by use lives in horizontal_cable_category; code multiplies outlet counts from device_counts by cables_per_outlet to compute drops.

backbone_cabling.title: Backbone and campus cabling
backbone_cabling.description: Fiber backbone segments between MDF and IDFs and between buildings (fiber type, strand count, connector, armored or innerduct, splice or field termination), copper multipair riser pair counts, and whether outside-plant cabling leaves the building. WHY: Singlemode versus multimode, strand counts and connector style change material and termination labor significantly, and strand counts usually appear only on the riser diagram; a missed segment or campus run is unpriced scope. WHERE: 27 13 00 / 27 13 23 Part 2; telecom riser diagram (often the only place strand counts appear); site telecom plans.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

anyOf.description: Backbone cabling requirements.

backbone_cabling.x-extraction-notes: Take strand counts from the riser diagram, not the narrative spec. Campus duct banks are wiring_and_lighting.duct_bank_encasement and underground_raceway_installation; telecom entrance conduit runs are trench segments in power_distribution.site_electrical; carrier entrance and demarc extension responsibility is the scope_responsibility row telecom_carrier_entrance. Absorbs the useful part of the former telecom_service_entrance field (outside-plant cabling).

telecom_pathway_method.title: Telecom pathway method and limits
telecom_pathway_method.description: Horizontal low-voltage pathway method by area (J-hooks, conduit throughout, conduit stub to accessible ceiling, cable tray, basket tray, surface raceway, open cabling in exposed ceilings), J-hook spacing and maximum cables per support, minimum drop conduit size, fill limit, and sleeve requirements through rated walls. WHY: G3 carries low-voltage pathway on most jobs even when the cabling is by others, so this hits nearly every bid. Conduit and tray cost far more material and labor than J-hooks; a spec requiring conduit in clinical, secure or exposed areas that we price as J-hooks is a large margin loss, and spacing, fill and size rules set the whole support takeoff. WHERE: 27 05 28 Pathways for Communications Systems Part 2 and Part 3; T sheet notes and typical details; owner standards.

anyOf.description: Low-voltage pathway requirements.

Clinical, secure, exposed and inaccessible areas often require conduit; give each its own row. telecom_room_fitout.description: Telecom rooms by type (MDF, IDF, entrance facility, equipment room) with count and fit-out: open racks versus enclosed cabinets (count, rack units), ladder rack, rack PDUs and room UPS. WHY: Enclosed cabinets with PDUs and UPS cost far more than open two-post racks and add dedicated circuits; room fit-out is commonly under-scoped when the takeoff looks only at cable. WHERE: 27 11 00 / 27 11 16 Communications Equipment Room Fittings Part 2; enlarged MDF/IDF plans and rack elevations.

patch_cords_and_equipment_cords.description: Whether the cabling spec includes patch and equipment cords or states the owner furnishes them, the quantity basis, which ends (closet, workstation or both), and lengths and colors. telecom_grounding_bonding.description: Required telecom bonding infrastructure: primary and secondary bonding busbars (TMGB/TGB or PBB/SBB) per room, bonding backbone conductor size, and bonding of racks, cabinets and tray to the building electrical ground. telecom_labeling_administration.description: Required TIA-606 administration class, any owner labeling scheme, machine-printed labels, and the cabling documentation deliverable (cable database, spreadsheet, CAD records). cabling_field_testing.description: Share of copper links to be certified, test configuration (permanent link or channel) and standard, fiber test tier (loss only or loss plus OTDR) and standard, native tester file requirement, and owner witness. fire_alarm_system.title: Fire alarm system type, completeness of the bid design and spare capacity
fire_alarm_system.description: Fire alarm architecture (conventional, addressable, addressable with voice evacuation, wireless or hybrid), networked panel count, FACP and annunciator locations, high-rise features (fire command center, firefighter telephones, smoke control panel), how complete the fire alarm design on the bid drawings is (devices and riser shown, devices only, riser only, or performance spec only), and the spare capacity the spec requires on loops, circuits, power supplies, amplifiers and batteries. WHY: Voice evacuation panels, amplifiers and speakers cost far more than a basic addressable system. When the bid drawings show no devices or riser, the device, panel and power-supply counts come from our own design and grow after award. Spare-capacity percentages have no code analog and add loops, NAC extenders, amplifiers and battery size. Missing any of these is a large hit on the fire alarm number. WHERE: 28 31 00 / 28 31 11 Part 1 Summary, Design Requirements, Delegated Design and Submittals articles and Part 2 panel, power supply and amplifier articles; fire alarm plans and riser (or their absence); code analysis on the cover sheet; Division 01 delegated design article.

networked_panel_count.description: Networked FACPs or nodes shown or specified.

high_rise_features.description: High-rise and fire command features required.

bid_drawing_completeness.description: How much of the fire alarm design the bid drawings show.

spare_other.description: Requirement as written when not a percentage (e.g. 'one spare NAC per panel').

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

anyOf.description: Fire alarm system type and design basis.

fire_alarm_system.x-extraction-notes: 'Contractor shall provide complete engineered shop drawings' with no devices on the plans is performance_spec_only even without a Delegated Design heading. A missing riser does not mean fire alarm is out of scope. Voice requirements sometimes appear only on the riser or code sheet; record what is stated and never infer voice from occupancy (project_profile.building_type holds occupancy). Who designs, the design level and the stamp are scope_responsibility.delegated_design_items (fire_alarm row); a validator checks that performance_spec_only agrees with a delegated design row there. Spare-capacity percentages hide in Part 2 panel and power supply articles; record them literally, never a habitual 20 or 25 percent. Standby battery duration, when stated, is a fire_alarm row in system_power_provisions. Envelope not_applicable only when no fire alarm work appears in the package. Replaces the former fire_alarm_system_type and fire_alarm_design_basis fields.

fire_alarm_wiring_requirements.title: Fire alarm wiring class, survivability and raceway
fire_alarm_wiring_requirements.description: Circuit class by circuit type (SLC, NAC, speaker, network or riser), pathway survivability level, required cable type (FPLP, 2-hour circuit-integrity cable, MI cable, standard cable in a rated enclosure), whether fire alarm wiring must be in conduit everywhere, only where exposed or inaccessible, or may be open cable, and red identification of boxes, conduit or jacket. WHY: Class A return loops roughly double circuit wiring, survivability can require rated cable that costs many times standard FPLP, and all-in-conduit fire alarm versus open plenum cable is one of the largest labor swings in the fire alarm number. WHERE: 28 31 00 Part 2 Wiring and Part 3 Installation; FA riser notes; general FA notes.

applies_to.description: Building, area or riser the row applies to; null when project-wide.

cite.description: Envelope citation ids supporting this row.

conduit_rule_detail.description: Exceptions or area detail for the conduit rule, as written.

red_identification.description: Red identification required on boxes, conduit or jacket, as written.

anyOf.description: Fire alarm wiring requirements.

fire_alarm_wiring_requirements.x-extraction-notes: Quote circuit class and survivability exactly; never infer them from building height or occupancy. Add a row per circuit type when classes differ (for example Class A SLC and Class B NAC). Review-queue escalation: treat as critical when systems_inventory gives fire_alarm a scope_model of full_turnkey or cable_and_pathway_only and conduit_rule is all_in_conduit or any row requires circuit-integrity or MI cable.

fire_alarm_interfaces.title: Fire alarm interfaces and sequence of operations
fire_alarm_interfaces.description: Monitoring and control points the fire alarm must provide, from the sequence of operations matrix and other trades' schedules: sprinkler waterflow and tamper, fire pump, elevator recall and shunt trip, duct smoke detectors, fire/smoke dampers, smoke control or stair pressurization, door holders, access control release, HVAC shutdown, kitchen hood suppression, generator or ATS status and releasing panels, with counts where shown. WHY: Every interface is a module, relay and homerun, and many appear only on the sequence matrix or on mechanical drawings (damper and duct detector counts).
