infrared_scan_required.description: Whether infrared scanning is required at or after energization.

infrared_rescan_after.description: Time after the stated trigger for a second infrared scan.

infrared_rescan_text.description: Rescan requirement as written, e.g. '11 months after substantial completion'.

report_recipients_text.description: Who receives test reports, as written.

independent_acceptance_testing.x-extraction-notes: When the spec says only 'NETA' with no standard, record neta_unspecified and set verify_action rfi asking which standard governs. Keep manufacturer startup (manufacturer_startup_services), AHJ inspections and structural special inspections out of this field. Individual tests by system are field_testing_requirements; infrared scanning is recorded only here. Who retains and pays the testing agency is scope_responsibility row neta_acceptance_testing; never assume the owner pays because special inspections usually are. Relay and breaker settings from the coordination study are power_distribution.power_system_studies.
independent_acceptance_testing.x-reference-facts: NETA publishes separate ANSI standards that specs often conflate: ATS (acceptance testing of new equipment before energization), MTS (periodic maintenance testing) and ECS (electrical commissioning, system level), plus a separate technician certification standard. ANSI/NETA ATS has a 2025 edition.

field_testing_requirements.title: Required field tests by system
field_testing_requirements.description: Every field test the specs require of electrical work, per system: insulation resistance, torque checks, ground resistance, ground-fault protection performance, breaker and relay testing, VLF or hi-pot on medium-voltage cable, generator load bank and run tests, transfer switch tests, UPS and battery tests, lighting controls functional tests, emergency lighting duration tests; with standard, extent, witness and who performs it. WHY: Each test is labor, rental equipment or a subcontract (load banks, VLF sets), and load bank duration and witness rules alone can swing a generator package; listing them lets estimators price them and confirm vendor quotes include them. WHERE: Part 3 'Field Quality Control' or 'Testing' articles of every Division 26 section, 26 08 00, generator, transfer switch, UPS and lighting control sections, 01 91 00, energy-code notes on the lighting sheets.

spec_section.description: CSI section that requires the test.

extent_text.description: Extent, load steps, duration or sample size as written, e.g. '4 hours at full nameplate load'.

witness_required.description: Whether the owner, engineer, CxA or AHJ must witness.

performed_by.description: Who the spec says performs the test.

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

field_testing_requirements.x-extraction-notes: One row per system and test type. Infrared scanning is independent_acceptance_testing; fire alarm acceptance testing and structured cabling certification are low_voltage_life_safety; grounding resistance targets and equipment configuration are power_distribution and wiring_and_lighting. Energy-code lighting controls functional testing can apply on non-LEED work; record it whenever the spec or code notes call for it.
field_testing_requirements.x-reference-facts: Clark County (permit applications from January 11, 2026) and the City of Las Vegas (from January 5, 2026) enforce the 2024 IECC with Southern Nevada amendments; the edition cited on the drawings is project_profile.code_editions.

retest_and_failed_test_terms.title: Retest and failed-test cost terms
retest_and_failed_test_terms.description: How the documents treat failed tests: how many retests are free, the rate billed for later retests by the CxA, testing agency or inspector, any cap, and whether a testing allowance excludes retesting after failure. WHY: A clause billing us for the second retest makes repeated deficiencies cost the CxA's or agency's time on top of rework, and allowance-covered testing still leaves first-failure retests with us. WHERE: 01 91 00 Commissioning (Deficiencies / Retesting), 01 45 00 Quality Control, 01 21 00 Allowances, 26 08 00.

retest_billing_terms_text.description: Retest billing terms and any cap as written.

allowance_excludes_retesting.description: Whether a testing allowance excludes retests after failure.

retest_and_failed_test_terms.x-extraction-notes: Who pays retests is scope_responsibility row retest_costs; the testing allowance line and amount are bid_submission.allowances. Record here only the retest count, rate and terms. Treat allowance-covered testing as still carrying first-failure risk.

factory_witness_testing.title: Factory witness testing
factory_witness_testing.description: Factory acceptance tests the owner, engineer or CxA must witness at the manufacturer's plant (switchgear, generators, UPS, paralleling gear), with number of witnesses and days. WHY: Witnessed factory tests add travel cost for several owner representatives and can add weeks to gear release; the vendor quote or the gear number must carry them. WHERE: Part 2 'Source Quality Control' or 'Factory Tests' articles of switchgear, switchboard, generator, UPS and paralleling gear sections.

spec_section.description: CSI section that requires the test.

duration.description: Length of the witnessed test when stated.

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

factory_witness_testing.x-extraction-notes: Distinguish witnessed factory tests from standard production tests that need only a certified report. Whether G3 or the vendor pays witness travel and lodging is a scope_responsibility row (item_code other, factory_witness_travel), not recorded here.
factory_witness_testing.x-bdr-overlap: Check against the Switchgear and Generator & Equipment vendor RFQ quotes.

manufacturer_startup_services.title: Manufacturer startup and field services
manufacturer_startup_services.description: Manufacturer field representative services the specs require (startup, installation inspection, certification letters, programming, settings) for switchgear, generators, transfer switches, UPS, lighting controls and similar equipment, with number of visits or days. WHY: These are normally in vendor quotes only when the RFQ asks for them; listing them lets us confirm the gear, generator and lighting quotes include startup and site visits, and keeps vendor startup separate from formal commissioning. WHERE: Part 3 'Startup Service', 'Manufacturer's Field Service' or 'Field Quality Control' articles of Division 26 equipment and lighting controls sections.

spec_section.description: CSI section that requires the service.

visits_or_days_text.description: Number of visits or days as written.

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

manufacturer_startup_services.x-extraction-notes: Record the service as the spec states it; do not assume a vendor includes it. Generator startup and load bank responsibility is scope_responsibility row generator_startup_load_bank.
manufacturer_startup_services.x-bdr-overlap: Supports BDR vendor RFQ categories (Switchgear, Generator & Equipment, Lighting): each row should be confirmed as included in the matching vendor quote.

commissioning_level.title: Commissioning level and electrical participation
commissioning_level.description: Whether formal commissioning applies to electrical systems or only normal startup (none, startup only, fundamental, enhanced), the basis cited (LEED, owner requirements, ASHRAE guideline), who the commissioning authority is, and what G3 must do (prefunctional checklists, functional test support, Cx meetings, issues-log updates, systems manual input). WHY: Formal Cx participation is the MEP scope GCs most often find excluded when leveling: subs price startup but not Cx hours, meetings and functional test support. Getting it right avoids a leveling gap and avoids giving away unpriced hours. WHERE: 01 91 00 / 01 91 13 General Commissioning Requirements, 26 08 00 Commissioning of Electrical Systems, Owner's Project Requirements, LEED requirements in 01 81 00.

basis_as_written.description: Commissioning basis cited, e.g. 'LEED v4.1 Enhanced Commissioning' or 'Owner's Project Requirements'.

contractor_duties.description: Duties the documents assign to the electrical contractor.

cx_software_as_written.description: Required commissioning software or platform as written.

commissioning_level.x-extraction-notes: Cx often lives entirely in Division 01; read 01 91 00 even when Division 26 is silent. LEED enhanced Cx implies CxA submittal review plus systems manual and training verification. Systems in scope go in commissioned_electrical_systems; Cx meeting frequency in meetings_and_reporting; who hires the CxA and whether our participation is in our price is scope_responsibility row commissioning_cx.

commissioned_electrical_systems.title: Commissioned electrical systems and deferred testing
commissioned_electrical_systems.description: The electrical systems in the Cx scope (switchgear and distribution, generator and ATS, UPS, lighting controls, metering, PV and BESS, fire alarm and BAS interfaces), whether each needs functional performance testing, any seasonal, deferred or post-occupancy testing, and any warranty-period review months after substantial completion. WHY: Deferred or seasonal tests and end-of-warranty reviews force a remobilization, sometimes with a factory technician, after we have left; if the estimate assumes Cx ends at closeout that cost is lost. WHERE: 01 91 00 Commissioning plan or systems list, 26 08 00, Commissioning Plan exhibit, each Division 26 system's Commissioning or Field Quality Control article.

fpt_required.description: Whether functional performance testing is required.

deferred_or_seasonal.description: Whether testing is deferred, seasonal or post-occupancy.

timing_text.description: When the testing happens, as written.

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

systems.description: Electrical systems in the Cx scope.

warranty_period_review_required.description: Whether a warranty-period or end-of-warranty review is required.

warranty_review_after.description: When the warranty-period review happens after substantial completion.

commissioned_electrical_systems.x-extraction-notes: The process is in 01 91 00 but the system list is often only in Division 26 sections or the Cx plan; cross-reference both. Fire alarm acceptance testing itself is low_voltage_life_safety; here only its Cx interface.

sustainability_certification_documentati.title: Green certification and waste diversion documentation
sustainability_certification_documentati.description: Whether the project targets LEED or another green rating (and level), and the electrical documentation it triggers: construction waste diversion percentage with scrap separation and weight tickets, product documentation (recycled content, EPDs), and energy-code compliance forms. WHY: Green certification adds documentation labor, separated scrap handling and CxA coordination that uncertified jobs do not have, and missing reports can hold final payment. WHERE: 01 81 00 Sustainable Design Requirements, 01 74 19 Construction Waste Management, 01 91 00, LEED scorecard on the cover or G-series sheets.

rating_version_as_written.description: Rating version as written, e.g. 'LEED v4.1 BD+C'.

scrap_separation_and_reporting.description: Whether scrap separation and weight-ticket reporting are required.

energy_code_forms_required.description: Whether lighting energy-code compliance forms are required from the contractor.

sustainability_certification_documentati.x-extraction-notes: The Cx level that LEED drives is recorded in commissioning_level; here record the target and the documentation burden. Capture only a stated diversion percentage, never a default.

extended_warranties.title: System and extended warranties
extended_warranties.description: Warranties longer than or different from the general contract warranty for specific electrical and low-voltage equipment or systems (generators, UPS and batteries, LED fixtures and drivers, lighting controls, switchgear, PV and BESS, surge devices, structured cabling system warranties): term, coverage, whether it must be a manufacturer warranty, any different start trigger, and registration deliverables and deadline. WHY: Extended manufacturer warranties are quotable costs per item (a multi-year comprehensive generator warranty is real money), and a structured cabling system warranty sets the certified-installer tier and testing rigor we must price; bidding a lower tier is nonconforming and a missed registration voids a warranty we promised. WHERE: Part 1 'Warranty' or 'Special Warranty' articles of each Division 26, 27 and 28 section (generators, UPS, lighting, lighting controls, SPD, PV, structured cabling), 01 78 36 Warranties.

spec_section.description: CSI section that requires the warranty.

term.description: Warranty term as written (years or months).

coverage.description: Coverage; the cabling_ values are structured cabling warranty types.

manufacturer_warranty_required.description: Whether it must be the manufacturer's warranty.

start_trigger_as_written.description: Start trigger verbatim, only when it differs from the general warranty start.

registration_deliverables.description: Deliverables that activate the warranty, e.g. 100 percent test results, as-builts, registration package.

registration_deadline_text.description: Registration deadline as written; null when the spec defers to the manufacturer.

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

extended_warranties.x-extraction-notes: The general contract warranty period and start trigger are contract_terms. This field is the single owner of system warranties, including structured cabling manufacturer system warranties (moved from low_voltage_life_safety.cabling_system_warranty); low_voltage_life_safety.certified_installer_programs.implied_by_warranty reads these rows. Do not default to 25 years for cabling; some projects require 15 or 20. If the spec says 'per manufacturer requirements', record that text and leave the deadline null. Capture a different start trigger verbatim.
extended_warranties.x-bdr-overlap: None stored; check each row against the Generator & Equipment, Lighting and low-voltage vendor quotes.

post_completion_service_obligations.title: Post-completion maintenance and service obligations
post_completion_service_obligations.description: Service the contractor must provide after substantial completion beyond warranty repair: preventive maintenance visits (generators, UPS), fuel top-off after testing, lighting controls software support and updates, warranty call response times, and end-of-warranty walkthroughs. WHY: Generator and UPS specs often require scheduled maintenance for a period after acceptance, and resorts and hospitals demand fast warranty response; these recurring costs come after our crews leave and must be carried or quoted by the vendor. WHERE: Part 1 'Maintenance Service' or 'Warranty' articles of generator, UPS and lighting controls sections, 01 78 36 Warranties, 01 91 00.

spec_section.description: CSI section that requires the service.

response_time_text.description: Required response time verbatim, e.g. 'on site within 4 hours'.

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

post_completion_service_obligations.x-extraction-notes: Capture response times verbatim; they drive on-call cost. Warranty terms themselves are extended_warranties.

attic_stock_spare_parts.title: Attic stock, spare parts and extra materials
attic_stock_spare_parts.description: Extra materials turned over to the owner at closeout, by item and spec section: spare lamps, drivers and fixtures, fuses, loose breakers, devices and cover plates, keys, touch-up paint, wire and other maintenance materials, stated as counts or as a percent of installed quantity with any minimum. WHY: Attic stock is pure extra material with no code trigger, scattered across product sections, and often a condition of final payment; missing it is a straight margin loss and a payment delay. WHERE: Part 1 'Maintenance Material Submittals' or 'Extra Materials' articles of each Division 26, 27 and 28 product section (lighting, fuses, panelboards, wiring devices), plus 01 78 00 Closeout Submittals.

quantity_basis.description: What the quantity is measured against.

minimum_count.description: Stated minimum, e.g. 'but not less than 2 of each type'.

unit_as_written.description: Unit as written (each, box, carton, foot).

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

attic_stock_spare_parts.x-extraction-notes: Scan every product section's closeout article, not only Division 01; requirements are usually split across both. Keep percentages as stated; the takeoff resolves them to counts. Installed spare breakers and spaces in panels are power_distribution, not attic stock.

record_drawings.title: Record drawings (as-builts)
record_drawings.description: Required as-built format (field redlines, PDF markups, CAD, BIM model), update frequency during construction, whether a current as-built set is a condition of monthly payments, and how underground conduit must be located (survey, GPS coordinates or dimensioned redlines). WHY: CAD or model as-builts and surveyed underground records are real drafting and survey cost compared with redlines, and progress-payment gating can stall cash flow mid-job. WHERE: 01 78 39 Project Record Documents, 01 77 00 Closeout Procedures, 26 05 00 Common Work Results, underground raceway sections.

update_frequency_text.description: How often as-builts must be updated, as written.

current_set_required_for_progress_paymen.description: Whether a current as-built set is a condition of monthly payment.

underground_location_method.description: How underground runs must be located.

record_drawings.x-extraction-notes: BIM-model as-builts are not equivalent to redlines. The final due date and any retention or final-payment gate are closeout_deliverables_checklist rows (deliverable record_drawings).

owner_training.title: Owner training and demonstration
owner_training.description: Required training of owner staff per system (generator, switchgear, lighting controls, UPS, metering): hours or sessions, whether a manufacturer representative must deliver it, video recording, and training plan submittals. WHY: Manufacturer-led training carries rep and travel cost, and installer-led sessions pull a foreman back after demobilization; unbudgeted training is a small but repeating margin leak. WHERE: 01 79 00 Demonstration and Training, 'Demonstration' articles of Division 26 system sections, 01 91 00.

spec_section.description: CSI section that requires the training.

recording_required.description: Whether sessions must be video recorded.

training_plan_required.description: Whether a training plan or agenda submittal is required.

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

owner_training.x-extraction-notes: Extract training separately from testing and commissioning; it is priced separately. Training records as a closeout deliverable are closeout_deliverables_checklist.

closeout_deliverables_checklist.title: Closeout deliverables, O&M and payment gates
closeout_deliverables_checklist.description: The full list of electrical closeout deliverables with due dates and which of them gate retention or final payment (O&M manuals, record drawings, warranties, attic stock transmittal, test and Cx reports, training records, as-left settings, typed panel directories and labels, arc-flash labels, permit final and inspection sign-offs, software and keys, systems manual input), plus the O&M manual format, copies and draft review. WHY: One missing deliverable can hold retention for months; knowing the full list at bid lets us price closeout labor and plan it. Multi-copy or early-due O&M manuals, common on public work, must be budgeted and started early. WHERE: 01 77 00 Closeout Procedures, 01 78 00 Closeout Submittals, 01 78 23 Operation and Maintenance Data, 26 05 00 closeout requirements, Part 1 'Closeout Submittals' of equipment sections, subcontract closeout exhibit.

due.description: Time before or after the trigger that the deliverable is due.

due_trigger.description: Event the due time counts from.

requirements_text.description: Content or format requirements as written (for O&M: contents beyond cut sheets, as-left settings, parts lists).

cite.description: Citation ids in this field's envelope that support the row.

om_draft_review_required.description: Whether a draft O&M must be submitted for review before final.

closeout_deliverables_checklist.x-extraction-notes: This field owns due dates and payment gating for every closeout deliverable; record_drawings, owner_training, attic_stock_spare_parts and extended_warranties hold the detail. Watch for O&M due before substantial completion; it moves the labor earlier. Power system and arc-flash studies are power_distribution; list them here only as a deliverable. Retainage percent and release terms are contract_terms.

document_control.title: Document control and set quality
document_control.description: What was issued, what is missing and how reliable the set is: extraction coverage, sheet and spec indexes, issue stage, addenda with item-level changes and who distributed them, order of precedence, conflicts, completeness checks, the single missing-reference request list, existing-conditions reliability, cost-bearing notes and pre-bid RFIs. Lets us price the current revision and see where the set is weak.

extraction_coverage_and_quality.title: Extraction coverage and quality
extraction_coverage_and_quality.description: Which files the record was built from (file, BDR category, doc role, pages, pages read by text layer or by OCR or vision, unreadable pages, truncation, duplicates), expected document types that are missing (no spec book, no E-sheets, an addendum referenced but not received), and which critical fields ended not_found, conflicting, with an unverified quote or unreviewed; with the run time, trigger and package version. WHY: A record built without the spec book, or from an unreadable scanned sheet, looks as confident as a complete one; the team needs to see coverage before trusting any risk flag, and an uncited critical fact should never drive a price. WHERE: Generated by the extraction pipeline from the files it processed and each field's envelope; not read from the documents.

text_pages.description: Pages with a usable text layer

ocr_or_vision_pages.description: Pages read by OCR or vision

unreadable_pages.description: Pages that could not be read

truncated.description: Read was cut short by a page or character cap

duplicate_of_file_id.description: File id this one duplicates by hash; null if unique

detail.description: What is missing, e.g. Addendum 3 referenced by Addendum 4

missing_document_types.description: Expected document types not in the package

critical_not_found.description: Critical field keys with status not_found

critical_conflicting.description: Critical field keys with status conflicting

critical_unverified_quote.description: Critical field keys whose quote failed verification

critical_unreviewed.description: Critical field keys not yet reviewed

value.description: Pipeline-generated coverage and quality summary for the latest run

extraction_coverage_and_quality.x-extraction-notes: Code writes this field; the model writes nothing here. Pages without a text layer go to OCR or vision. A truncated read (BDR's self-hosted pypdf path caps at 50 pages and 200,000 characters) is recorded here and turns every field routed to that document into not_found, never not_stated. Duplicate files are detected by hash and extracted once. The run history keeps one entry per run so the original set and each addendum stay comparable. Status, citations and review state are defined by the envelope, not by this field.
extraction_coverage_and_quality.x-bdr-overlap: BDR file categories supply bdr_file_category and project_files.id supplies file_id.

sheet_index.title: Sheet index and drawing log
sheet_index.description: Every sheet actually in the issued PDFs (number, title, discipline, revision, revision date, issued in the base set or by which addendum), reconciled against the cover-sheet index (listed but not provided, provided but not listed, superseded), with the PDF page size, the full sheet size the title block states and whether the sheet can be measured (scale bar, stated scale only, NTS). WHY: Shows what was truly issued, catches a sheet an addendum reissued while the index stayed stale, and keeps pricing off superseded revisions; a listed-but-missing E-sheet is an RFI before bid day, not a surprise after award. Scaled trench and feeder lengths are wrong on half-size or NTS sets, so the record must say whether a PDF can be measured at all. WHERE: Cover sheet or G-000 sheet index, each sheet's title block, revision table and scale notes, addenda sheet lists, the actual PDF page set.

sheet_number.description: Sheet number from the title block

issued_via.description: base, or the addendum number that issued this revision

superseded_by.description: Addendum or revision that replaced it

pdf_page_size_in.description: Set by code from the PDF, e.g. 30x42; model returns null

full_size_stated_in.description: Full sheet size the title block or scale note states

scale_reliability.description: Whether the sheet can be measured

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per sheet in the issued PDFs or listed in the index

sheet_index.x-extraction-notes: Code builds rows from text-layer title blocks and uses vision only for image-only sheets; the model reconciles against the index. Indexes are often not reissued when addenda replace sheets, so diff actual title blocks against the index. Keep superseded revisions with superseded true so the current one is unambiguous. Include all disciplines: architectural reflected ceiling plans and mechanical schedules drive electrical cost. Code sets pdf_page_size_in and flags a reduced set when it is smaller than full_size_stated_in; scaled quantities (quantities_rollup.site_underground_lengths) are unreliable on those sheets and on NTS sheets. Listed-but-missing sheets roll into referenced_documents_not_provided.
sheet_index.x-bdr-overlap: BDR file categories hold drawings by discipline and the bid file splitter splits drawing sets by trade, but no sheet-level index is stored.

spec_section_index.title: Spec section index
spec_section_index.description: Every section actually present in the project manual (division, number, title, which of Parts 1, 2 and 3 exist, and any addendum that added, revised, replaced or deleted it), reconciled against the table of contents. WHY: It is the routing backbone for per-section extraction, and a missing section (no 26 05 19 conductors, no 26 05 73 studies section) means the requirement lives in a drawing note or nowhere, which changes price; a drawings-only bid with no Division 26 book is itself a qualification to state. WHERE: Project manual section headers and footers, table of contents, addenda.

in_toc.description: Listed in the table of contents

addendum_change.description: Latest addendum action on this section

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per spec section present or listed

spec_section_index.x-extraction-notes: Code builds rows from real section headers and footers, not only the TOC; addenda add and delete sections without reissuing it. Include Divisions 00 and 01 because contract, testing and closeout requirements live there. When no project manual is in the package, the status is referenced_not_provided if the drawings refer to one and not_applicable (drawings-only set, with the reason) if nothing does; either way extraction_coverage_and_quality lists it. Sections listed in the TOC but absent roll into referenced_documents_not_provided.
spec_section_index.x-bdr-overlap: BDR file category 'specifications' holds the book; no section index is stored.

issue_status.title: Issue status and design stage
issue_status.description: The issue designation of the set per discipline (issued for bid, permit, construction, conformed, a CD percentage, design development, schematic or pricing set) with the stated percent complete and the issue date. WHY: A sub-100% or pricing set will change before construction, so contingency, qualification language and the 'based on documents dated' line in our proposal must reflect it; pricing a 50% CD set as if final is a common margin loss. WHERE: Cover sheet title block, each sheet's issue line, spec book cover.

percent_complete.description: Stated percent complete, e.g. 90 for a 90% CD set

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per discipline or document set

issue_status.x-extraction-notes: Disciplines in one set can be at different stages (civil at permit, electrical at 90% CD); one row per discipline. The label exactly as printed is the row's citation quote, so there is no raw_label property. percent_complete only when a number is printed. The permit status of the set is ahj.permit_status.

addenda_log.title: Addenda log with electrical changes
addenda_log.description: Every addendum and bulletin (number, issue date, when G3 first received it and from which GCs or portals) with a per-item diff tied to the sheet or spec Part and Article it touched: added, removed, revised, replaced in entirety, clarification or RFI answer; the electrical impact; and the record fields each item changes. WHY: Addenda arrive in the last days before bid and one missed item (a clouded feeder upsize, a copper-only flip, a closed substitution list) can erase the margin; an addendum sentence making 'the electrical subbidder responsible' for work has held a subcontractor liable in court. Acknowledgment is per GC, so the team must see that every inviting GC distributed, and will acknowledge, the same highest addendum; a GC working from an older set prices different scope. WHERE: Addendum narratives and attachments, reissued sheets (clouds, deltas, revision tables), reissued spec sections, RFI answer attachments, and the GC emails and portals that delivered each addendum.

issue_date.description: Issue date printed on the addendum

received_at.description: Earliest receipt by G3; set by code
When it arrived from this source

distributed_by.description: Set by code: each GC or portal that delivered it

ref_sheet_or_section.description: Sheet or spec section and article touched

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per addendum or bulletin, oldest first

addenda_log.x-extraction-notes: Extract one addendum at a time, oldest first, item by item. Diff reissued sheets and sections against the prior version: 'replace sheet E-201 in its entirety' hides what changed inside it and earlier clouds are removed. Scan every sentence for 'responsible for', 'shall include' or 'shall provide' near a trade name; mark it responsibility_change, keep the verbatim sentence as the item's citation, and name the A6 scope_responsibility row it creates in feeds_field_keys. RFI-answer-only addenda are still logged because they must be acknowledged (the method is A1 addenda_acknowledgment). Code fills received_at and distributed_by from BDR's email and portal ingestion and flags an inviting GC that has not distributed the highest addendum. Re-run affected fields on every new addendum. This is the single master log; A5 keeps only its topical low-voltage view.
addenda_log.x-bdr-overlap: BDR stores addenda as a file category and as first-class addenda in the Plans & Specs log at file level, and RFP email ingestion knows which GC delivered each file; this field adds item-level content.

order_of_precedence.title: Order of precedence
order_of_precedence.description: Each order-of-precedence rule the documents state (prime contract, subcontract or bid instructions): whether documents are ranked or complementary, the stated order, whether specs or drawings govern, whether a greater-quantity-or-quality clause exists and whether large-scale drawings govern small-scale. WHY: Tells the estimator which side of a conflict to price; bidding the cheaper reading while the contract enforces the stricter one turns every conflict into unrecovered cost after award. WHERE: Agreement, General and Supplementary Conditions, Instructions to Bidders, Division 01, GC subcontract or scope exhibit when provided.

governing_order.description: Documents in stated order, highest first

most_stringent_governs.description: Greater quantity or quality governs clause

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per contract level that states a precedence rule

order_of_precedence.x-extraction-notes: Extract this before resolving any conflict. With no clause (envelope status not_stated) every conflict's working value is the costlier reading until an RFI or addendum answers it. Never assume specs beat drawings or the reverse. When the subcontract and the prime contract rank differently keep both rows; the subcontract governs G3, but the prime's rule is what the owner enforces on the GC.
order_of_precedence.x-reference-facts: Per the extraction design: AIA A201 ranks nothing (documents are complementary; what one requires, all require), while ConsensusDocs 200 and FAR 52.236-21 do rank (FAR: specifications govern over drawings).

document_conflicts.title: Document conflicts register
document_conflicts.description: Every place two current documents describe the same item differently (drawing vs spec, schedule vs plan count, drawing vs drawing, spec vs spec across divisions, an addendum vs base text it did not expressly replace, invitation vs documents, code edition), with both positions and their citations, which side governs under the order of precedence, which side costs more, the recommended pricing action and where it stands. WHY: Each conflict is a pricing decision: price the costlier reading, RFI it, or qualify it. Unflagged conflicts get resolved after award in the direction that costs us money, and GC leveling treats unexplained gaps as missing scope. WHERE: Cross-reference of drawing schedules (panel, fixture, feeder, equipment connection) and notes against Division 26/27/28 Part 2 and 3 text, Division 01, addenda and the GC invitation scope description, plus every field whose envelope status is conflicting.

topic.description: Item in conflict, e.g. feeder conductor material

applies_to.description: Area, building, feeder or tag affected

source_field_key.description: Record field whose envelope holds this conflict; null for cross-reference finds

value.description: One row per open or resolved conflict

document_conflicts.x-extraction-notes: Code writes a row for every field whose envelope status is conflicting (source_field_key set, positions copied from the envelope). The cross-reference pass adds only conflicts no field owns (panel AIC vs one-line fault current, generator size between one-line and spec, fixture types in the schedule but not in 26 51 00). Who-furnishes and who-installs contradictions are A6 matrix rows flagged conflicting, not rows here. Supersession by an addendum is not a conflict. Never auto-resolve: both positions stay visible. An empty list after complete coverage means none were found; with partial coverage the status is not_found.

design_completeness.title: Design completeness checks
design_completeness.description: A fixed checklist of whether the set contains what is needed to price electrical work with confidence (one-line, riser, load calculation, available fault current, a schedule for every panel shown, feeder schedule, fixture schedule reconciled to plans, lighting control sequence, grounding details, site electrical plan, equipment connection schedule, fire alarm design or performance spec, low-voltage design, utility service design, every keyed note and symbol defined, master-spec leftovers removed, and every code-sheet item with an owning spec section), each with a result and detail, plus an overall rating. WHY: Several missing or inconsistent items signal a rushed design that needs more contingency and an RFI round before bid, and tell the team whether a competitor's low number is likely a scope miss. Undefined symbols under-count code-required devices; leftover master-spec text (bracketed options, another city's name) marks an incompletely edited set; ERRCS or fire alarm required only on the code sheet with no owning section is scope nobody priced. WHERE: Derived across the whole set from sheet_index, spec_section_index, schedules, legends, general and keyed notes and the code sheet.

overall_rating.description: Set by code from the checks under the team's rule

detail.description: What is missing or inconsistent, e.g. undefined symbols

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

checks.description: One row per fixed check item

value.description: Fixed completeness checklist and overall rating

design_completeness.x-extraction-notes: Answer every check_item on every project so ratings compare. overall_rating is set by code from the results under a rule the team fixes (see open questions), not by the model. The absorbed legend check records only undefined, unused or inconsistently used symbols and nonstandard suffix meanings in detail; the whole legend is not copied. This is QA about the documents; the technical values live in A4 and A5. A missing load calculation or fault-current value is a finding, not an extraction failure.

referenced_documents_not_provided.title: Referenced documents not provided
referenced_documents_not_provided.description: The single request list: documents, details and standards the set refers to but did not include (detail callouts to missing sheets, sheets listed in the index but not issued, spec sections listed but absent, NV Energy standards cited by number, owner design standards, geotechnical or hazmat reports, other-trade drawings, the agreement or subcontract), each with the next step and the field that needs it. WHY: A referenced owner standard or utility detail is binding scope we cannot price without seeing it; each missing reference is a request, an RFI or a stated qualification, and owner standards often impose stricter products and methods than the specs. WHERE: Detail bubbles and sheet references on plans, Division 01 and 26 05 00 references articles, general and utility notes, the sheet_index and spec_section_index reconciliation, and every field envelope with status referenced_not_provided.

reference.description: The reference as written, e.g. NV Energy RE-4 or Detail 5/E-502

source_field_key.description: Record field that needs it; null when none owns it

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per referenced item missing from the package

referenced_documents_not_provided.x-extraction-notes: Code adds rows for listed-but-missing sheets and sections and for every field whose status is referenced_not_provided (source_field_key set); the cross-reference pass adds references no field owns. List only what is not provided. An NV Energy standard cited by number is noted here and its scope is left to A4 nv_energy_service_requirements and A6 utility_point_of_demarcation.

existing_conditions_basis.title: Existing conditions reliability
existing_conditions_basis.description: On renovation, TI and addition work: whether existing-condition drawings, as-builts or a survey are provided, whether the documents disclaim their accuracy, and whether bidders must field-verify existing conditions before bid. WHY: A 'field verify, as-builts not guaranteed' clause shifts discovery risk to us; in older Las Vegas buildings that is where unpriced demolition, re-feeds and rework hide. WHERE: Division 01 existing conditions article, Instructions to Bidders (examination of site), demolition sheet general notes.

accuracy_disclaimed.description: Documents disclaim accuracy of existing information

field_verify_before_bid.description: Bidders must verify existing conditions before bid

existing_conditions_basis.x-extraction-notes: On new construction the status is not_applicable with project_profile.work_type as the reason. Hazardous materials and whether a survey exists belong to A3 schedule_and_site.hazardous_materials_existing; existing equipment to remain or be reused is A4 demolition_and_existing_equipment; relief for concealed conditions is A2 differing_site_conditions_relief. This field only records whether existing-condition information can be relied on.

scope_bearing_notes.title: Scope-bearing general and keyed notes
scope_bearing_notes.description: General, keyed, detail and schedule notes that add cost not visible as a device or circuit ('provide new 200A panel here', 'patch and paint', 'verify in field', 'provide temporary power', 'coordinate with'), with sheet, note number, a one-line summary, what the note costs, and whether it departs from the designer's boilerplate. WHY: Blanket obligations in notes are where electrical estimates most often lose money, because a device count never shows them; keyed notes often carry the real trigger for new equipment or demolition that a symbol takeoff misses. WHERE: E-001 and E-002 general notes, per-sheet general notes blocks, keyed note legends on each plan sheet, schedule notes.

note_number.description: Note number; keyed notes are keyed by sheet plus number

summary.description: What the note requires, in one line

non_boilerplate.description: Differs from the designer's standard boilerplate

feeds_field_keys.description: Record fields this note also feeds, e.g. the A6 matrix row

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per cost-bearing general or keyed note

scope_bearing_notes.x-extraction-notes: Key keyed notes by (sheet, note_number); the same number means different things on different sheets. Surface non-boilerplate notes first and skip copy-paste boilerplate; boilerplate naming another city or systems not on the job is a design_completeness finding. Who furnishes or installs is not recorded here: when a note assigns work between trades, the A6 row (furnish_install_language_map or responsibility_matrix) owns it and feeds_field_keys names it. This field records what the note costs.

prebid_rfi_log.title: Pre-bid RFI log
prebid_rfi_log.description: Pre-bid questions and answers that touch electrical scope or pricing (ours, and other bidders' when published): question, answer, how and when it was answered, state at bid time, whether it changes price, and the sheet or section it clarifies. WHY: An unanswered scope question means we are bidding that item blind and must price the worst case or qualify it; answered questions bind every bidder and are easy to overlook when they arrive as a list inside an addendum. WHERE: Addenda RFI-response attachments, GC bid-portal Q&A, GC emails, prebid meeting minutes, our own RFI submissions.

question.description: Question in one or two lines

answer.description: Answer in one or two lines; null when unanswered

ref_sheet_or_section.description: Sheet or spec section the question concerns

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per pre-bid question touching electrical

prebid_rfi_log.x-extraction-notes: Many GCs do not publish a shared log; fill only what is available. Answers that arrive inside an addendum are also addenda_log items. The RFI submission cutoff belongs to A1 bid_submission.rfi_cutoff_and_contact_rules. New questions we should ask go to bid_brief.rfis_to_send.

quantities_rollup.title: Quantity roll-up
quantities_rollup.description: Building size and stated unit counts from the documents, plus a small set of electrical totals computed by code from A4 and A5, each carrying its count basis so $/SF, $/unit and density comparisons use only trustworthy inputs. First-pass AI counts are labeled and never feed ratios or prices.

building_size.title: Building size
building_size.description: Gross building area, the area of electrical scope when smaller (TI or partial floor), stories above grade, levels below grade, number of buildings with per-building rows when stated, site area in acres for site-heavy work, and where the area came from. WHY: The denominator for $/SF, fixtures per SF and labor per SF; using gross SF on a partial-floor TI makes the job look far cheaper than it is and corrupts the benchmark. WHERE: Architectural code analysis area table, cover sheet project data, civil site data table, Division 01 summary, GC invitation.

gross_sf.description: Gross building area in SF as stated

electrical_scope_sf.description: Area of electrical scope when smaller (TI, partial floor)

site_area_acres.description: Site or disturbed area in acres as stated

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

building_size.x-extraction-notes: Prefer the code analysis area table. For TI, electrical_scope_sf is the TI area as stated. Never scale an area from plans (a measured area is a guessed number): when none is printed, leave it null for the estimator to enter, with sf_basis estimator_entered and envelope status entered. site_area_acres gives site and infrastructure jobs a usable denominator.

unit_counts.title: Keys, units and other count drivers
unit_counts.description: Counts the documents state for repeated units that drive electrical cost and comparison: hotel keys, dwelling units, senior or assisted units, patient beds, classrooms, parking stalls, seats, slot positions and table games, each as a total and, when a unit mix or room matrix gives them, per typical type, by building or phase. WHY: Resort, multifamily and senior-living electrical is estimated as a typical room times a count, and GCs and owners compare on $/key or $/unit. Square footage alone cannot tell a 1,200-key tower from a 1,200-key renovation. Unit counts enable $/key comparables and a check that fixture and device counts scale with units. WHERE: Code analysis sheet, architectural unit mix or room matrix, enlarged typical unit plans, ITB project description, parking tabulation on the site plan, gaming floor or slot layout plans.

row_kind.description: Total for the unit type, or one typical type

typical_type_label.description: Typical type as labeled, e.g. King A; null on total rows

applies_to.description: Building, tower or phase; null for the whole project

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per stated unit count

unit_counts.x-extraction-notes: Counts only as printed in a table or narrative; never count rooms, stalls or slot bases from plan symbols. Total rows and their typical_type rows must agree; code flags a mismatch. Slot positions and table games are separate rows because slot bases carry power and data at every base. EV spaces are A4 ev_charging.

service_size.title: Service size and voltage
service_size.description: A roll-up of the utility services from A4: number of services, total and largest main amps, voltage system of the largest service, any customer-owned medium-voltage service, whether the service work is new, an upgrade or existing to remain, total service kVA and the printed demand kVA. WHY: Service size and voltage are the quickest comparable for gear cost and project scale; a 4000A 480V service and a 400A 208V service set very different gear, feeder and utility scope. WHERE: Computed from A4 power_distribution.service_entrance and power_distribution.load_calculation.

largest_service_voltage.description: Voltage system of the largest service

total_service_kva.description: Computed from each service's amps and voltage

demand_kva.description: Demand kVA from the printed load calculation

service_size.x-extraction-notes: Code computes it; no model call. total_service_kva uses each service's own voltage and phase (amps x volts x 1.732 / 1000 for three-phase, amps x volts / 1000 for single-phase). demand_kva is copied only from a printed load calculation. The service detail shown on the project page is A4 service_entrance; this is the comparison roll-up.

distribution_equipment_counts.title: Distribution and backup power equipment counts
distribution_equipment_counts.description: Counts of switchgear and switchboard assemblies, MCCs, panelboards and dry-type transformers, plus generator count and total kW, transfer switch count and UPS or central inverter kVA, rolled up from A4 inventories. WHY: Panel and gear counts drive gear pricing and labor and give a scale comparison that holds across building types; generator kW is a large-ticket comparable that separates life-safety-heavy projects (resort, healthcare) from projects with none. WHERE: Computed from A4 switchgear_lineup, panelboard_schedule, transformers, generators, transfer_switches and ups_and_central_inverters.

ups_or_inverter_kva_total.description: Sum of UPS and central inverter kVA

value.description: Gear and backup power counts computed from A4

distribution_equipment_counts.x-extraction-notes: Code counts unique tags from the latest addendum's schedules; zero is a valid answer when the documents show none (for example no generator). Panels shown on plans with no schedule are a design_completeness finding. Absorbs the former generator_and_backup_power roll-up.
distribution_equipment_counts.x-bdr-overlap: BDR Switchgear and Generator & Equipment vendor RFQ categories and the gear pricing section supply matching cost figures.

lighting_fixture_totals.title: Lighting fixture totals
lighting_fixture_totals.description: Total interior fixtures, exterior building-mounted fixtures, site poles and fixture types, rolled up from the A4 fixture schedule and exterior site lighting, with the count basis and whether any type's schedule quantity and plan count disagree. WHY: Fixture count is the main lighting cost driver and the most common comparison between similar projects; a schedule-vs-plan mismatch is a pricing risk to resolve before bid. WHERE: Computed from A4 wiring_and_lighting.lighting_fixture_schedule and wiring_and_lighting.exterior_site_lighting.

schedule_vs_plan_mismatch.description: Any type where schedule quantity and plan count disagree

lighting_fixture_totals.x-extraction-notes: Code computes it. count_basis ai_plan_count_first_pass marks totals built from first-pass plan counts where the schedule carries no quantities; they are for comparison only, never a bid quantity, and density_ratios will not use them.
lighting_fixture_totals.x-bdr-overlap: BDR Lighting vendor RFQ category; its quotes give the package price for cost per fixture.

site_underground_lengths.title: Site trench and saw-cut lengths
site_underground_lengths.description: Total site trench length, trench length under paving, concrete-encased duct bank length and saw-cut length when printed, with how the lengths were obtained (printed or tabulated, dimensioned, scaled first pass), rolled up from A4. WHY: Trench and saw-cut footage drive G3's trenching and saw-cut markups and the underground pricing section; comparing LF across similar sites catches a missed run. WHERE: Computed from A4 power_distribution.site_electrical and wiring_and_lighting.duct_bank_encasement.

paved_trench_lf.description: Trench LF under asphalt or concrete

value.description: Site trench and saw-cut lengths computed from A4

site_underground_lengths.x-extraction-notes: Code copies totals and each segment's length_source from A4. sawcut_lf only when printed; never derive it from trench length. Scaled lengths are first-pass measurements: they are unreliable where sheet_index shows NTS or a reduced set, and are never priced without the estimator's takeoff.
site_underground_lengths.x-bdr-overlap: BDR saw-cut and trench markup RFQ categories and the underground pricing section.

density_ratios.title: Density ratios
density_ratios.description: Computed ratios (fixtures per 1,000 SF, service VA per SF, panels per 10,000 SF, data drops per 1,000 SF, fixtures per unit), each with the quality of its inputs, withheld when any input is a first-pass count or missing. WHY: Ratios compare projects of different sizes, and a ratio far outside our history for the building type points to a takeoff miss or an unusual design; but only trustworthy inputs count, because ratios built on first-pass AI counts look authoritative and pollute comparisons. WHERE: Computed from building_size, unit_counts, service_size, distribution_equipment_counts, lighting_fixture_totals and A5 low_voltage_life_safety.device_counts.

unit_type.description: Unit type for fixtures_per_unit; null otherwise

density_ratios.x-extraction-notes: Code computes a ratio only when every input has a schedule, printed or estimator-confirmed basis, and sets inputs_basis accordingly; otherwise value is null with withheld_first_pass_input or withheld_missing_input. Use electrical_scope_sf for TI. Data drops come straight from A5 device_counts (the former low_voltage_device_totals copy is removed). Service VA uses service_size.total_service_kva.

bid_price_per_sf.title: Our bid price per SF and per unit
bid_price_per_sf.description: Our proposal amounts per GC (lowest, highest and to the awarded GC once known) divided by the area used, each BDR pricing section per SF, and the lowest amount per key or unit when unit_counts are stated. WHY: The fastest sanity check on a finished number: well below our own history for the same building and work type usually means missing scope, well above means we are likely to lose; resort and multifamily owners and GCs compare on $/key or $/unit. WHERE: Computed by the app from BDR per-GC proposal amounts and pricing sections, building_size and unit_counts.

awarded_gc_per_sf.description: Amount to the awarded GC per SF

value.description: Our price per SF and per unit, computed by the app

bid_price_per_sf.x-extraction-notes: Computed by the app after pricing, not by the LLM; recompute when proposal amounts change. Use electrical_scope_sf when stated, otherwise gross_sf, and record which. Actual cost per SF after the job lives in history_and_outcome.estimate_vs_actual.
bid_price_per_sf.x-bdr-overlap: Uses BDR per-GC proposal amounts and pricing sections (materials, gear, underground, low_voltage).

history_and_outcome.title: History and outcome
history_and_outcome.description: Results and lessons the team enters after bid day and after the job (bidders and spread, award reason, post-bid buyout revisions, estimate vs actual, change orders traced to documents, gear lead times) so future bids learn from past ones and the catalog can be re-prioritized.

bid_result_market_data.title: Bid results and spread
bid_result_market_data.description: After bid day: number of electrical bidders, our rank, the winning electrical contractor and amount, our amount to the awarded GC, the spread in dollars and percent, where the numbers came from and how firm they are. WHY: Spread against the actual winner, tracked by GC, building type and estimator, is the clearest signal of whether we price high (losing winnable work) or low (winning jobs that lose money); field size shows whether a very low competitor probably missed scope. WHERE: Public bid tabulations, the awarded prime's subcontractor listing on public work, GC feedback after award, team notes.

our_amount_to_awarded_gc.description: Set by the app from BDR proposal amounts

spread_amount.description: Set by the app: our amount minus the winner, signed

spread_pct.description: Set by the app: signed percent

value.description: Bid results and spread entered after bid day

bid_result_market_data.x-extraction-notes: Entered by the team after results are known; the app fills our amount and the spread from BDR proposal amounts. Store a rumored number with reliability informal, never as fact. On Nevada public work the awarded prime's NRS 338.141 listing can name the winning electrical sub but does not give its price.
bid_result_market_data.x-reference-facts: NRS 338.141(2) requires the prime's bid to name each listed first-tier sub and describe its work; license numbers appear on the list the three lowest bidders submit within 2 hours after bid opening under path (b). The statute as fact-checked does not require sub amounts.
bid_result_market_data.x-bdr-overlap: BDR per-GC proposal amounts supply our amount; competitor_known in the go/no-go rubric.

award_and_debrief.title: Award, buyout and debrief
award_and_debrief.description: Which GC won the prime, whether that GC carried G3, the main reason we won or lost, every price revision between bid day and subcontract (value engineering, scope clarification, buyout reduction, BAFO) with its amount and GC, the subcontract value at signing, GC feedback, any scope surprise found after submission, and one process change with an owner. WHY: Losing because our GC lost the prime is different from losing on our price. Buyout pressure and VE rounds between bid day and subcontract differ sharply by GC; without them the bid-day spread overstates margin and GCs cannot be compared on post-bid behavior. Debriefs only improve the next bid when they are recorded and assigned. WHERE: Team debrief after results, GC feedback call, buyout correspondence and the signed subcontract.

g3_carried_by_awarded_gc.description: Whether the awarded GC carried G3

gc_name.description: GC that asked for it

post_bid_revisions.description: Price changes between bid day and subcontract

scope_surprise.description: Scope found after submission that we missed or others missed

award_and_debrief.x-extraction-notes: Not extracted from documents; editable later without re-running extraction. amount_change is signed (a buyout reduction is negative). subcontract_value_at_signing differs from estimate_vs_actual.final_contract_value_at_closeout, which includes change orders.
award_and_debrief.x-bdr-overlap: BDR bid outcome won/lost and is_rebid; this field adds the reason, the awarded GC and buyout history.

estimate_vs_actual.title: Estimate vs actual
estimate_vs_actual.description: For awarded jobs at closeout: estimated vs actual cost by BDR pricing section (materials, gear, underground, low voltage) and labor with signed variance percent, estimated vs actual labor hours, final contract value including change orders, and actual cost per SF. WHY: Measured variance by section and building type (for example labor running low on healthcare TI) turns history into a correction factor for the next bid instead of gut feel. WHERE: BDR pricing sections at bid; job-cost accounting at closeout.

final_contract_value_at_closeout.description: Final contract value including change orders

estimate_vs_actual.x-extraction-notes: Job-cost categories must map to BDR pricing sections; agree the mapping once. variance_pct is signed, so it does not use the 0-100 percent type. Labor hours per SF, per fixture and per labor condition are computed from this field, quantities_rollup and labor_condition_profile. Worthless if actuals are never entered; the PM module is the natural place to enter them.
estimate_vs_actual.x-bdr-overlap: BDR pricing sections (materials, gear, underground, low_voltage) and the PM module (SOV billing).

change_orders_traced_to_documents.title: Change orders traced to bid documents
change_orders_traced_to_documents.description: For each change order or scope gap during construction: description, amount, cause, the bid document and record field it traces to, whether this record flagged it before bid, and how much of the cost was recovered. WHY: This is the feedback loop for the record itself: it shows which field types (conductor material, OFCI, low-voltage boundary, commissioning) cause real losses and whether extraction caught them, so fields can be added or re-prioritized. WHERE: Internal change order log, tagged back to the bid document or addendum when known.

traced_to_document_ref.description: Sheet, section or addendum it traces to

flagged_before_bid.description: Whether the record flagged it before bid

cite.description: Citation ids for this row

value.description: One row per change order or scope gap

change_orders_traced_to_documents.x-extraction-notes: Entered after award, most naturally in the PM module; cite points at the bid document page when the person gives one. flagged_before_bid is checked against the record's history (was the field found, not_stated or conflicting at bid). Review periodically to re-prioritize this catalog.
change_orders_traced_to_documents.x-bdr-overlap: BDR PM module (RFI log, SOV billing).

gear_lead_time_quoted_vs_actual.title: Gear lead time, quoted vs actual
gear_lead_time_quoted_vs_actual.description: For switchgear, generators, large transformers and other major equipment: equipment class, manufacturer, lead time quoted at bid (weeks, firm or budgetary), quote date, PO date, delivery date and actual weeks. WHY: Lead times move quarter to quarter; our own quoted-vs-actual record by manufacturer and gear class is the best basis for accepting or qualifying a schedule with liquidated damages on the next bid. WHERE: BDR vendor quotes (Switchgear, Generator & Equipment) at bid; procurement and PM records after award.

quoted_weeks.description: Lead time quoted at bid, weeks

actual_weeks.description: Set by code from PO and delivery dates

value.description: One row per major equipment item

gear_lead_time_quoted_vs_actual.x-extraction-notes: Quoted weeks and firmness can be copied from vendor quotes at bid; code computes actual_weeks from PO and delivery dates. Which equipment is long-lead on this project is A4 power_distribution.long_lead_equipment; early-release terms are A2 contract_terms.long_lead_early_release.
gear_lead_time_quoted_vs_actual.x-bdr-overlap: BDR Switchgear and Generator & Equipment RFQ categories and quote records; PM module.

datetime.description: ISO 8601 date-time with an explicit offset.

duration.description: An amount with its unit; days keep calendar vs working as written.

cite_ids.description: Ids of citations in this field envelope that support the row.

status.description: found: stated, with a verified quote. inferred: follows from cited text by a named rule (never for numbers, dates or money). computed: derived by code from other fields. not_stated: every routed location was read and none addresses it (a risk finding). referenced_not_provided: the governing document is referenced but missing from the package. conflicting: current sources disagree. not_applicable: the subject does not exist on this project. not_found: the extractor could not establish an answer (routed to a person). entered: typed by a team member. pending: not yet extracted for this package version.

document.description: File name, or the invitation sender and date.

page.description: 1-based physical PDF page, used only to open the viewer.

location.description: Schedule, table row, keyed note or detail, e.g. 'Panel schedule LP-1A'.

addendum.description: Addendum number when the source is an addendum or a page it reissued.

quote.description: Verbatim text, about 300 characters at most, never paraphrased.

quote_verified.description: True only when code found the quote in the stored page text.

envelope.description: Evidence wrapper used by every field. The field schema constrains only value.

value.description: Typed per field; null when status is not_stated, referenced_not_provided, not_applicable, not_found or pending.

computed_from.description: Field refs used by a computed field.

searched.description: Every location read for this field; required when status is not_stated or referenced_not_provided.

confidence.description: Set by pipeline rules (quote verified, literal vs interpreted, second read agrees), not by model self-report alone.
